title: They/Them
tagline: Fear doesn't discriminate.
overview: Campers at an LGBTQ+ conversion camp endure unsettling psychological techniques while the campsite is stalked by a mysterious killer.
plot:
They/Them is a 2022 American satirical horror film written and directed by John Logan, produced by Jason Blum's Blumhouse Productions. The movie takes place at Camp Redwood, a summer camp for teenagers that has been converted into a conversion therapy program.

The story follows Jamie (played by Cooper Hoffman), a teenager who is struggling to come to terms with their identity as non-binary and gay. They are sent to Camp Redwood, where they meet the other campers, including Alex (played by Tyler James Williams), a charismatic and confident camper who becomes Jamie's friend and confidant.

As the summer progresses, Jamie begins to realize that something is not quite right at the camp. The counselors seem overly aggressive and controlling, and the campers are subjected to a series of humiliating and dehumanizing activities designed to "cure" them of their non-heterosexual identities.

Jamie soon discovers that the camp's director, Dr. Lerner (played by Deborah Ann Woll), has a sinister agenda for her campers. She believes that conversion therapy is the key to helping teenagers overcome their identities and conform to societal norms.

As Jamie delves deeper into the camp's secrets, they begin to uncover a dark history of abuse and trauma inflicted upon the campers. The more Jamie learns, the more they realize that Dr. Lerner's true intentions are far more sinister than they initially thought.

The movie builds towards a climactic confrontation between Jamie and Dr. Lerner, as well as the other counselors who have been complicit in her abuse of power. In the end, Jamie and their friends must band together to take down the camp and expose its dark secrets to the world.

Throughout the film, Logan uses satire to critique the conversion therapy industry and the ways in which it has been used to silence and marginalize LGBTQ+ individuals. The movie is a powerful commentary on the importance of acceptance, self-identity, and the need for safe spaces for marginalized communities.

Overall, They/Them is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores themes of identity, trauma, and resistance. With its talented young cast and sharp script, it is a must-see for fans of horror and satire alike.

plot:
Ida Red is a 2021 American crime thriller written, directed and co-produced by John Swab. Melissa Leo stars as Ida "Red" Walker, the matriarch of a criminal family, with Josh Hartnett as her son Wyatt, Frank Grillo as her brother Dallas, Deborah Ann Woll as her daughter Jeanie, and Sofia Hublitz, William Forsythe, George Carroll, Mark Boone Junior and Beau Knapp in supporting roles. Ida Walker has been in prison for years, ever since the bust that also left her a widow. Now she has been diagnosed with terminal cancer and wants to die a free woman, so she sets about engineering both her parole and, true to her nature, one final heist. Outside, the family business is run by her son Wyatt, a successful career criminal with his own code of ethics, and her violent and unpredictable brother Dallas.

The family is complicated by Ida's daughter Jeanie, who is estranged from her mother because she married Bodie Collier, a kind but not especially sharp police officer. Their rebellious teenage daughter Darla is drawn to her uncle Wyatt's world and is involved with a local lowlife named Petey. After a truck robbery goes wrong, Wyatt finds himself under pressure, while FBI Special Agent Lawrence Twilley, working alongside Collier, begins to close in on the family. Dallas appoints himself the cleaner and ruthlessly shoots those responsible for the botched job, or their relatives, raising the stakes as Wyatt tries to pull off the job that will secure his mother's release. Loyalties between blood relatives, lawmen and criminals are tested as the plan unfolds, and Wyatt must decide how far he is willing to go for a mother who has shaped his whole life.

The film is a family crime saga set in Oklahoma, blending heist thriller elements with themes of inheritance, loyalty and violence passed from one generation to the next, and its score was composed by David Sardy.

title: The Little Prince(ss)
overview: When Gabriel, a 7-year-old Chinese kid who loves ballet, becomes friends with Rob, another Chinese kid from school, Rob’s dad gets suspicious about Gabriel's feminine behavior and decides to intervene.
plot:
The Little Prince(ss) is a 2021 American live-action short drama film written and directed by Moxie Peng and produced by Walt Disney Pictures as part of the first season of Launchpad, a Disney+ programme overseen by Disney's diversity and inclusion team that gives filmmakers from under-represented backgrounds the chance to make a short. Six projects on the theme of discovery were chosen from more than 1,100 applications, and each director was mentored by someone from one of the company's studios. The 19-minute film, with music by Robert Ouyang Rusli, stars Kalo Moss and Ching Yin Ryan Hu, with Evan Lai, Brian Yang, Lynn Chen and Danni Wang in supporting roles, and was released on Disney+ on 28 May 2021. Its title nods to Frances Hodgson Burnett's novel A Little Princess.

Gabriel (Moss) is a gentle, kind seven-year-old Chinese-American first-grader who takes ballet lessons, plays with dolls and loves the colour pink. At school he befriends Rob (Hu), a sporty boy who has recently moved to the United States from China and who is mocked by classmates because of the smell of the Chinese food he brings for lunch. After some hesitation Rob comes to enjoy his new friend's company and encourages him rather than trying to change him. Rob's father, however, grows suspicious of Gabriel's feminine interests and decides to intervene, confronting Gabriel's parents over dinner, who respond by accepting their son exactly as he is.

Peng, who identifies as non-binary and grew up in China, based the story on an incident from their own childhood, when a neighbour's father came to the family's dinner table to tell Peng's father that his child was not normal and needed to be fixed, and Peng's father defended them. In an interview with Laughing Place, Peng said the film was meant to encourage viewers to stay open-minded and curious about people who are different rather than rushing to judgement, explained that both boys' most painful moments take place while eating as a way of linking their experiences of being othered, and described a nationwide search before Moss was cast. Alex Reif of Laughing Place called it a charming short about not being afraid to be oneself, likely to resonate deeply with LGBTQ+ viewers, and Franck Armand-Zuniga of Chronique Disney found it particularly moving, praising the two young actors for conveying overwhelming emotion.

One of the standout aspects of Memory is its exploration of themes such as identity, trauma, and the human condition. Ruth's struggles to come to terms with her past serve as a metaphor for the fragility of human memory and the ways in which our experiences shape us.

The film features strong performances from both Baptista and Radcliffe, who bring depth and nuance to their characters. The cinematography is also noteworthy, capturing the eerie atmosphere of Ruth's world with a blend of stark realism and surrealism.

Overall, Memory is a thought-provoking and unsettling thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat. With its complex narrative and exploration of themes, it's sure to leave you pondering long after the credits roll.

His stressful work routine leads to a nervous breakdown, and at the hospital he learns that his hearing is literally hanging by a thread and that the next loud noise could be fatal. On medical advice, he and his wife Joana sell everything, leave Rio de Janeiro and buy a house in a small mountain town, hoping to find peace and quiet surrounded by nature. Their plans for a tranquil life are shattered, however, when they meet their new neighbor, Toninho, a good-natured man who loves throwing parties and is the drum master of a samba school. He holds samba rehearsals at home, and his children practice drums and tuba in the garden. A war breaks out over which will prevail in the neighborhood, noise or silence, as Walter's increasingly desperate attempts to silence the household next door clash with Toninho's carefree lifestyle. Amid music, arguments and very different ways of living, the two neighbors and their families must eventually learn to coexist.

Fenced In premiered on Netflix on 1 September 2022. Critical reception was mixed to negative. CinePOP felt that the comedy rarely got laughs, finding Walter too abrasive for viewers to sympathize with and the conflict essentially one-sided, while praising the colorful sets, costumes and lighting and Manfrini's adorably irritating performance; it also noted a recreation of the famous Porta dos Fundos sketch that made Rabello a viral sensation. Omelete criticized a script made up of incoherent scenes while acknowledging the talent of the cast, A Gazeta considered the film unoriginal but effective thanks to the chemistry between Hassum and Manfrini, and UOL Splash was much more negative, objecting to its humor and its many jokes.

title: Through My Window
tagline: It all started with the Wi-Fi password...
overview: Raquel's longtime crush on her next-door neighbor turns into something more when he starts developing feelings for her, despite his family's objections.
plot:
Through My Window (Spanish: A través de mi ventana) is a 2022 Spanish teen romantic drama directed by Marçal Forés from a screenplay by Eduard Sola, based on Ariana Godoy's novel of the same name. Clara Galle stars as Raquel Mendoza and Julio Peña as Ares Hidalgo, with Pilar Castro and Eric Masip.

Raquel, who writes stories but lacks the courage to share them, narrates how her life changed. Her modest family home sits beside the mansion of the wealthy Hidalgos, owners of Alpha 3, one of the country's most influential companies, headquartered in Barcelona. The three Hidalgo heirs are Artemis, Ares and Apolo. Raquel is obsessed with Ares, though she has never spoken to him. When Apolo thanks her for letting the brothers use her Wi-Fi, she realizes that Ares has hacked her computer for the password. She confronts him in the woods, admits that she likes him and vows to make him fall for her. Their flirtation intensifies when he climbs through her window to reconnect the Wi-Fi she has unplugged, and at a party she seduces him only to walk away. Ares later opens up to her about his grandfather's death, and they sleep together.

Ares then turns cold, pushing her away repeatedly, until he finds Raquel drunk in the street and takes her home. He confesses that she makes him feel things he cannot afford, because his father has already mapped out a future for him with no room for love, and asks for another chance. Things go well until he brings her to a family party to defy his father, where Raquel is humiliated to see her mother working as a waiter. Her mother tells her that her father was a gifted writer who never dared publish his novel and urges her to be honest with Ares. When Raquel goes to his home, his family turns her away as a distraction. Ares defies them and goes to the prom, where Raquel's friend Yoshi, angry at how he has hurt Raquel, fights him and pushes him into a partly drained pool. Raquel stays at his side in the hospital until he recovers, after which his family lets him choose his own path, and he decides to study medicine in Stockholm. At the airport Ares admits that he broke the family's Wi-Fi on purpose so he could talk to her. Four months later Raquel publishes her own book, Through My Window, and Ares climbs through her window again.

Netflix released the film on 4 February 2022. Critics were negative, with a 0% Rotten Tomatoes rating from six reviews, and Cinemanía faulted its toxic clichés. Two sequels followed in 2023 and 2024.

title: Carnaval
overview: After a breakup, an influencer takes her friends on a free trip to Bahia's vibrant Carnival, where she learns life's not just about social media likes.
plot:
Carnaval is a 2021 Brazilian comedy film directed by Leandro Neri, who wrote the screenplay with Audemir Leuzinger and Luisa Mascarenhas. Produced by Camisa Listrada in partnership with Netflix, it stars Giovana Cordeiro, Bruna Inocencio, Gessica Kayane and Samya Pascotto as four friends who spend the Carnival holiday in Salvador, Bahia. Netflix released it simultaneously in 190 countries on 2 June 2021.

Nina (Cordeiro), an aspiring digital influencer, discovers that a video of her famous boyfriend cheating on her has gone viral. To get over the break-up, she uses her contacts to land an all-expenses-paid trip to Salvador during Carnival week, invited by the charming singer Freddy Nunes (Borges), and brings along her three best friends: the crowd-shy Mayra (Inocencio), the nerdy, guarded Vivi (Pascotto) and the loud, flirtatious Michelle (Kayane). On arrival, they find themselves in a poor hotel with fewer privileges than the more famous influencers. Desperate to climb the social media ladder, Nina neglects her friends to chase likes and Freddy's attention. Vivi is courted by a fellow geek, Samir (Medrado), and the popular influencer Luana (Pavanelli) courts cancellation after drunken offensive remarks. Salvador (Pedro), a local tour guide who develops a crush on Nina, shows her the city away from the sponsored Carnival floats and teaches her to enjoy the moment rather than live behind a phone screen. A late twist involves a character trying to pass as straight, whom one of the friends supports when the truth comes out. Each of the women learns something about herself, and Nina realises that social media fame is a poor substitute for real friendship.

Although set in Salvador, much of the film was shot at a resort in Praia do Forte, about 30 kilometres away, while the street celebration scenes were filmed during the 2020 Carnival. The film topped Netflix's Top 10 in Brazil and also charted in Portugal and Spain. Critics were less kind, with only one of six reviews counted by Rotten Tomatoes positive. Monica Castillo of RogerEbert.com likened it to Girls Trip, praising the vivid Carnival spectacle but finding the leads close to stock characters and the comedy over-exaggerated. In Brazil the film was criticised for geographical errors, for having few black actors in its main cast despite being set in the Brazilian city with the largest black population, and for casting a Rio de Janeiro singer as a Bahian star.

title: The In Between
tagline: Love never dies.
overview: After surviving a car accident that took the life of her boyfriend, a teenage girl believes he's attempting to reconnect with her from the after world.
plot:
The In Between is a 2022 American romantic fantasy drama directed by Arie Posin and written by Marc Klein. Joey King stars as Tessa, a teenage photographer, with Kyle Allen as her boyfriend Skylar, Kim Dickens and John Ortiz as her adoptive parents, and Celeste O'Connor. It was released on Paramount+ on 11 February 2022 and later on Netflix in some territories.

After a car accident, two young people lie on the road: the girl barely moving, the boy motionless. Tessa wakes up in hospital and learns that her boyfriend, Skylar, has died. Through flashbacks, the film traces their relationship. A guarded, cynical teenager raised by adoptive parents, Tessa spends her free time taking photographs around her coastal town. One day she wanders into a local cinema to watch a classic French film, and Skylar, a hopeless romantic, offers to translate it for her. Their very different views on love spark an immediate connection. They later meet again at a rowing regatta, spend the day together, and at an abandoned honeymoon hotel called the Empyrean, Skylar teaches her to waltz and they share their first kiss.

In the present, Tessa returns to school, haunted by grief. She is reminded of the approaching deadline to apply to the Rhode Island School of Design, where her teacher thinks she could study photography, but she throws away her darkroom supplies, and her adoptive father reminds her of her tendency to give up on things. Soon she begins experiencing strange signs: objects move, her photographs change, and she becomes convinced that Skylar is trying to communicate with her from beyond. With the help of her best friend, Shannon, Tessa searches for a way to reach him, believing that the dead can contact the living in a state between life and death. As she revisits the places they shared and relives their relationship, including their arguments and the circumstances of the accident, she must come to terms with her loss, her fear of being loved and abandoned, and what Skylar is trying to tell her.

The In Between received mixed reviews, with a 64 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on eleven reviews. Critics praised King's performance and the chemistry between the leads, but many found the story sentimental and predictable.

title: A Cinderella Story: Starstruck
overview: Finley Tremaine, a small-town farm girl, longs to spread her wings and soar as an aspiring performer. When a Hollywood film crew arrives in her sleepy town, she is determined to land a role in the production and capture the attention of handsome lead actor Jackson Stone. Unfortunately, a botched audition forces her to change course. Now, disguised as cowboy “Huck,” Finley finally gets her big break. But can she keep the charade a secret from everyone, including her evil stepmother and devious step-siblings?
plot:
A Cinderella Story: Starstruck is a 2021 American musical teen comedy written and directed by Michelle Johnston, starring Bailee Madison and Michael Evans Behling. A stand-alone sequel to A Cinderella Story: Christmas Wish (2019), it is the sixth and final instalment of the A Cinderella Story series, released digitally on June 29, 2021, and on DVD on July 13. Like the earlier films, it reworks the Cinderella fairy tale in a contemporary setting, here mixed with a gender-disguise comedy.

Finley Tremaine lives on a farm in Dreary, Idaho, built by her late father, with her stepmother Valerian, stepbrother Kale and stepsister Saffron, who make her do all the chores and sleep in the cold barn while she dreams of becoming an actress. When the popular star Jackson Stone comes to town to shoot a musical about Billy the Kid, the family plans to audition, but they send Finley to the butcher with her pet pig Jon Ham and announce they intend to sell the farm. Finley goes to the auditions instead and impresses with her singing, guitar playing and lasso skills, until the runaway pig drags her through the mud. Jackson helps her up and is smitten, but the director Trevor throws her out, and Jackson never learns her name.

Determined to get onto the production, Finley returns disguised as a boy named Huck and is hired, while Saffron is cast for her looks as a saloon girl and Valerian volunteers the farm as a location. Saffron develops a crush on "Huck", Kale tries to ingratiate himself with Jackson, and Finley juggles filming with her chores. Jackson confides in Huck that he would happily give up acting to return to his uncle's ranch. When Huck outshines the actor playing Saffron's love interest, Trevor gives her the part, to her horror, since it requires kissing Saffron.

Jackson finally meets the real Finley and takes her on a date, but Kale uncovers her secret and the stepfamily locks her in the barn. Jon Ham fetches the keys, and Finley returns to the set, removes her disguise and confesses her feelings to Jackson, and they kiss. Trevor offers her a role in a new film, and the estate agent discovers her father's will, which names Finley as the farm's legal owner, allowing her to evict her stepfamily. Jackson retires from acting to look after the farm while Finley pursues her dream.

title: Emergency
tagline: It's not what it looks like.
overview: Ready for a night of legendary partying, three college students must weigh the pros and cons of calling the police when faced with an unexpected situation.
plot:
Emergency is a 2022 American thriller comedy-drama directed by Carey Williams and written by K.D. Dávila, expanded from their 2018 short film of the same name. RJ Cyler, Donald Elise Watkins and Sebastian Chacon star as Sean, Kunle and Carlos, three college students forced to weigh the risks of calling the police, with Sabrina Carpenter as Maddy, Maddie Nichols as her younger sister Emma, Madison Thompson as Alice and Diego Abraham as Rafael.

Best friends Sean and Kunle are determined to become the first Black students to complete the campus "Legendary Tour", a circuit of seven fraternity parties in a single night. Before setting out, they and their roommate Carlos find an underage white girl, Emma, unconscious in their living room. Sean insists that calling 911 would make three young men of color the immediate suspects, so Kunle persuades the others to drive her to a hospital ten minutes away themselves. Meanwhile Emma's older sister Maddy and her friends Alice and Rafael begin searching for her.

The night spirals out of control. An attempt to leave Emma outside a party ends with Kunle chased off and their car damaged, Carlos mistakes a bottle of spiked punch for a sports drink and gives it to her, and Sean fails to borrow a relative's car. Emma wakes up in a stranger's vehicle, panics and lashes out, causing a crash, then runs into the woods before collapsing again. Tracking her phone, Maddy's group finds them and attacks, until Carlos and Rafael discover they are cousins and the situation is explained, though Maddy stays suspicious until she learns that Emma's phone was hidden on her body. A frightened Sean walks off to the final party. As Emma begins to overdose, Kunle performs CPR while Carlos speeds to the hospital, pursued by police who think the girl has been kidnapped. At the emergency entrance an officer points a gun at Kunle, the only Black man in the car, before Alice explains what happened, and a white officer tells Kunle they should simply have called the police. Sean and Kunle reconcile. The next day the sisters arrive with a gift basket, and Kunle shuts the door on Maddy's written apology. Later, Sean notices Kunle flinching at the sound of distant sirens.

The film premiered at the 2022 Sundance Film Festival, where Dávila won the Waldo Salt Screenwriting Award, and was released by Amazon Studios in limited theaters in May 2022 before streaming on Prime Video. Critics praised it, giving it a 92% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Found
tagline: Their search for answers led them to each other.
overview: Follows the story of three American teenage girls—each adopted from China—who discover they are blood-related cousins on 23andMe. Their online meeting inspires the young women to confront the burning questions they have about their lost history.
plot:
Found is a 2021 documentary film directed and produced by Amanda Lipitz. An international co-production between the United States and China, it follows three teenage girls, adopted from China as babies by American families, who discover through the DNA testing service 23andMe that they are biological cousins. The film premiered at the Hamptons International Film Festival on 9 October 2021 and was released by Netflix on 20 October 2021.

The three girls grew up in very different circumstances. Chloe was adopted by a Jewish family living in Seattle and later Phoenix; Sadie was raised by a Christian family with divorced parents in Nashville; and Lily grew up in a large Catholic family in Oklahoma City. After learning that they share DNA, they connect online and form a close bond, sharing their experiences of growing up as Chinese adoptees in the United States and their questions about where they came from.

The cousins eventually meet in person and work with Liu Hao, a genealogist from the organisation My China Roots, who helps adoptees search for their birth families. With her assistance, and with the support of their adoptive families, they travel to China. The documentary follows them as they visit the places where they were abandoned as infants, tour the orphanages where they spent their earliest months, and meet couples who gave up daughters for adoption decades earlier and are hoping to find them. Throughout the journey, the girls and the people they meet grapple with questions of identity, belonging and loss, and with the legacy of China's one-child policy, which led many families to give up baby girls. None of the potential birth parents they meet turns out to be related to them, but in the closing moments one of the families discovers a match with another adoptee.

The documentary approaches its subject with sensitivity, giving voice both to the adoptees and to the birth parents, many of whom have lived for years with grief and guilt over the children they lost. It also shows how genetic testing has opened new possibilities for international adoptees seeking their origins.

Found received critical acclaim and was widely praised for its emotional poignancy. On Rotten Tomatoes all of the critics' reviews counted are positive, and Metacritic assigned it a score of 82 out of 100, indicating universal acclaim.

title: Crimes of the Future
tagline: Surgery is the new sex.
overview: Humans adapt to a synthetic environment, with new transformations and mutations. With his partner Caprice, Saul Tenser, celebrity performance artist, publicly showcases the metamorphosis of his organs in avant-garde performances.
plot:
Crimes of the Future is a 2022 science fiction body horror drama written and directed by David Cronenberg. Viggo Mortensen and Léa Seydoux play the performance artists Saul Tenser and Caprice, with Kristen Stewart as Timlin and Scott Speedman as Lang. It is not a remake of his 1970 film of the same name, and it marked his first science fiction horror film since eXistenZ (1999).

In an unspecified future, biotechnology lets machines interface directly with the human body, and humanity has changed in mysterious ways. Most people no longer feel pain or catch infections, so surgery is done on conscious people. Some bodies are changing even more radically. In the opening scene, an eight-year-old boy, Brecken, eats plastic. His mother, convinced he is not human, smothers him and leaves his body for his father, Lang. Saul Tenser suffers from "accelerated evolution syndrome", which makes his body grow new organs. With his partner Caprice, he turns their surgical removal into celebrated live art. He lives in pain, dependent on biomechanical devices such as a twitching chair that helps him eat. At the National Organ Registry, which catalogs new organs to enforce the state's restrictions on evolution, the nervous bureaucrat Timlin becomes fascinated by his work and tells him that "surgery is the new sex".

Tenser secretly works as an informant for a police unit trying to infiltrate a group of radical evolutionists. Their leader turns out to be Lang. Lang explains that his followers have altered their digestive systems to live on plastic and toxic waste bars that would poison anyone else, and that Brecken was born with this ability. Lang asks Tenser and Caprice to perform a public autopsy on the boy to prove that humans are evolving. When Tenser opens the body, he finds that Brecken's organs have been surgically replaced. Lang leaves in tears and is murdered by two agents linked to the maker of Tenser's machines. Tenser learns that Timlin replaced the organs to keep the truth hidden. He breaks with the police, and in the final scene he eats a plastic bar as Caprice films him, and his chair finally goes still.

Cronenberg wrote the script in 1998 as Painkillers and shot it unchanged in 2021. The film competed for the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2022 and was released in France on May 25 and in North America in early June. Reviews were generally positive, with Rotten Tomatoes calling it quintessential if not classic Cronenberg, but it grossed only $4.5 million.

title: The Quintessential Quintuplets Movie
original_title: 映画 五等分の花嫁
overview: When five lovely young girls who hate studying hire part-time tutor Futaro, he guides not only their education but also their hearts. Time spent has brought them all closer, with feelings growing within the girls and Futaro. As they finish their third year of high school and their last school festival approaches, they set their sights on what’s next. Is there a future with one of them and Futaro?
plot:
Following their summer vacation, Futaro Uesugi and the Nakano quintuplets Ichika, Nino, Miku, Yotsuba, and Itsuki, now third-year high school students, prepare for the upcoming school festival. On the day of the festival, Futaro invites the quintuplets to a room and confesses his love to them, but he tells them to wait until the end of the festival to know whom he has chosen among them. During her acting work on the second day of the festival, Ichika learns that one of her sisters collapsed and rushes to a hospital, where she sees Futaro and Nino visiting. Ichika strolls outside with Futaro, during which she kisses him at a park. On the second day of the festival, Nino is expecting the quintuplets' father Maruo to visit the school but is unable to find him among the crowd. Futaro approaches her with a video confirming Mauro's attendance. Nino and Futaro visit Mauro in the hospital, where she cooks a pancake for him. After the successful meeting, Nino kisses Futaro and thanks her father for choosing him as the quintuplets' tutor.
On the first day of the festival, Miku is accompanied by Futaro in approaching the boys' takoyaki stand, where she promises that the girls supporting the pancake stand are going to enjoy their food. Later, Miku returns to the stand with the girls but finds the place on fire. On the third day of the festival, Miku invites Futaro to a rooftop, where they find two of their classmates arguing about the takoyaki stand incident. After reprimanding her classmates, Miku confronts Futaro out of jealousy from catching up with Takebayashi, a female classmate from his elementary school, and kisses him. Yotsuba overworks herself in helping different clubs, and on the second day she collapses from exhaustion. While in the hospital, Yotsuba learns from Futaro that some of the students she has helped before offered their assistance during her absence. On the third day of the festival, Yotsuba kisses a resting Futaro. On the first and second days, Itsuki meets guest teacher Mudō, who reveals he is the quintuplets' biological father. Itsuki scolds Mudō for abandoning her mother upon finding out she was pregnant with quintuplets. On the third day, Futaro motivates Itsuki to keep following her dream of being a teacher against Mudō's advice. Later, Maruo, Futaro's father Isanari, and Miku (disguised as Itsuki) meet with Mudō. Itsuki tells Mudō that he is not suitable to be the quintuplets' father after failing to see through Miku's disguise. Itsuki thanks Futaro for helping her find her confidence; unlike her sisters, Itsuki does not kiss Futaro.
At the end of the festival, the quintuplets advise Futaro to approach one of them in individual classrooms to confess. Futaro meets with Yotsuba and confesses his love, but she rejects him as she sees herself as unfit for him. As she runs away from him, Yotsuba recalls her first meeting with Futaro and the promise they made to each other.

title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Sibling's Bond
original_title: 鬼滅の刃 兄妹の絆
overview: Tanjiro finds his family slaughtered and the lone survivor, his sister Nezuko Kamado, turned into a Demon. To his surprise, however, Nezuko still shows signs of human emotion and thought. Thus begins Tanjiro's journey to seek out the Demon who killed their family and turn his sister human again. A recap film of Kimetsu no Yaiba, covering episodes 1-5 with extra footage.
plot:
Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba – Sibling's Bond (Japanese: Kimetsu no Yaiba: Kyōdai no Kizuna) is a 2019 Japanese animated dark fantasy compilation film produced by Ufotable, based on Koyoharu Gotouge's manga Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba. Running 105 minutes, it assembles the first five episodes of the anime television series with additional footage and was screened in theaters shortly before the series premiered on television. The series was directed by Haruo Sotozaki with scripts by the Ufotable staff, character designs by Akira Matsushima and music by Yuki Kajiura and Go Shiina. The voice cast is led by Natsuki Hanae as Tanjiro Kamado and Akari Kito as his sister Nezuko, with Takahiro Sakurai as Giyu Tomioka and Hōchū Ōtsuka as Sakonji Urokodaki.

Set in Japan's Taishō era, the story follows Tanjiro, a kind-hearted boy who supports his family by selling charcoal in a town below their snowy mountain home. Returning one day, he finds his family slaughtered by a demon; only his younger sister Nezuko survives, but she has been turned into a demon herself. The Demon Slayer Giyu Tomioka arrives to kill her, but Tanjiro defends her, and when Nezuko resists her craving for human flesh, Giyu spares them and sends Tanjiro to the trainer Sakonji Urokodaki on Mount Sagiri. After burying their family, the siblings set out. Urokodaki tests Tanjiro's resolve and accepts him as a pupil, and over two years Tanjiro learns Total Concentration and Water Breathing, aided by the mysterious swordsmen Sabito and Makomo, former students of Urokodaki, until he cuts a giant boulder in two. At the Final Selection, a seven-day ordeal on a mountain full of captive demons, he defeats the Hand Demon, which had killed Sabito, Makomo and other students of his master. Tanjiro returns as one of only a handful of survivors, reunites with an awakened Nezuko, receives a sword that turns black and is sent on his first mission to a village where young girls have been disappearing.

Sibling's Bond played in Japanese theaters for two weeks from 29 March 2019, a week before the television premiere on 6 April. Aniplex of America screened it at the Aratani Theatre in Los Angeles on 31 March 2019, and Madman Entertainment presented it in select Australian theaters on 2 April. The series' opening theme, "Gurenge," is performed by LiSA, and Aniplex of America licensed the anime for streaming in North America.

title: Downton Abbey: A New Era
tagline: A cinematic return.
overview: The Crawley family goes on a grand journey to the south of France to uncover the mystery of the dowager countess's newly inherited villa.
plot:
Downton Abbey: A New Era is a 2022 British comedy-drama film directed by Simon Curtis, written by Julian Fellowes, and produced by Carnival Films. The movie serves as the sequel to the 2019 film Downton Abbey and follows the Crawley family on a new adventure.

The story begins with the Crawleys preparing for their annual summer ball at Downton Abbey. However, the festivities are disrupted when Lady Mary's cousin, Patrick Crawley (played by Luke Thompson), arrives unexpectedly. Patrick is revealed to be the long-lost son of Robert Crawley, Earl of Grantham, and his late wife, Cora.

As it turns out, Patrick has been living in France with his wife, Lucy Smith (played by Emma Corrin), a cousin of Lady Mary's. The couple has been struggling financially due to a series of unfortunate events, including the loss of their home and business. They are forced to sell their belongings and move back to England.

The Crawleys take Patrick and Lucy in, offering them a place at Downton Abbey. However, things become complicated when it is revealed that Patrick's presence could potentially disrupt the family's inheritance plans. The family must navigate this new development while also dealing with their own personal struggles and relationships.

Meanwhile, Daisy Mason (played by Sophie McShera), who has been working as a travel agent, convinces the Crawleys to join her on a trip to the south of France. They embark on a journey to the village of Saint-Agnès-sur-Mer, where they hope to find inspiration for their own lives and perhaps even discover some long-lost family secrets.

Upon arrival in Saint-Agnès-sur-Mer, the group becomes embroiled in a mystery surrounding a local artist who has been accused of theft. As they delve deeper into the mystery, they uncover a web of deceit and betrayal that threatens to upend their own lives.

Throughout the film, the characters must navigate their relationships with each other while also confronting their personal demons. Lady Mary struggles with her feelings for Patrick, while Lady Edith (played by Laura Carmichael) grapples with her own sense of identity. Meanwhile, Mr. Carson (played by Jim Carter) and Mrs. Hughes (played by Phyllis Logan) must contend with the challenges of managing a large estate.

As the story unfolds, the Crawleys discover that the local artist is not who they seem to be. In fact, he is an imposter who has been using his charm and wit to swindle the villagers out of their money. The group must work together to expose the truth and bring the imposter to justice.

In the end, the Crawleys emerge victorious, but not without some unexpected twists and turns. Patrick and Lucy's relationship is put to the test as they navigate their feelings for each other amidst the chaos. Meanwhile, the rest of the family comes to terms with their own personal growth and development.

title: Persuasion
overview: Living with her snobby family on the brink of bankruptcy, Anne Elliot is an unconforming woman with modern sensibilities. When Frederick Wentworth - the dashing one she once sent away - crashes back into her life, Anne must choose between putting the past behind her or listening to her heart when it comes to second chances.
plot:
Persuasion is a 2022 American historical romance based on Jane Austen's 1817 novel of the same name. Directed by Carrie Cracknell from a screenplay by Ron Bass and Alice Victoria Winslow, it stars Dakota Johnson as Anne Elliot, Cosmo Jarvis as Captain Frederick Wentworth and Henry Golding as William Elliot, with Richard E. Grant as Sir Walter Elliot, Nikki Amuka-Bird as Lady Russell and Mia McKenna-Bruce as Mary.

Eight years before the story begins, Anne Elliot broke off her engagement to Frederick Wentworth, a young naval officer without wealth or connections, after being persuaded by her family and by Lady Russell, a family friend who has been like a mother to her, that the match was imprudent. Still unmarried years later, Anne lives with her vain and spendthrift father, Sir Walter, whose debts force him to rent out the family estate, Kellynch Hall, to Admiral Croft. While her father and her sister Elizabeth move to Bath, Anne is sent to stay with her self-absorbed younger sister Mary.

Anne soon learns that Admiral Croft's wife is Wentworth's sister, and that Wentworth, now a wealthy and celebrated captain, has returned to shore after years at sea. Their reunion is awkward and painful, especially as Mary's sister-in-law Louisa Musgrove sets her sights on him. On a seaside trip to Lyme, Anne meets Wentworth's naval friends and attracts the attention of her charming cousin William Elliot, the heir to her father's estate. As old feelings resurface and misunderstandings multiply, Anne must decide whether to trust her own heart and whether a second chance at love is possible.

The adaptation takes a deliberately modern approach, with Anne breaking the fourth wall to address the audience directly and contemporary dialogue and humor, a choice that divided viewers and critics.

Persuasion opened in select theaters in the United States on July 8, 2022, a week before its streaming release on Netflix on July 15. Reviews were largely negative: it has about 30 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it chaotically anachronistic, and a Metacritic score of 42.

title: Catch the Fair One
tagline: The predators are her prey.
overview: A Native American boxer embarks on the fight of her life when she goes in search of her missing sister.
plot:
Catch the Fair One is an American thriller written, directed and produced by Josef Kubota Wladyka, from a story he developed with Kali Reis. Reis, a professional boxer of Native American heritage, makes her acting debut in the lead role, with Daniel Henshall, Tiffany Chu, Michael Drayer, Lisa Emery, Kimberly Guerrero and Kevin Dunn in supporting roles. Darren Aronofsky served as an executive producer. The film premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival in 2021 and was released in February 2022.

Reis plays Kaylee, an Indigenous woman and former professional boxer whose career has collapsed. She now struggles with addiction, lives in a women's shelter and works as a waitress. Years earlier, her younger sister Weeta disappeared and is believed to have been taken by a sex trafficking ring, one of the many Indigenous girls who vanish every year with little attention from the authorities. Having received no help from the police, Kaylee has continued the search on her own.

When she finds a lead that may point to Weeta's whereabouts, Kaylee deliberately offers herself to a local trafficking network, convincing one of its recruiters that she is desperate for money. She is drugged and delivered to a buyer, a man who has asked for a "Native girl", by Bobby, the son of the ring's leader, Willie, played by Henshall. Kaylee has planned for this moment: she frees herself with a concealed razor blade and turns the tables on her captors, using her boxing skills and fierce determination to fight her way deeper into the organisation. Each confrontation brings her closer to the people responsible for her sister's disappearance, but also pushes her further into violence and danger, as she discovers that the network extends far beyond a single gang.

The film is a lean, tense revenge thriller that draws attention to the crisis of missing and murdered Indigenous women and girls in North America. It relies heavily on Reis's physical and emotionally raw performance.

Catch the Fair One received positive reviews from critics, who praised Reis's commanding debut, Wladyka's restrained direction and the film's refusal to sensationalise its subject, although some found its narrative bleak and sparse.

title: The Novice
overview: A college freshman joins her university's rowing team and undertakes an obsessive physical and psychological journey to make it to the top varsity boat, no matter the cost.
plot:
The Novice is a 2021 American psychological sports drama film written and directed by Lauren Hadaway in her feature debut. Isabelle Fuhrman stars as an obsessive university freshman who joins the rowing team, with Amy Forsyth and Dilone.

Alex Dall, a fiercely driven college freshman, retakes the same physics exam again and again. Although she has no experience in the sport, she joins her university's novice rowing program and quickly becomes consumed by it, fixating on perfecting her stroke. Her rival is Jamie Brill, a naturally athletic fellow novice who needs a rowing scholarship to stay in school and is soon hailed as the best on the team, which only intensifies Alex's determination. Alex trains relentlessly, letting her studies slide, and both women are promoted to the varsity squad. Jamie fits in easily, but Alex struggles socially and athletically, and after she knocks herself out during a major race she is sent back to the novice boat.

Alex's isolation deepens. She loses her fragile friendship with Jamie, collapses during a joint practice, and trains alone after a varsity rower doubts her. The coach, Pete, is concerned about her self-destructive dedication but eventually helps her practice alone over the break. She begins a relationship with Dani, her former teaching assistant, even as her health declines and a wound on her palm repeatedly reopens and becomes infected.

In the spring, Alex and Jamie compete for a vacant seat in the elite first varsity boat. Alex loses, convinced that teammates deliberately held back while rowing with her, and in her despair she harms herself. Dani ends their relationship, and Alex accuses Jamie of cheating, prompting Jamie to dismiss her as just another privileged student. At a casual end-of-season competition, Alex announces that she will break the team record. She collides with other boats and refuses to turn back when a violent storm sets in, continuing to row alone through the downpour. She finishes, then returns to the boathouse, erases her name from the team board, leaves her jersey behind and walks away.

The Novice premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival in June 2021, where Fuhrman won the award for Best Actress, and was released in the United States on December 17, 2021. It received widespread acclaim, particularly for Fuhrman's performance and Hadaway's direction, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 95% approval, and earned five Independent Spirit Award nominations, including Best Film.

title: Bull
overview: Ten years after he was last seen, a vicious mob enforcer returns home to find his son and methodically track down the gang that double-crossed him. His quest for revenge soon leads to a savage showdown between his wife and her mob boss father.
plot:
Bull is a 2021 British crime thriller with a supernatural edge, written and directed by Paul Andrew Williams. Neil Maskell plays the title character, a former gang enforcer who returns to take revenge on his old associates and his father-in-law and to find his son. It premiered at the Fantasia Film Festival in Montreal on 6 August 2021, screened at the BFI London Film Festival and opened in British cinemas on 5 November 2021.

The film begins with three men burying a burning body in a lonely field. Bull, seemingly unstoppable, then reappears and begins killing those who betrayed him, starting with his ex-wife's sister, Cheryl, and her husband, Ollie, and then the gangster Marco. Flashbacks reveal that ten years earlier Bull was the brutal enforcer for his father-in-law, Norm, a ruthless crime boss. When Bull learned that his wife, Gemma, was using heroin and having an affair with fellow gang member Gary, Norm pressed him to divorce her and give up their son, Aiden, so that Gemma could marry Gary, whose drug connections Norm wanted to exploit. Bull refused. Norm, Gemma, Gary, Marco and a reluctant Clive took him away, set him alight in a caravan and shot him as he staggered out, while the young Aiden looked on.

Enraged by Cheryl's death, Norm tortures Bull's mother, Marge, for information; after he leaves, Bull, watching from the shadows, ends her suffering. Bull forces Clive to help by taking his children, then releases them once Clive lures Gary to a funfair, where Bull leaves Gary to bleed to death on a ride. He mutilates a heroin dealer to learn Gemma's address, forces her to summon Norm, and tricks Norm's men into shooting the dealer in his place. Under torture, Gemma reveals that Aiden, traumatized by his father's death, became a heroin addict. Bull kills Norm and Gemma, then finds Aiden sleeping rough under a bridge and carries him to a church. In the morning the vicar recoils from Bull, whose eyes are entirely black, implying he died a decade ago and came back for vengeance. He asks her to help save Aiden, leaves the dealer's money for his care and returns to the field where he was buried.

David Hayman plays Norm, with Lois Brabin-Platt as Gemma, Henri Charles as Aiden, David Nellist as Clive and Kevin Harvey as Gary. Critics responded strongly, giving it 93% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 72, and Empire's Ian Freer felt Williams and Maskell revitalized the familiar one-man-army story.

title: The Swimmers
overview: From war-torn Syria to the 2016 Rio Olympics, two young sisters embark on a risky voyage, putting their hearts and their swimming skills to heroic use.
plot:
The Swimmers is a 2022 British biographical sports drama directed by Sally El Hosaini, who wrote the screenplay with Jack Thorne, made for Netflix with Working Title Films. It recounts the true story of the Syrian sisters Yusra and Sara Mardini, played by the real-life sisters Nathalie Issa and Manal Issa. Ahmed Malek plays their cousin Nizar, Ali Suliman their father and coach Ezzat, Kinda Alloush their mother Mervat, Matthias Schweighöfer the German coach Sven, and James Krishna Floyd, Elmi Rashid Elmi and Nahel Tzegai fellow refugees.

The film begins in 2011 at a sunny swimming pool in a suburb of Damascus, where the young sisters train under their demanding father. By 2015 the Syrian civil war can no longer be ignored, and the teenagers decide to join the millions of refugees making the dangerous journey to Europe. With Nizar, the sisters, Yusra then only 17, travel through Turkey and are put by smugglers into an overcrowded dinghy heading from near İzmir towards the Greek island of Lesbos. When its motor fails and it begins to sink in the Aegean Sea, Yusra and Sara slip into the water and swim alongside it for hours to lighten the load, helping the eighteen people aboard reach shore.

Their ordeal continues across the Balkans as they are misled and exploited by smugglers, sleep in crowded camps and struggle with the bureaucracy that blocks them from bringing their family out of Syria. Arriving at last in Berlin, Yusra finds a coach, Sven, who helps her return to serious training and to forgive herself, and against the odds she is selected for the Refugee Olympic Team at the 2016 Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro. Closing titles note that Sara later went back to Lesbos to help arriving refugees and was arrested there, facing charges that could bring a long prison sentence.

Filming was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic and took place in 2021 in the United Kingdom, Belgium and Turkey, and both lead actresses learned to swim for their roles; Manal Issa later criticized aspects of the production. The film opened the 2022 Toronto International Film Festival on September 8, had a limited cinema release on November 11 and began streaming on Netflix on November 23, reaching the top ten in 85 countries, and it was nominated for the BAFTA for Outstanding British Film. Critics were largely positive, with Rotten Tomatoes finding it heavy-handed and overlong but uplifting, and RogerEbert.com calling it a moving tribute to the sisters and to refugees.

title: 8 Years
overview: How to overcome true love? Jose considers David the man of his life, but when he suddenly breaks up with him after 8 years together, Jose is haunted by memories of their past relationship, which bring home to him that their life together wasn't as ideal as he once thought.
plot:
8 Years (8 años) is a 2022 Spanish drama film written and directed by JD Alcázar in his feature debut. Starring Miguel Diosdado and Carlos Mestanza as a gay couple trying to come to terms with the end of their long relationship, it also features Natalia Rodríguez, María Maroto, Sergio Momo, Isabel Torres and Eloi Catalán, with music by Sergio Jiménez Lacima and cinematography by Luis Ángel Pérez. The film, which runs 97 minutes, is set on the Canary Island of La Palma. It won the award for best director at the South Film and Arts Academy Festival and was shown at the Madrid Indie Film Festival, was made available on the Spanish streaming platform Filmin, and was given a limited theatrical release in Spain by Phoenix Entertainment Group on 20 January 2023.

Jose (Diosdado) considers David (Mestanza) the man of his life, so when David suddenly breaks up with him after eight years together, he struggles to move on. Some months after the separation, the two men, who have not seen each other since, agree to meet again on La Palma, the island where they first met. Their reunion turns into a road trip around the island in which they attempt something like a second honeymoon, while also throwing old resentments in each other's faces. As Jose is haunted by memories of their past, he begins to realise that their life together was not as ideal as he had believed, and the trip exposes the emotional dependence of one partner and the evasiveness of the other, their experiments with an open relationship and the infidelities that came with it, and the fear of loneliness that keeps them tied to a love that may already be over.

The film was poorly received by Spanish critics. Miguel Ángel Pizarro of eCartelera gave it 3 out of 10, calling it a failed debut and a jumble of ideas that tries at once to be a drama of heartbreak, a Call Me by Your Name-style celebration of its natural landscapes and a defence of open relationships, while sacrificing coherence in its characters' actions; he praised the chemistry between Mestanza and Diosdado but felt the actors could not save a tedious film that recalled the low-budget niche gay cinema of the late 1990s. Salvador Llopart of La Vanguardia gave it one star out of five, describing a clumsy island road movie that wants to be both physical and sentimental but ends up resembling an advertisement, and decine21 rated it 1 out of 10.

title: Seal Team
tagline: Jaws will drop!
overview: After his best friend is killed in a shark attack, Quinn, a lovable yet tenacious seal assembles a SEAL TEAM to fight back against a gang of sharks overtaking the neighborhood. But this merry band of international seals are not at all trained for such a mission. They seek the help of a much more skillful combatant, Claggart, but even his tricks and flips can’t whip these guys into shape. However, with a little bit of ingenuity, intelligence and a lot of heart, our SEAL TEAM may actually be able to bring peace back to their undersea community.
plot:
Seal Team is a 2021 South African animated action comedy co-directed by Greig Cameron and Kane Croudace and produced by Triggerfish Animation Studios, with Cinema Management Group handling worldwide sales. The voice cast includes J. K. Simmons, Jessie T. Usher, Matthew Rhys, Patrick Warburton, Kristen Schaal, Sharlto Copley, John Kani, Dolph Lundgren and the singer Seal. The film follows a group of misfit Cape fur seals who band together to fight a gang of ruthless sharks. After cinema releases in several European and Middle Eastern countries beginning in October 2021, Netflix acquired the rights for other territories and released it in December 2021.

In the 1980s, off the Cape of Storms, an animal military unit called the Hydro Marine Military Force, made up of the veteran seal Claggart, the tech genius seal Switch and a dolphin named Dolph, is ordered to defuse a naval mine. Because seals are color-blind, Claggart cuts the wrong wire, and the explosion wrecks their ship. The unit survives but later drifts apart: Claggart stays alone on the wreck, Switch retreats into eccentric isolation in his own laboratory, and Dolph becomes the star of a popular television show. Claggart's lost dog tags wash up near Seal Island, home to a large colony of seals.

In the present day, a bold young seal named Quinn and his anxious best friend Benji find the tags while fishing. The colony lives in constant fear of a gang of great white sharks, which preys on seals with impunity, and when one attack claims a friend, Quinn decides it is time to fight back. Inspired by the tags, he tracks down the grumpy Claggart and persuades him to train a squad of unlikely recruits, a team of oddball seals with little aptitude for combat, into an elite fighting force. With help from the old unit's members, the recruits learn teamwork and courage while preparing for a showdown with the sharks.

The film drew attention as a South African production from one of Africa's leading animation studios, combining an international voice cast with a story rooted in the wildlife of the Cape coast, where Cape fur seals and great white sharks share the same waters.

title: Blacklight
tagline: They're gonna need more men.
overview: Travis Block is a shadowy Government agent who specializes in removing operatives whose covers have been exposed. He then has to uncover a deadly conspiracy within his own ranks that reaches the highest echelons of power.
plot:
Blacklight is a 2022 action thriller directed and co-written by Mark Williams. Liam Neeson stars as Travis Block, an off-the-books fixer for the FBI who stumbles onto a government conspiracy, with Emmy Raver-Lampman as the journalist Mira Jones, Taylor John Smith as the undercover agent Dusty Crane and Aidan Quinn as FBI Director Gabriel Robinson. It was shot in Melbourne, with a car chase filmed in Canberra, and Mark Isham composed the score.

After a rally in Washington, D.C., the political activist Sofia Flores is killed in a deliberate hit-and-run outside her home. Travis, a Vietnam veteran who quietly handles problems for Robinson, wants to retire and spend time with his daughter Amanda and granddaughter Natalie, but Robinson gives him one more job: bringing in Dusty Crane, an undercover agent who has gone rogue. Dusty has contacted Mira, claiming to know the truth about Sofia's death, and keeps slipping away. When Travis finally reaches him, Dusty says that Robinson ordered the killing, moments before he is shot dead by two FBI agents.

Mira tells Travis that Dusty had spoken of Operation Unity, a secret program run by Robinson that murders innocent civilians. Robinson waves off Travis's questions and warns him to stay away. Mira's editor, Drew, publishes a story about Dusty's death and is killed that night by the same pair of agents, and Amanda and Natalie vanish. Persuaded to help Mira, Travis forces Robinson to open a safe at his house, fights his way past a group of agents, and recovers a hard drive. It reveals that Dusty had fallen in love with Sofia, the woman he was assigned to watch, and that Robinson had her killed because of it. Travis compels Robinson to surrender, Mira publishes the story of the cover-up, and Travis retires and is reunited with his family, who had been placed in witness protection.

Briarcliff Entertainment released the film in the United States on 11 February 2022, where it opened fifth at the box office with $3.5 million. Against a budget of $43 million, it grossed only about $16 million worldwide and was a box-office bomb. Critics were harsh: it holds an 11% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose entire consensus reads "Turn it off," and a Metacritic score of 27.

title: The Wonder
overview: Haunted by her past, a nurse travels from England to a remote Irish village in 1862 to investigate a young girl's supposedly miraculous fast.
plot:
The Wonder is a 2022 period psychological drama film directed by Sebastián Lelio from a screenplay by Emma Donoghue, Lelio and Alice Birch, based on Donoghue's 2016 novel of the same name. Florence Pugh leads an ensemble cast that includes Tom Burke, Niamh Algar, Elaine Cassidy, Toby Jones, Ciarán Hinds and Kíla Lord Cassidy. It premiered at the Telluride Film Festival on 2 September 2022, received a limited theatrical release on 2 November and began streaming on Netflix on 16 November 2022.

In 1862, not long after the Great Famine, Elizabeth "Lib" Wright, an English nurse who served in the Crimean War, is sent to a rural Irish village to observe Anna O'Donnell, a young girl whose devout family claims she has not eaten for four months. Working alongside a nun, Sister Michael, Lib is to report independently to a council of local dignitaries on whether the "fasting girl" is a miracle or a fraud. Many villagers, still scarred by the famine, distrust the English nurse. Anna appears healthy and says she lives on "manna from heaven". At her lodgings Lib meets William Byrne, a journalist for the Daily Telegraph who grew up in the area, lost his family in the famine and suspects the whole affair is a hoax, and the two begin a relationship. Lib, who is grieving the death of her only child and relies on laudanum to sleep, watches Anna closely and at first finds no sign of deception, until she notices the way Anna's mother kisses the girl goodnight and realizes how food is being secretly passed to her. Once the family is kept away from her, Anna's health begins to fail, and she confides the painful reasons behind her fast, which are bound up with her late brother and her family's faith. The council refuses to accept Lib's findings, the family will not intervene, and as Anna grows weaker, Lib must decide how far she is willing to go to save a child whom everyone else seems prepared to let die.

The Wonder received positive reviews, with critics praising its production design and its performances, particularly Pugh's. On Rotten Tomatoes, 85% of 171 critics' reviews are positive, with a consensus that its atmosphere is absorbing and its story fascinating but that the true wonder lies in Pugh's remarkable performance, and Metacritic gave it a score of 71 out of 100.

title: Easter Sunday
tagline: Home is where the crazy is.
overview: A man returns home for an Easter celebration with his riotous, bickering, eating, drinking, laughing, loving family, in this love letter to the Filipino-American community.
plot:
Joe Valencia is a comedian and struggling actor in Los Angeles, known for his beer commercial catch-phrase, "Let's Get This Party Started". He is also a single father to his son Junior, though his work schedule often comes first.
Joe's agent Nick obtains a sitcom audition, but when the producer learns he is half-Filipino, the role turns stereotypical. The audition also causes Joe to miss a school meeting with Junior and his teachers. To compensate, Joe resolves to take Junior with him to his family's Easter Sunday celebration in Daly City for the weekend.
Joe and Junior arrive and meet with Joe's mom, Susan, and his sister, Regina, his cousin Eugene, his aunt Yvonne, uncles Arthur and Manny, and aunt Theresa (who is feuding with Susan). The family goes to church, where Joe learns Eugene wasted an investment meant for a taco truck on a "hype truck" selling useless merchandise.
Joe learns Eugene borrowed from a gangster named Dev in order to pay for the hype truck merchandise. title: See for Me
tagline: Seeing is surviving.
overview: When blind former skier Sophie cat-sits in a secluded mansion, three thieves invade for the hidden safe. Sophie's only defense is army veteran Kelly, who she meets on the See For Me app. Kelly helps Sophie defend herself against the invaders and survive.
plot:
See for Me is a 2021 Canadian thriller film directed by Randall Okita. It stars Skyler Davenport as Sophie Scott, a visually impaired young woman, and Jessica Parker Kennedy as Kelly, a gamer who guides her through a smartphone app, with Laura Vandervoort, Matthew Gouveia, Emily Piggford, Joe Pingue and Kim Coates. The filmmakers spent several years searching for a blind or visually impaired actor for the lead role; Davenport is visually impaired in real life.

Sophie was a promising downhill skier until a diagnosis of retinitis pigmentosa, a degenerative eye disease, ended her Olympic dreams. Refusing her friend Cam's offer to guide her in training for the Paralympics, she gives up skiing and earns money by house-sitting and cat-sitting for wealthy clients, secretly stealing expensive bottles of wine to resell. She takes a job looking after the cat of Debra, a recently divorced woman with a remote mansion in upstate New York. After locking herself out, Sophie uses See for Me, an app that connects blind people with sighted volunteers through video calls, and is helped by Kelly, a gamer in Florida.

That night, three men break into the house to steal millions of dollars hidden in a safe. With the police far away, Sophie contacts Kelly again, but the intruders catch her and cut the call. Sophie tries to bargain with them for a share of the money, but when a sheriff's deputy is killed, she escapes with his gun and reconnects with Kelly, who uses her gaming skills to guide Sophie through the house and help her fight back. In the final confrontation, Sophie discovers who is really behind the robbery and must use her wits and the darkness of the house to survive.

The film adds a twist to the home-invasion thriller through its blind heroine, who is neither a simple victim nor a conventional hero.

See for Me was shot in Canada and released in 2022, grossing about 726,000 dollars worldwide. It received positive reviews, with 80 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised its nifty twist on the home invasion thriller and Davenport's magnetic lead performance.

title: Rogue Hostage
tagline: Free the hostages. Or everyone dies.
overview: A former Marine races against time to save a group of hostages -- including his young daughter and a congressman — when armed militants take over his stepfather's store.
plot:
Rogue Hostage is an American action thriller of 2021 directed by Jon Keeyes. Tyrese Gibson stars as Kyle Snowden, a former Marine, with John Malkovich as his stepfather, Congressman Sam Nelson, Christopher Backus as the mercenary leader Eagan Raize, Michael Jai White as Sparks, Holly Taylor as Mikki, Luna Lauren Velez as Sunshine, Carlos Sanchez as the boy Manny and Brandi Bravo as Kyle's colleague Clove Martinez.

Haunted by nightmares of the battlefield, Kyle left the military after accidentally shooting and killing his own partner, an incident that left him unable to pick up a gun again. He now works for Child Protective Services in a rural American town and is raising his young daughter, Angel, alone since his wife walked out. Meanwhile a band of rogue mercenaries led by Eagan Raize is plotting against Congressman Nelson. Eagan's father, Luther, was once Nelson's business partner and spent eighteen years in prison for fraud, and Eagan is convinced that Nelson destroyed his father's life in order to seize control of their business.

Eagan's crew plants a bomb and takes over Nelson's store while Kyle, Angel and many others are inside, holding them hostage. Intending to ruin Nelson and make an example of him before the town, Eagan instead ends up looting the store's money and taking Sunshine at gunpoint because he is infatuated with her. When the gunmen kill Clove, Kyle's CPS colleague, he finds himself responsible for Manny, a young boy in her care. Forced to take up arms again, Kyle conquers his fear, storms the store and defeats the mercenaries. In the aftermath Nelson tries to persuade the police that the siege was a robbery rather than an act of terrorism, in order to claim the insurance money, but his scheme collapses when Mikki makes off with his money for herself and Sunshine. Kyle prepares to ask the court for temporary custody of Manny, and he and his stepfather finally make their peace.

Originally titled Red 48, the film completed shooting in September 2020 and was released in the United States on 11 June 2021 by Vertical Entertainment and Redbox Entertainment. Critics were unimpressed, giving it a 0% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from ten reviews, though The Guardian's Leslie Felperin, awarding two stars, found the bloody, cheesy action decent fun.

title: Alone Together
tagline: A New York lockdown lovestory.
overview: Strangers June and Charlie have to learn to coexist when they accidentally book the same Airbnb to get away from the pandemic. Alone Together is the ultimate New York lockdown love story.
plot:
Alone Together is a 2022 American romantic drama written and directed by Katie Holmes, her second feature as a director, who also stars in it alongside Jim Sturgess and Derek Luke. Melissa Leo, Zosia Mamet and Becky Ann Baker play supporting roles. Holmes wrote the script at the very start of the COVID-19 lockdown in 2020 and produced it through her company Lafayette Pictures with Jordan Yale Levine, Jordan Beckerman and Jesse Korman of Yale Productions and Shaun Sanghani of SSS Entertainment.

The story opens with a montage of June, a Manhattan restaurant critic, enjoying a glamorous life of parties and lavish meals with her boyfriend John. In mid-March 2020, as the city shuts down and panic spreads, she sets out for a rental house in upstate New York that John has booked for the two of them. Train service has been cut, so she takes a Lyft, and on the way John texts that he will not join her after all because he wants to stay in the city with his worried parents. When June reaches the house she finds the lights on and a stranger, Charlie, already living there: the property has been double-booked, apparently because its owners are in the middle of a messy divorce.

With nowhere else to go, the two agree to share the house. June is a polished, type-A transplant who has made New York her identity; Charlie, a native New Yorker who restores old motorcycles and, as he puts it, just about anything, is at first wary of her haughty manner. Their prickly coexistence gradually warms as they cook, drink, sing karaoke, play games, sewing masks out of cloth and shoelaces as news reports mark the passing weeks of the pandemic. They confide in one another about their families, comfort each other through personal losses and encourage each other's ambitions. As the bond deepens into romance, June must eventually confront her unresolved relationship with John.

Alone Together had its world premiere in the Tribeca Film Festival's Spotlight Narrative section on July 14, 2022, and Vertical Entertainment released it theatrically in the United States on July 22, followed by video on demand a week later. Reviews were mostly negative, with about 28 percent of critics on Rotten Tomatoes rating it positively. The Hollywood Reporter found it a predictable but sweet and disarming time capsule of the early pandemic, praising the leads' easy chemistry, while RogerEbert.com faulted its heavy-handed, overly predictable script and thin characters.

title: Fortress
tagline: This prison has no bars.
overview: The story revolves around a top-secret resort for retired U.S. intelligence officers. A group of criminals led by Balzary breach the compound, hellbent on revenge on Robert, forcing the retired officer and his son to save the day.
plot:
Fortress is a 2021 American action thriller directed by James Cullen Bressack from a screenplay by Alan Horsnail, based on a story by Emile Hirsch and Randall Emmett. Jesse Metcalfe stars as Paul, with Bruce Willis as his father Robert, Chad Michael Murray as the villain Frederick Balzary, Kelly Greyson as Kate, the director of the facility, Shannen Doherty as its security chief Dobbs, alongside Ser'Darius Blain. It was the first of two films shot back to back in Puerto Rico in 2021, followed by Fortress: Sniper's Eye.

Robert, a retired CIA officer, lives at Forge Mountain, a secluded, top-secret resort that shelters former U.S. intelligence operatives after they leave government service. His son Paul, who runs a cryptocurrency company, has not seen or heard from him in three years, since around the time Paul's mother died, but now tracks him down out of necessity: the business is close to bankruptcy, and Paul needs $5 million to make it cash positive, which means persuading Robert to sign a document releasing money from his mother's estate. Paul is unaware that his father has been quietly following his life and career.

The awkward reunion is cut short when a team of mercenaries led by Balzary breaks into the resort. Balzary, who once worked alongside Robert, has a score to settle and knows about his old colleague's history with dark money. Robert hurries his son into the Fortress, a high-tech underground bunker with steel walls and an arsenal, but the attackers kill the guards, follow them inside and tie them up. Balzary explains that Russians have kidnapped his wife, Sasha, and that he needs the money Robert stole from him to pay her ransom; Robert has invested it in cryptocurrency, and he makes Paul memorise the access code exactly, telling him it could save his life. Learning for the first time about his father's past, Paul must fight alongside Robert, Kate and Dobbs to survive, discovering along the way that he can stand up for himself.

Lionsgate released the film in select theaters and on demand on 17 December 2021. Reviews were mostly negative, with only one of five critics positive on Rotten Tomatoes; The New York Times dismissed it as one of Bressack's cheap thrillers, while Film Threat and Cinema Daily US praised its pace, action and production values. Willis was nominated for a special Golden Raspberry category devoted to his 2021 performances, later rescinded after his retirement because of aphasia.

title: Rosaline
tagline: The love story you know, the ex you don’t.
overview: Left heartbroken after Romeo begins to pursue her cousin Juliet, Rosaline schemes to foil the famous romance and win back her guy in this comedic twist of Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet.
plot:
Rosaline is an American romantic comedy of 2022 directed by Karen Maine and written by Scott Neustadter and Michael H. Weber, adapted from Rebecca Serle's young adult novel When You Were Mine (2012), itself a riff on Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet. Kaitlyn Dever stars as Rosaline, Romeo's spurned love, with Isabela Merced as Juliet, Kyle Allen as Romeo, Sean Teale as the suitor Dario Penza, Minnie Driver as the Nurse, Bradley Whitford as Rosaline's father and Christopher McDonald as Lord Capulet.

Rosaline, a free-spirited member of the house of Capulet, has been secretly seeing Romeo, a Montague, and plans to meet him at the Capulet masquerade. Instead, an outing with Dario, a suitor chosen by her father, leaves them stranded on a boat in a storm, and she rudely rebuffs him. At the ball, Romeo meets and falls for her cousin Juliet. Discovering his new romance, Rosaline sets out to sabotage it, telling Juliet that Romeo courts many women, dragging her to a seedy tavern to meet other men and stealing Romeo's letters. Juliet sends Romeo away, but realises her cousin's deception when she sees Rosaline's necklace engraved with her and Romeo's names. Rosaline then persuades her friend Count Paris, who wants to hide his homosexuality, to court Juliet, and the Capulets eagerly approve.

Learning that Romeo plans to elope with Juliet, Rosaline reluctantly accepts Dario's escort to break into the Montague estate at night; Dario fights off the guards, but they arrive too late to stop the secret wedding. Rosaline's feelings for Dario soften just as he announces he is rejoining the navy. When Tybalt intercepts the letters Rosaline returns to Juliet, he duels Romeo and is killed, and the two families declare war. Rosaline apologises to Dario and asks him to smuggle the lovers away on his boat, but Juliet has already taken a potion to feign death. In the tomb, Rosaline finds Romeo alive, since Dario has told him of the ruse, and has him pretend to be dead too, then scolds the feuding families into reconciling. Rosaline and Dario see the couple off by boat and share a kiss, while a mid-credits scene shows Romeo and Juliet struggling to find anything in common.

After a premiere at the El Capitan Theatre on 6 October 2022, Rosaline was released on Hulu in the United States and on Disney+ abroad on 14 October. Critics praised Dever's performance, giving it 75% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Muppets Haunted Mansion

plot:
Muppets Haunted Mansion is a 2021 American comedy horror film directed by Justin Simien and written by Jason Segel, Nicholas Stoller, and Lee Eisenberg. The movie takes place in the classic Disney theme park attraction, The Haunted Mansion.

The story begins with Dr. Terminus (played by Eddie Murphy), a ghostly con artist who has been haunting the mansion for decades. He is determined to scare away all the living visitors and make it his own personal playground. However, his plans are foiled when he discovers that a new family, the Muppets, have moved into the mansion.

The Muppets, consisting of Kermit the Frog (played by Matt Vogel), Miss Piggy (played by Eric Jacobson), Fozzie Bear (played by Peter Linz), and Gonzo (played by Dave Goelz), are initially excited to explore their new home. However, they soon realize that it's not as empty as they thought.

As the family tries to settle in, they begin to experience strange occurrences and ghostly encounters. Dr. Terminus sees an opportunity to scare them away and starts to manipulate events to make it seem like the mansion is haunted by malevolent spirits.

Meanwhile, Kermit becomes convinced that there's a real ghost haunting the mansion, which he believes is the spirit of his late friend, Rizzo the Rat (played by Steve Whitmire). As the story unfolds, the Muppets work together to uncover the truth behind Dr. Terminus' sinister plans and put an end to his schemes.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of humorous moments, clever references to The Haunted Mansion attraction, and exciting ghostly encounters. The film also features a number of celebrity cameos, including Tiffany Haddish, Rosario Dawson, and Wanda Sykes.

As the Muppets delve deeper into the mystery, they discover that Dr. Terminus' plan is not just about scaring them away but also about using their energy to fuel his own ghostly powers. In a thrilling climax, Kermit and his friends must work together to outsmart Dr. Terminus and put an end to his evil plans.

In the end, the Muppets succeed in defeating Dr. Terminus and restoring peace to the mansion. The movie concludes with the family enjoying their new home and looking forward to many more adventures together.

Overall, Muppets Haunted Mansion is a fun and spooky comedy that brings a fresh take to the classic Disney theme park attraction. With its talented voice cast, clever writing, and exciting plot twists, it's sure to delight both fans of The Muppets and horror enthusiasts alike.
