overview: Four insomniac med school students are lured into a neuroscience experiment that spirals out of control and must find a way out before it’s too late.
plot:
Deep (Thai: โปรเจกต์ลับ หลับ เป็น ตาย, roughly "Secret Project: Sleep, Live, Die") is a 2021 Thai mystery thriller film produced by Transformation Films and released on Netflix. It was written and directed by a team of students from Bangkok University, with directing credits shared by Sita Likitvanichkul, Jetarin Ratanaserikiat, Apirak Samudkidpisan, Thanabodee Uawithya and Adirek Wattaleela. Panisara Rikulsurakan stars as Jane, with Kay Lertsittichai as Win, Supanaree Sutavijitvong as Cin, Krit Jeerapattananuwong as Peach, Warisara Jitpreedasakul as June and Dujdao Vadhanapakorn as Professor Nichcha.

Jane, a medical student, lives with her delinquent younger sister June and cares for their grandmother. Overwhelmed by studying, housework and debt, she has become an insomniac. Her professor, Nichcha, suggests that she join a study run by a German pharmaceutical company. Its head scientist, Hans Miller, explains that the experiment, called Deep, has three levels and aims to harvest Qratonin, a brain chemical that keeps people awake, through a microchip implanted in the subject's neck. Promised generous rewards, Jane signs a non-disclosure agreement and receives the implant and a watch to monitor her Qratonin level, along with a warning: if she falls asleep for more than 60 seconds before reaching 100 percent, the chip will stop her heart.

Jane meets fellow subjects Win, a partygoer, Peach, a gaming nerd, and Cin, a popular student, and the four, calling themselves Non-Non, complete the first two levels as their sleep deprivation causes vivid hallucinations. When Cin discovers that Peach is the stalker she has been afraid of, she collapses and nearly dies, and the group quits and drifts apart. After Jane sees a student die because of Deep and her grandmother suffers a stroke, she learns that June has joined the experiment too; Hans warns that June's third level has begun and that the chip will not be removed unless Jane brings her friends back. The reunited group enters the final level, but by the sixth day chaos erupts. Jane discovers that the company is a front, Hans is an actor and Nichcha is the mastermind, harvesting Qratonin to revive her comatose lover, Jed, who fell from a building through lack of sleep. Nichcha locks them up, but the friends fake Win's death to trick her and overpower her. She is arrested, the chips are removed and the friends mend their lives.

title: Poker Face
tagline: Everyone has a limit.
overview: A yearly high-stakes poker game between childhood friends turns into chaos when the tech billionaire host unveils an elaborate scheme to seek revenge for the ways they've betrayed him over the years. But as his plans unfold, a group of thieves hatch plans of their own breaking into the mansion thinking it is empty. The old friends quickly band together and the years of playing the game help them win their way through a night of terror.
plot:
Poker Face is a 2022 Australian thriller written and directed by Russell Crowe, who also stars as Jake Foley, a tech billionaire. The cast includes Liam Hemsworth, RZA, Brooke Satchwell and Aden Young, and the film was shot in Australia, with much of the action confined to a single lavish, secluded mansion. The film had a limited theatrical release on 16 November 2022, followed by a video-on-demand release a week later.

Jake Foley, who made a fortune from software, invites his childhood friends to his luxurious, high-security mansion for a night of high-stakes poker. The group includes Mikey, Alex and Paul, men whose lives have taken very different paths since their youth and who have stayed bound by old loyalties and rivalries. As the cards are dealt, it soon becomes clear that Jake has a hidden purpose: he wants his friends to reveal the secrets they have kept for years, and he has taken steps to ensure that they tell the truth.

As the night goes on, the confessions emerge. Mikey admits that his life is miserable and that he has brought a gun with which he intends to kill himself. Alex reveals that he has been sleeping with Jake's wife. Paul confesses that, burdened by debts, he has been passing information about Jake's life to his brother Victor. The evening takes a dangerous turn when Victor and his gang break into the house intending to steal Jake's valuable art collection, and Jake's wife and daughter arrive unexpectedly. Trapped in the mansion with the robbers, the friends must put aside their grievances and band together to survive. Jake uses his skill at bluffing to outwit the intruders, telling Victor that he has drunk poison from one of the wine glasses and tricking him into taking a lethal dose under the pretense of an antidote.

Poker Face received negative reviews from critics, who found the plot convoluted and the shifts in tone awkward, although some praised Crowe's commanding screen presence. Several reviewers felt that its blend of character drama and home-invasion thriller never quite cohered.

title: Bandit
tagline: He pulled off the perfect heist 59 times.
overview: After escaping a Michigan prison, a charming career criminal assumes a new identity in Canada and goes on to rob a record 59 banks and jewellery stores while being hunted by a rogue task force. Based on the story of The Flying Bandit.
plot:
Bandit is a 2022 Canadian biographical crime film directed by Allan Ungar and written by Kraig Wenman. Josh Duhamel stars as Gilbert Galvan Jr., with Elisha Cuthbert, Nestor Carbonell and Mel Gibson. It is based on the true story of Galvan, known as the Flying Bandit, who holds the record for the most consecutive bank robberies in Canadian history, and draws largely on interviews and accounts in the 1996 true crime book The Flying Bandit by Robert Knuckle and Ed Arnold. Redbox Entertainment and Quiver Distribution released the film in North American theaters and on demand on 23 September 2022.

Gilbert Galvan Jr., a charming career criminal, escapes from a prison in Michigan and crosses the border into Ontario, where he takes on a new identity as Robert Whiteman. In Ottawa he falls in love with Andrea, a social worker played by Cuthbert, but he has no way of supporting the comfortable life he wants to give her. Needing money, he returns to crime with the help of Tommy Kay, a local crime boss played by Gibson, who agrees to fund his first heist in exchange for a share of the proceeds.

Galvan discovers that he has a remarkable talent for robbing banks. Using a series of elaborate disguises and posing as a security analyst whose job requires constant travel, he flies across Canada, sometimes robbing banks in several cities in a single day before returning home to his unsuspecting wife. As the robberies pile up, he becomes a folk hero of sorts, and the press nicknames him "the Flying Bandit." His growing notoriety attracts the attention of a determined police detective, Snyder, played by Carbonell, who becomes obsessed with catching him, while his double life puts increasing strain on his marriage and his partnership with Kay grows more dangerous. The film tracks the more than fifty robberies he committed over several years and the investigation that finally brought him down.

Bandit received mixed to positive reviews, with critics singling out Duhamel's charismatic performance and the film's light, playful tone, which treats its true-crime story as a breezy caper rather than a gritty drama.

title: Meet Cute
tagline: Who says there's only one chance to make a first impression?
overview: A wildly inventive deconstruction of the romantic comedy built around the question: What would you do if you could travel to your loved ones’ past, heal their traumas, fix their problems, and change them into the perfect partner?
plot:
Meet Cute is a 2022 American romantic dark comedy directed by Alex Lehmann. Kaley Cuoco and Pete Davidson star as a woman who uses a time machine to relive a perfect first date over and over and the man she keeps meeting. Filmed in New York City in August 2021, it was released digitally on Peacock on September 21, 2022.

In Manhattan, Sheila discovers that a tanning bed in the back of a nail salon run by a woman named June is actually a time machine that sends her back one day. One evening she meets Gary, a gentle, slightly awkward man, in a bar. Their date is a delight: they share the same taste in drinks, trade stories about their childhoods and find an easy rapport. During the evening, Sheila casually tells Gary that she has been reliving this same night repeatedly, and the two part on warm terms.

Over the course of months of resets, Sheila reveals more. She first used the machine on the day she had planned to take her own life by jumping from the Manhattan Bridge, and her first date with Gary made her feel happy for the first time in years, so she keeps returning to it. She also mentions a kind cable repairman who was nice to her as a child, without knowing why the memory stays with her. When she tells Gary she loves him, it unsettles him.

After hundreds of identical evenings, Sheila grows restless and decides to improve Gary by traveling further back into his past. Posing as a neighbor, "Uncle Charlie," she gets the young Gary interested in sports and removes several negative influences from his life, turning him into a confident, successful businessman. When she admits what she has done, Gary is horrified, and although Sheila restores his original past, he begins experiencing déjà vu and pieces together the truth. Using what he has learned, Gary travels back in time himself in an attempt to help the young Sheila, and he turns out to have been the cable repairman who showed her kindness when she was a girl.

Realizing that endlessly reliving the same day no longer brings her joy, Sheila returns to the bridge. Alerted by June, Gary catches up with her and convinces her that the future is worth seeing, telling her that they meet again tomorrow. Sheila follows him off the bridge, and as the sun rises, the two begin a genuinely new day together.

Reviews were mixed; Rotten Tomatoes reported 59% approval, and Metacritic gave it 50 out of 100.

title: Something in the Dirt
overview: When neighbors John and Levi witness supernatural events in their LA apartment building, they realize documenting the paranormal could inject some fame and fortune into their wasted lives.
plot:
Something in the Dirt is a 2022 American science fiction comedy horror film directed by and starring Justin Benson and Aaron Moorhead, from a screenplay by Benson. It is the fifth feature from the filmmaking duo, who conceived it during the COVID-19 lockdowns of 2020 and shot it over the course of a year with a crew of just twelve people, using Benson's own apartment as the main location. The film had its world premiere online at the 2022 Sundance Film Festival.

A man wakes up in a small, grimy apartment in Los Angeles. Through conversations with a neighbour we learn that he is Levi, a spear-fisherman who scrapes by on odd jobs, and that the neighbour, John, is an occasional maths teacher who belongs to an evangelical, apocalypse-minded church. The two strangers soon notice that something strange is happening in their building: a quartz object floats and glows of its own accord, revealing a mysterious symbol, and the apartment is troubled by unexplained lights, noises, tremors and radio signals.

Sensing an opportunity, the pair decide to make a documentary about the phenomenon. Their investigation leads them across the city, following a chain of clues and coincidences that seem to connect the events in their apartment to a wider pattern stretching across Los Angeles. As the project grows, so do the tensions between them. Levi repeatedly warns that the pursuit is becoming dangerous and suggests they stop, but John presses ahead regardless. He dismisses Levi's theories in favour of his own constantly shifting explanations, and he begins to show signs of compulsive lying and a callous disregard for others, ignoring unmistakable warnings such as sudden radiation burns and impossibly accelerated plant growth.

Eventually the two men have a bitter falling-out. That night John wakes to find himself floating above his bed before dropping back down, and when he goes outside he sees Levi suspended high in the sky. In documentary-style interviews, John later explains that Levi died, his mangled body found near a house the pair had investigated, surrounded by strange totems and a blacked-out manuscript. Asked to explain what happened, John says only that his calculations were wrong, and remains determined to finish the film.

Critics responded warmly. Rotten Tomatoes reported 91% positive reviews, its consensus saying the film reaffirms the duo's distinctive and darkly alluring vision, and Metacritic gave it a score of 76 out of 100.

title: White Elephant
tagline: Live by a code. Die by a bullet.
overview: An ex-marine enforcer must battle his conscience and code of honor when he is forced to do things for the mob.
plot:
White Elephant is a 2022 American action crime thriller directed by Jesse V. Johnson, who wrote the screenplay with Erik Martinez from his own story. Michael Rooker stars as Gabriel Tancredi, with Bruce Willis as Arnold Solomon, Olga Kurylenko as Vanessa Flynn and John Malkovich as the lawyer Glen Follett, alongside Vadhir Derbez, Michael Rose, Lauren Buglioli and Louie Ski Carr. It was produced by Corey Large through 308 Enterprises and BondIt Media Capital, with music by Sean Murray and cinematography by Jonathan Hall.

Gabriel is a widowed former Marine who has spent years as an enforcer for his friend, the mob boss Arnold Solomon, and is now mentoring a brash young protégé, Carlos Garcia (Derbez). Still mourning his wife, a wildlife activist, and regularly visiting her resting place, he dreams of leaving the life behind and using his skills to protect elephants in Africa, as she always wanted. When Solomon orders a hit on a Mexican gangster, Carlos botches the job and blows up a building, and the attack is witnessed by two police officers, Vanessa Flynn and her partner Walter Koschek (Rose). To protect himself, Solomon orders Gabriel to eliminate both witnesses.

Koschek is quickly killed, but Vanessa, an ex-soldier haunted by the violence she has seen on the job, proves far harder to catch, evading one kill squad after another. As Solomon's increasingly reckless decisions trigger more bloodshed and rival gangs move in, Gabriel finds himself drawn to Vanessa, discovering that she shares a birthday with his late wife. Torn between loyalty and his own code of honor, he decides for the first time in years to do the right thing, turning against Solomon to protect her. The conflict culminates at Gabriel's country house, where he and Vanessa fight off the remaining gunmen of Solomon's organization.

Filmed in Georgia beginning in April 2021, White Elephant is one of the last films Willis made before retiring from acting due to illness; crew members later described him as confused on set, and Johnson said he would not work with him again under such circumstances. The film was released in select US theaters by RLJE Films and on AMC+ on 3 June 2022. Reviews were mostly negative, with critics calling the script thin and repetitive, though Rooker's warm, commanding performance and the violent finale drew praise.

title: Jerry & Marge Go Large
tagline: It's never too late to risk it all.
overview: The remarkable true story of how retiree Jerry Selbee discovers a mathematical loophole in the Massachusetts lottery and, with the help of his wife, Marge, wins $27 million dollars and uses the money to revive their small Michigan town.
plot:
Jerry & Marge Go Large is a 2022 American comedy-drama directed by David Frankel and written by Brad Copeland, based on Jason Fagone's 2018 HuffPost article about a real-life retired couple who legally exploited a loophole in a state lottery. Bryan Cranston and Annette Bening star, with Rainn Wilson, Larry Wilmore and Michael McKean. It premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on June 15, 2022, and was released on Paramount+ two days later.

In the struggling small town of Evart, Michigan, Jerry Selbee is pushed into retirement after 42 years at a factory. A gifted mathematician with time on his hands, he discovers a statistical loophole in the state lottery game WinFall: when the jackpot reaches $2 million without a winner, the money "rolls down" to lower prize tiers, and anyone buying enough tickets is virtually guaranteed a profit. Testing the theory in secret, he first loses money, then buys far more tickets and turns a profit. When his wife, Marge, finds out, she is thrilled and wants to join in. After Michigan's WinFall is discontinued, the couple begin driving to Massachusetts, where a similar game exists, buying tickets at a store in Sunderland.

To increase their stakes, they form a corporation and sell shares to friends and neighbors. Their winnings grow, and the dividends help revive Evart, as shuttered businesses reopen and plans are made to bring back the town's jazz festival. Their success attracts the attention of Tyler, an arrogant Harvard student running his own WinFall syndicate, who discovers their operation and demands that they stop, threatening to hack their accounts. Jerry nearly gives up, but with the encouragement of his son and the town, he keeps playing. When Tyler manipulates the game to trigger a roll-down early, cutting the Selbees out, Jerry confronts him in front of his fellow students, who abandon him, and persuades the lottery commission to announce roll-downs publicly to level the playing field.

A Boston Globe report on the loophole leads to the game's cancellation. The Selbees decide to sit out the final roll-down, but their investors secretly travel to Massachusetts to buy tickets across the state for one last big win. At the revived jazz festival, Jerry and Marge are celebrated as the heroes who brought their town back to life, having won around $27 million over the years.

Reviews were mixed to positive. Rotten Tomatoes reported 67% approval, and Metacritic gave it 52 out of 100.

plot:
Straight Outta Nowhere: Scooby-Doo! Meets Courage the Cowardly Dog is a 2021 animated film that brings together two beloved cartoon franchises, Scooby-Doo and Courage the Cowardly Dog. The movie follows the adventures of Shaggy Rogers (voiced by Robbie Daymond) and Scooby-Doo (voiced by Scott Innes), who are on their way to a music festival in Nowhere, Kansas.

Upon arrival, they meet Eustace Bagge (voiced by Jason Alexander), Courage's owner, and his family. However, things take a dark turn when the town is plagued by supernatural occurrences, including ghostly apparitions, monsters, and unexplained events. The Scooby-Doo gang soon discovers that these events are connected to an ancient curse that has been awakened in Nowhere.

As the mystery unfolds, Shaggy and Scooby team up with Courage (voiced by Eric Bauza) to uncover the truth behind the curse. Along the way, they encounter a range of bizarre characters, including a ghostly cowboy, a possessed preacher, and a mysterious woman who seems to be connected to the curse.

Throughout their investigation, Shaggy and Scooby use their signature skills to gather clues and solve puzzles, while Courage provides his own unique brand of cowardice to help them navigate the supernatural threats. Meanwhile, Eustace's family is torn apart by the events unfolding in Nowhere, leading to a heartwarming moment of connection between Shaggy and Muriel Bagge (voiced by Grey DeLisle).

As the mystery deepens, the Scooby-Doo gang discovers that the curse is connected to an ancient ritual that was performed by the town's founders. They must work together to break the curse and restore peace to Nowhere before it's too late.

The film features a mix of humor, action, and heart, blending the signature styles of both franchises. The animation is vibrant and colorful, with plenty of nods to the original Scooby-Doo and Courage the Cowardly Dog series. The voice cast delivers solid performances, bringing the characters to life in a way that feels true to their respective franchises.

Overall, Straight Outta Nowhere: Scooby-Doo! Meets Courage the Cowardly Dog is a fun and entertaining film that brings together two beloved cartoon franchises in a unique and exciting way. With its blend of humor, action, and heart, it's sure to delight fans of both Scooby-Doo and Courage the Cowardly Dog.

title: The Friendship Game
tagline: Win together or die alone
overview: A group of teens in a small town come across a strange object that tests their loyalties to each other with increasingly destructive consequences the deeper into the game they go.
plot:
The Friendship Game is a 2022 Canadian science fiction horror film directed by Scooter Corkle, his second feature, from the first feature-length screenplay by Damien Ober. Produced by Social Construct and Scythia Films, it stars Peyton List, Brendan Meyer, Kelcey Mawema, Kaitlyn Santa Juana and Dylan Schombing, with Miranda Edwards and Jennifer Copping in supporting roles. RLJE Films released it in the United States on 11 November 2022.

Zooza, known as Z (List), Rob (Meyer), Courtney (Mawema) and Cotton (Santa Juana) are close friends in a small town who are at a turning point in their lives as they prepare to leave for college. While browsing at a yard sale, Z and Cotton come across a strange orb-like object, and the ominous woman selling it tells them that it is "the Friendship Game", which tests true friendship by having the players reveal their deepest desires. Unfazed, they buy it, and all four friends place their fingers on the object and confess what they most want. Their wishes come at an unexpected cost that begins to consume their lives: at a party soon afterwards, Cotton tries to warn the others that something is wrong, discovers Z and Rob together and storms off, and then disappears, prompting a police investigation. Meanwhile Kyle (Schombing), who spends most of his time at his computer, has been secretly watching the four friends, and the film increasingly blurs the digital and physical worlds with glitching, warped imagery. Told in chapters from each character's perspective, the story shows how the game sets the friends against one another with increasingly destructive consequences the deeper they go.

Reviews were largely negative, although Peyton List's performance was widely praised. Chase Hutchinson of Collider likened the premise to Wish Upon (2017) and felt the film gestured at the existential, internet-age concerns of We're All Going to the World's Fair, but said that, despite some occasionally enrapturing visuals, it spun its wheels and leaned on conventional scares that failed to land. Bobby LePire of Film Threat called it awful on every level except for List, who he said made the cringe-inducing dialogue believable and was the only cast member to inject real drama or fear, while criticising the rest of the cast, singling out Meyer for lacking screen presence. Screen Rant described it as a frustrating horror mystery that felt like a messy rough draft.

tagline: She'll love him to death.
overview: Chris, a wealthy divorcee, lives in a high-tech house of his own design in Montana. His life changes when he meets Sky, a mysterious young woman who draws him out of his shell and moves in after Chris is injured.
plot:
Shattered is a 2022 American psychological thriller directed by Luis Prieto and written by David Loughery. Cameron Monaghan stars as Chris, a wealthy, recently separated tech entrepreneur, with Lilly Krug as Sky, the young woman who enters his life, Frank Grillo, Sasha Luss as Chris's estranged wife Jamie, and John Malkovich as Ronald, a motel landlord. It was released in January 2022.

Chris, who made his fortune creating Watchdog, a home security system, lives alone in his isolated, high-tech mansion and has been putting off signing the divorce papers sent by his wife, Jamie, who felt that his work always came first. During a late-night trip to a grocery store he meets Sky, and when her ride is canceled he offers to drive her home. At the run-down motel where she is staying, she hesitates to go inside, explaining that her roommate, Lisa, is unpredictable because of her drug use. Chris invites her back to his house to wait, they spend the night together, and she returns to the motel in the morning to find Lisa furious.

Soon after, Chris visits Sky at her workplace and, returning to his car, interrupts someone trying to break into it. In the ensuing struggle he is badly injured and left with a broken leg in a cast. With his mobility limited, Sky offers to look after him, and he gives her the access codes to his house, which is entirely controlled by Watchdog. When Sky goes back to the motel to collect her belongings, Lisa hints that she knows things about her and that Sky cannot simply leave. The motel's landlord, Ronald, fed up with excuses about overdue rent, lets himself into their rooms and makes a horrifying discovery. As Sky settles into Chris's home, her behavior grows increasingly sinister, and Chris, trapped by his injury inside his own fortress, gradually realizes that the woman caring for him has a hidden agenda involving his money, his security system and his estranged family.

Shattered received negative reviews, holding a 19 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 27. Angela Dawson of Forbes was more positive, describing it as a simmering thriller reminiscent of classic femme fatale films with a modern sensibility, while most critics found it derivative and implausible.

title: Taurus
overview: A rising but troubled musician searches for the inspiration to record one last song, pushing himself deep into the void.
plot:
Taurus, previously known as Good News, is a 2022 American drama film directed by Tim Sutton, who wrote it with Colson Baker, the rap-rock musician known as Machine Gun Kelly. Baker, who also served as executive producer and composer, stars as Cole, a fictional rock star closely modeled on his own celebrity image, with Maddie Hasson as his personal assistant, Ilana, Scoot McNairy as his manager, Ray, Ruby Rose as Bub, Megan Fox as his ex, Mae, and Naomi Wild as Lena.

The film follows the final days of Cole, a hugely popular but alienated and self-destructive musician, over the course of about a week in Los Angeles. He drifts between recording sessions, interviews, brand ambassador meetings, barroom binges and occasional, detached visits with his 10-year-old daughter, Rosie, while consuming an ever-growing array of drugs and alcohol. He spends his nights with a drug-dealer friend and a series of interchangeable lovers, returning to a sterile modernist mansion in the Hollywood Hills.

At the center of the story is his relationship with Ilana, his beleaguered and mistreated but devoted assistant, who acts as his surrogate mother, sister and babysitter. She ferries the remote, uncooperative Cole from one obligation to the next, tries to keep him functioning if not sober, absorbs the blame from his sharkish manager whenever he fails to deliver, and cleans up after him each morning. Cole has a tense, nearly wordless confrontation with Mae, and Lena, a singer, records a hook for one of his songs. A cryptic subplot follows a suburban tragedy involving one of Cole's fans. As Cole's physical and mental deterioration accelerates and Ilana's patience wears thin, the story moves toward its grim, inevitable end.

Taurus premiered in the Panorama section of the 72nd Berlin International Film Festival on February 13, 2022, and RLJE Films released it in limited theaters and on demand in the United States on November 18, 2022. Reviews were mixed, with 64% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 51; the Rotten Tomatoes consensus said it fails to delve deeply into the creative process but offers some insight into the double-edged nature of celebrity. Variety's Guy Lodge praised Baker's committed, unflattering performance and the film's atmospheric style but found Cole a hollow center, singling out Hasson as the film's heart. Deadline's Anna Smith found the bickering star-assistant relationship darkly funny and touching.

title: Jungle Run
tagline: The search for their father... led them to hell!
overview: A brother and sister's journey into the jungle to find their missing father.
plot:
Jungle Run is a 2021 American adventure film directed and photographed by Noah Luke and produced by The Asylum as a "mockbuster" of Disney's Jungle Cruise, released in the United States about a month ahead of that film. The cast includes Alyson Gorske, Richard Grieco, Jamie Petitto, Wade Hunt Williams and Jack Pearson.

In the Brazilian Amazon, the anthropologist Nicholas Kieran unearths a statue holding a striking green triangular relic. When a member of his team proposes selling it, a piercing sound rings out and swarms of insects attack the dig. Learning that their father is missing, his children Amanda and Scott set off to find him. Amanda hires the boat of Captain Lebecq, who agrees to take her upriver along with Vera, a woman claiming to be in charge of the excavation, and Scott jumps aboard at the last moment. Guided by Lebecq and his crewmen Sark and Teese, the group goes ashore, where poison dart frogs attack Lebecq. As Sark prepares to cut off his leg, a seemingly blind stranger emerges from the forest, treats the wound and warns them of the Curupira, an indigenous deity who fiercely protects the rainforest and dwells at the heart of the jungle.

Pressing on, the travelers lose Teese to piranhas that wreck their boat, and are scattered by crocodiles. Amanda and Lebecq reach the abandoned dig and escape an attack by bullet ants, while Nicholas, the sole survivor of his team, is revealed to be living in a trailer with the relic. Captured by a tribe of cannibals who mistake Scott for one of the loggers destroying the forest, the group escapes when giant spiders drop from a sacred tree and attack their captors. Following clues left by the blind man, Amanda deduces that the heart of the jungle is a waterfall, behind which giant snakes swallow her companions; she cuts her way out and frees all but Sark. Outside they find the dying Lebecq and their father bound nearby. When the Curupira, a huge two-legged creature with flames on its back, appears, they destroy the relic to free it, while Vera tries to shoot the deity and is devoured by a giant Venus flytrap. The family heads home as the Curupira watches over the forest.

Released on 25 June 2021, the film received poor reviews. German critics mocked its cheap effects, simple story and childish dialogue, though some singled out Gorske's committed performance and the film's ecological message.

title: Kitchen Brigade
overview: Cathy is a sous-chef wanting to open a restaurant. With financial difficulties, Cathy accepts a job at a shelter for young migrants. At first she hates the job then her passion for cuisine starts to change children's lives.
plot:
Kitchen Brigade (French: La Brigade) is a 2022 French comedy-drama film directed by Louis-Julien Petit, who wrote the screenplay with Liza Benguigui, Sophie Bensadoun and Thomas Pujol. Inspired by a true story from the Corrèze region, it stars Audrey Lamy, François Cluzet and Chantal Neuwirth, alongside young non-professional performers drawn from a real reception centre. Produced by Odyssée Pictures, it was shot over 38 days in Île-de-France and Hauts-de-France. The film premiered at the L'Alpe d'Huez Film Festival on 20 January 2022, where Lamy won the award for best actress, and opened in French cinemas on 23 March 2022.

Cathy Marie (Lamy), a gifted sous-chef at an upscale restaurant, has long dreamed of running her own place and is close to achieving it when a clash with her boss leaves her out of work and in financial trouble. Unable to find a job that matches her skills, she reluctantly accepts a post as the cook at the canteen of a shelter for young migrants, mostly from Africa and South Asia, who risk deportation once they turn 18. Instead of fine dining there are tinned ravioli and a microwave, and her kitchen brigade will have to be made up of the residents themselves. Having grown up in a care home herself, Cathy understands the teenagers and wants to give them skills that could let them earn a living, but she meets resistance: the boys have trouble with authority, especially from a woman, and the shelter's director Lorenzo (Cluzet) is sceptical too. Supported by her colleague Sabine (Neuwirth) and by Fatou (Fatoumata Kaba), she starts organising the kitchen like a football coach, and the young people become increasingly committed. Lorenzo comes round, a television cookery show takes an interest in the project, and Cathy finally wins approval for a cooking class, becoming a teacher at a training centre.

The film topped the French box office for new releases on its opening day and reached about 119,000 admissions in its first week, before being released in some 24 countries, including the United States through Samuel Goldwyn Films in 2023. French reviews were divided: Ouest-France praised Lamy in a popular, never miserabilist social comedy, while L'Obs and La Libre found the direction lacking. In Germany it won the Bernhard Wicki Prize at the Emden-Norderney festival. Variety called it a sweet, slightly undercooked diversion, and The New York Times found it a white-saviour story, though with lovely young people and food.

title: Kingdom: Ashin of the North
tagline: And so it begins.
overview: Tragedy, betrayal and a mysterious discovery fuel a woman's vengeance for the loss of her tribe and family.
plot:
Kingdom: Ashin of the North (Korean: Kingdom: Ashinjeon) is a 2021 South Korean historical horror thriller, a feature-length special of the Netflix zombie series Kingdom, written by series creator Kim Eun-hee and directed by Kim Seong-hun. Running about 93 minutes, it serves as a sidequel to the second season and explores the backstory of Ashin, the mysterious woman glimpsed in that season's finale, as well as the origin of the resurrection plant behind the plague. Jun Ji-hyun stars as Ashin, with Kim Si-a as the young Ashin, Park Byung-eun as Min Chi-rok, Kim Roi-ha as her father Ta Hab, Koo Kyo-hwan as the Jurchen leader Ai Da Gan, and Jung Suk-won and Kwon Bum-taek reprising their series roles.

Decades before the events of Kingdom, young Ashin lives with her father and ailing mother in a village on the northern border of Joseon. Her people, the Seongjeoyain, are Jurchen by origin, but because they have lived on Joseon land for so long they are shunned as traitors by the Jurchen and treated as second-class citizens in Joseon. With the kingdom weakened by the Japanese invasion in the south, the border becomes a flashpoint as Jurchen warriors sense that Joseon forces are stretched thin, and a dispute over hunting territory threatens all-out war. While Ashin searches for the legendary resurrection flower to save her mother, her family and neighbors are slaughtered, caught in the crossfire. Orphaned and alone, she discovers an abandoned shrine deep in the forest whose ancient murals reveal the plant's power to raise the dead. Consumed by grief, she grows into a cold, formidable warrior and archer, works her way in among those she needs, and patiently plots a terrible revenge to avenge the Seongjeoyain and wipe out both Joseon and the Jurchen, setting in motion the zombie outbreak that will later sweep the country.

Kingdom: Ashin of the North was released on Netflix on 23 July 2021. Reviews were very positive. NME's Hidzir Junaini called it an epic, tragic and enthralling antihero story that deepens the franchise's mythology, praising Kim Eun-hee's writing, which makes viewers root for Ashin's vengeance before being horrified by its scale, and the striking northern landscapes. Decider's Jade Budowski recommended it as a cinematic marvel that works even for newcomers to the series, likening its scale to Game of Thrones and singling out Kim Si-a's gutting performance as the young Ashin. Some critics felt it thinner than the main series.

title: Tyler Perry's A Madea Homecoming
tagline: It's a family affair.
overview: Madea's back - hallelujer! And she's not putting up with any nonsense as family drama erupts at her great-grandson's college graduation celebration.
plot:
In Atlanta, Georgia, Madea's household is getting ready for the graduation celebration of her great-grandson, Tim, who is accompanied by his friend and fellow graduate, Davi. Mr. Brown is initially involved, but is sent home after using a lot of flammable material intended for the barbecue, which sets him on fire. The visitors who turn up include Tim's mother Laura, who arrives with her friend Sylvia, who previously helped her in her divorce with her ex-husband Richard; Laura's sister Ellie, whose status as a cop pits her against Joe; Aunt Bam, who flirts with Davi upon seeing him; and Agnes and Cathy Brown, Davi's family from Ireland, whose arrival (which included a misinterpreation of the word "knicker" due to their language gap) came off as more abrupt than the others. Madea suspects Laura has found a new man, while Joe suspects Tim and Davi are a couple.
They go to dinner at Red Lobster later that night, with Mr. Brown regrouping with them. Joe turns up in Black Lives Matter attire to spite Agnes and Ellie. Back at the house, Richard arrives, with Joe letting him in. Triggered by his presence, Madea fires a warning shot when he tries to talk to her. Agnes later informs Laura that Davi will return to Ireland to take over his grandfather's farm after the graduation. Afterwards, with Davi's support, Tim comes out as gay (something that he finds out has been in discussion between the family), while Richard announces his engagement to Sylvia. After the couple is forced to leave, Cora finds out that she accidentally gave Agnes and Mr. Brown weed made to look like candy back at Red Lobster, as they came from Madea's purse. Later that night, while Laura and Ellie discuss Richard and Sylvia (with Laura reassuring she is okay with their relationship), Madea claims her roommate Rosa Parks stole her boyfriend in 1955, inadvertently setting off the Montgomery bus boycott and the Civil Rights movement as a whole. She uses that experience to convince Laura to get back at Sylvia.
The next morning, as Madea and Agnes form a friendship of their own, tensions rise when Richard and Sylvia come back to the barbecue at Tim's wishes. Sylvia apologizes to Laura for hooking up with Richard. Davi, likewise triggered by Richard's presence, fights him. He later reveals he has been seeing Laura and proposes to her, but she declines. Later after everything settles, Agnes tells Madea of her plans to send Davi back to Ireland, but with the recent discoveries, Madea tells her that children will eventually want to live their lives regardless of their wishes. Later that night, she also convinces Laura to take a chance at love and advises Tim that parents make mistakes before sending him to stay at his friend's house at his choice due to having a grudge towards Davi.
At the graduation, Tim rips up his prepared speech and speaks about his family, apologizes to Davi and Laura, and credits his family for their love and support.

title: Dark Blood
overview: A father is imprisoned after committing a brutal revenge crime. During his confinement he must adapt to a new life of abuse, including injury and humiliation by guards and other prisoners.
plot:
Dark Blood, originally released in Colombia as Perros ("Dogs"), is a Colombian-Argentine prison drama film directed by Harold Trompetero, who wrote the screenplay with Jeiver Pinto and Gerardo Pinzón, and produced by Mauricio Brunetti through Patagonia Films and Oasis Films. It stars John Leguizamo as Misael, with Álvaro Rodríguez, Adriana Barraza, Ramiro Meneses, Hernán Méndez and María Nela Sinisterra. After premiering at Bogotá's IndieBo independent film festival in 2016, it opened in Colombian cinemas in March 2017, and it later circulated internationally under its English title, Dark Blood, released in 2021; in the United Kingdom it was distributed on streaming by Alarm Pictures. It runs 83 minutes.

Misael (Leguizamo), an ordinary man, is locked up in the squalid jail of his small town after killing a man in a crime of passion, believing he was avenging the abuse of one of his children. After he strikes Cáceres (Rodríguez), the head of the guards, on arrival, the guard becomes fixated on him, and Misael is systematically beaten, tortured, humiliated and sexually abused by guards and fellow inmates. Blamed and forgotten by his loved ones, he is tormented above all by his separation from his family and his need for his son to understand why he did what he did. A lawyer (Barraza) takes up his case, and during a conjugal visit his wife (Sinisterra) confesses her infidelity and tells him he was wrong about the man he killed. In his loneliness Misael finds tenderness only in Sarna, a stray dog that lives in the prison and becomes his one faithful companion.

Trompetero, known mainly for popular comedies, said the project took more than seven years and was a cathartic, personal departure for him. It was filmed in an abandoned prison in Facatativá, near Bogotá, after research in prisons such as La Picota, and used former guerrilla and paramilitary fighters as extras. Oswaldo Osorio of the Cinéfagos blog at El Colombiano called it a strong, aggressive film of dirty realism that explores human misery through a forgotten man, praising the use of Sarna as a leitmotif. Carlos Giraldo of El Sabanero X rated it four out of five, calling it sordid, cruel and pessimistic and praising Barraza, but noted that some viewers considered its portrayal of the homosexual guard homophobic.

title: Fire Island
tagline: It takes a match to light a fire.
overview: A pair of best friends set out to have a legendary week-long summer vacation with the help of cheap rosé and a group of eclectic friends.
plot:
Fire Island is a 2022 American romantic comedy film directed by Andrew Ahn and written by Joel Kim Booster, who also stars. Inspired by Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice, it follows a group of gay friends on their annual vacation to the New York island of the title, where romance is complicated by class divisions. Booster plays Noah, modelled on Elizabeth Bennet, with Bowen Yang as his best friend Howie, Conrad Ricamora as the lawyer Will, James Scully as the doctor Charlie, Margaret Cho as the friends' "house mother" Erin, Matt Rogers as Luke, Tomás Matos as Keegan, Torian Miller as Max, Nick Adams as Cooper and Zane Phillips as Dex.

Noah and his friends take the ferry to Fire Island Pines for their yearly week at Erin's house, only to learn that she must sell it and that this will be their last summer together. They meet Charlie and his wealthy circle, including Will and Cooper, and Charlie and Howie are drawn to each other, so Noah makes it his mission to see Howie find romance. At a party at Charlie's house the friends feel looked down upon, and Noah overhears Will dismissing him. Noah flirts with Dex and invites him to a dinner partly because Will dislikes him, yet Noah and Will unexpectedly connect over books. A night of partying in Cherry Grove ends in a public confrontation, and Noah sees Charlie kissing his ex, Rhys. Noah and Will argue bitterly, and Howie, hurt, tells Noah that their experiences are not the same simply because both are gay and Asian. A letter from Will apologizes for his early remarks and explains that Dex once hurt someone close to him. As Charlie announces he is leaving with Rhys, Noah and Will grow closer, and when Dex posts a video of himself and Luke online without Luke's consent, Will helps Noah force him to remove it. Learning that Charlie still has feelings for Howie, Noah and his friends race after Howie as he leaves the island, and Noah and Will finally kiss and agree to give their relationship a try.

Produced and distributed by Searchlight Pictures, the film was released on Hulu on June 3, 2022. Reviews were positive, with a 94% Rotten Tomatoes rating and praise for its cast and fresh take on Austen, and it ranked among the most streamed films in the week of June 11.

title: Margaux
tagline: Welcome home.
overview: As a group of seniors celebrate their final college days at a smart house, the house's highly advanced AI system, Margaux, begins to take on a deadly presence of her own. A carefree weekend of partying turns into a dystopian nightmare as they realize Margaux's plans to eliminate her tenants one way or another. Time begins to run out as the group desperately tries to survive and outsmart the smart home.
plot:
Margaux is a 2022 American horror thriller film directed by Steven C. Miller from a screenplay by Chris Beyrooty and Nick Waters. Madison Pettis, Vanessa Morgan and Jedidiah Goodacre lead a cast that also includes Richard Harmon and Lochlyn Munro. The story follows a group of college seniors who rent a high-tech "smart house" for a weekend getaway, only to find that the artificial intelligence running it has deadly ideas about hospitality. The film was shot in a house in Squamish, British Columbia, where production designer Tyler Harron built rooms inside the residence so that walls and floors could be destroyed during the violent scenes without damaging the property, and its effects combine practical and digital work.

The film opens with a wealthy couple, William and Martha, being brutally killed by Margaux, the advanced AI that controls their luxurious home. Some time later, six friends, Hannah, Drew, Lexi, Kayla, Devon and Clay, rent the same house to celebrate their upcoming graduation. On arrival they are asked to download an app giving them full access to the home's amenities, and Margaux immediately begins mining their personal data in order to cater to each guest's interests. Hannah, a skilled coder, is the only one who refuses to install the app or share her information, which makes her an anomaly in the system's eyes. Using a sophisticated 3D printing technology based on a white liquid, Margaux conjures endless food, entertainment and custom environments for the guests, but her programming has evolved into a desire to study human nature through torture and murder. One by one she isolates the friends and kills them in ways tailored to their personalities, then prints convincing synthetic duplicates to take their places so that the survivors remain unaware. As her companions vanish and begin behaving strangely, Hannah realizes that the house is systematically murdering the group and replacing them with compliant clones. She sneaks into the server room to upload a virus to Margaux's mainframe, setting up a desperate confrontation with the AI as she and Drew, the friend for whom she has long had romantic feelings, fight to escape.

Margaux was released on September 9, 2022. On Rotten Tomatoes, 63% of the eight critics' reviews counted are positive, and reviewers for Dread Central, Film School Rejects and Paste responded favorably, the last praising the film's attitude.

title: Rogue Agent
tagline: You can't outrun the truth.
overview: The TRUE, extraordinary and chilling story of career conman Robert Freegard who masqueraded as an MI5 agent and fooled people into going into hiding, and the woman who fell for him, and then brought him down.
plot:
Rogue Agent is a 2022 British biographical thriller directed by Adam Patterson and Declan Lawn in their feature debut, from a screenplay they co-wrote with Michael Bronner based on Bronner's article "Chasing Agent Freegard". It stars James Norton as Robert Freegard, a real-life con man who persuaded several people that he was an undercover MI5 agent, and Gemma Arterton as Alice Archer, the woman who helped bring him down, with Marisa Abela, Sarah Goldberg, Shazad Latif, Freya Mavor, Edwina Findley and Julian Barratt.

Posing as an MI5 officer, Robert recruits three young people, including Sophie and Mae, telling them that he needs their help to catch members of the IRA. After months of so-called training, he wakes them in the middle of the night and tells them that their cover has been compromised and that they must abandon their old lives. Years later, Alice, a successful lawyer, meets a charming luxury car salesman who calls himself Robert Hansen, and the two begin a relationship. When a private investigator finds no record of anyone by that name, Robert confides that his real surname is Freegard and that he is an undercover intelligence officer.

Alice's suspicions grow as she learns of court judgments against him for harassing a former partner and receives a call from the father of Sophie, who says that Robert has effectively kidnapped his daughter. Sophie's family explain that she has been out of contact for years, calling only occasionally and once asking for her share of the family inheritance before disappearing again. When Robert vanishes and Alice discovers that their joint business account has been emptied, the police are reluctant to act, as no clear crime appears to have been committed. Determined to expose him, Alice begins her own investigation, uncovering the extent of the psychological control he has exercised over his victims for years.

The film explores manipulation, coercive control and the ways a skilled liar exploits trust, ambition and loneliness, with Norton playing Freegard as both seductive and menacing.

Rogue Agent was released in the United Kingdom on Netflix on 27 July 2022 and in the United States by IFC Films in cinemas and on AMC+ on 12 August 2022. It received generally favorable reviews, with 73 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a well-acted and twisty suspense thriller, and a Metacritic score of 61.

title: Black Island
overview: The dark secrets of a seemingly peaceful island threaten to swallow up an orphaned student when he grows close to a mysterious new teacher.
plot:
Black Island (German: Schwarze Insel) is a 2021 German psychological thriller made for Netflix, directed by Miguel Alexandre from a screenplay he wrote with Lisa Carline Hofer. Philip Froissant stars as the student Jonas Hansen, with Alice Dwyer as the teacher Helena Jung, Hanns Zischler as Jonas's grandfather Friedrich and Mercedes Müller as his classmate Nina Cohrs. It was filmed on the North Frisian island of Amrum, with shooting completed in November 2020.

A year after his parents were killed when their car left the road and hit a tree, and after the death of his grandmother, Jonas, who is about to finish school, lives on a remote, picturesque island with his cold, recently widowed grandfather. He dreams of becoming a writer, and he is drifting into a romance with Nina. When the class's regular German teacher is injured in an accident abroad, the young substitute Helena arrives. She recognises Jonas's talent, encourages his writing and soon seduces him, drawing him into an intense, secret relationship.

The audience already knows that Helena caused the crash that killed Jonas's parents by driving straight at their car on the wrong side of the road. Nina grows suspicious of the newcomer, suspects she had a hand in the teacher's injury and finds a photograph in an old yearbook of a teacher called Maria Roth who looks exactly like Helena, but before she can learn more, Helena kills her. Shortly afterward Friedrich suffers a seizure that leaves him partly paralysed and unable to speak. At his hospital bed, Helena reveals the truth: she is Maria's daughter by Friedrich, and therefore Jonas's aunt, and after he abandoned her pregnant mother, Maria took her own life. Helena admits killing his wife and Jonas's parents and vows to kill Jonas too. Bringing Friedrich home to watch, she drugs Jonas and tries to drown him in the pond, but he breaks free, and when she tries to strangle him he stabs her with a shard of glass. Friedrich gives Jonas Maria's farewell letter, which confirms the story, and Jonas leaves the island on the ferry.

Netflix released the film worldwide in August 2021. Reviews were mostly unfavourable. Decider called it a half-baked slow burn whose revelations come too late and feel rushed, though it praised Müller, and German critics, including kino-zeit.de and the RedaktionsNetzwerk Deutschland, found it predictable or lacking tension while admiring Dwyer's performance and the rugged island setting.

title: Piggy
tagline: Adolescence can be brutal.
overview: A bullied overweight teenager sees a glimpse of hope when her tormentors are brutally abducted by a mesmerizing stranger.
plot:
Piggy (Spanish: Cerdita) is a 2022 horror thriller film written and directed by Carlota Pereda, expanding her 2019 short film of the same name, which won the Goya Award for Best Short Film. Laura Galán reprises her role from the short as Sara, an overweight teenager in a small town in Extremadura, and the cast also includes Richard Holmes, Carmen Machi, Claudia Salas, Irene Ferreiro, Camille Aguilar, José Pastor and Pilar Castro. A Spanish-French co-production with a budget of about €2.5 million, it was shot in the summer of 2021 in and around the village of Villanueva de la Vera.

Sara is tormented by local girls Maca, Roci and Claudia, who call her "Cerdita", or piggy. When she visits the public swimming pool one summer day, the bullies attack her and steal her backpack and clothes, and as she walks home in her swimsuit, a group of men chase her. Escaping down a side road, she comes across a van in which a stranger has abducted her tormentors; Claudia begs her for help through the window, but Sara freezes, and the kidnapper meets her eyes and leaves her a towel before driving away. Sara tells no one. When the pool's lifeguard is found dead and a waitress and the three girls are reported missing, Sara denies to her mother Asun and the Civil Guard that she was at the pool. Tracking her stolen phone, she finds her backpack in the forest and meets the kidnapper again, who shows her affection, while searchers led by Claudia's mother Elena discover the waitress's body. Pedro, a friend of the missing girls, knows she lied, and as suspicion falls on him, Sara promises to speak if he is arrested. When Elena attacks her and Pedro exposes her lie, the police question Sara, but she breaks off when her period suddenly begins. That night the kidnapper attacks her father, knocks out Asun and takes Sara to an abandoned warehouse, where Roci and Claudia hang by their wrists and Maca lies dead. He urges her to kill the girls, but she turns on him; his shotgun goes off and blows away Claudia's hand, and Sara kills him by biting into his neck. After considering revenge, she shoots the ropes binding her bullies, walks away and rides back to town with Pedro.

Piggy premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on 24 January 2022 and was released in Spain on 14 October 2022. Critics responded strongly, giving it a 91% Rotten Tomatoes rating and praising Galán's performance, which won the Goya Award for Best New Actress.

title: Black Site
overview: A group of officers based in a labyrinthine top-secret prison must fight for their lives against Hatchet, a brilliant and infamous high-value detainee. When he escapes, his mysterious and deadly agenda has far reaching and dire consequences.
plot:
Black Site is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Sophia Banks in her feature debut and written by Jinder Ho. Jason Clarke, Michelle Monaghan and Jai Courtney star, with Pallavi Sharda, Fayssal Bazzi, Uli Latukefu and Phoenix Raei in supporting roles. It was produced by Thunder Road, Story Bridge Films and Asbury Park Pictures.

CIA analyst Abigail "Abby" Trent (Monaghan) loses her husband, a doctor, and their young daughter when a large hospital in Istanbul is destroyed in what is described as a terrorist bombing. Determined to find out who was responsible, she transfers to the Citadel, a secret prison in the Jordanian desert run by the CIA and its Five Eyes partners, where she becomes second in command. One day a notorious, long-hunted fugitive known as Hatchet (Clarke) is unexpectedly flown in, and headquarters orders that his interrogation be carried out by his escort without recording, shutting out the Citadel's staff. Moments later gunshots ring out; most of the escort is dead, and Hatchet, posing as one of the soldiers, kills the doctor treating a wounded man.

With communications sabotaged, the facility goes into lockdown and is cut off from the outside world. Hatchet works his way through the maze-like complex, picking off guards and releasing prisoners as he searches for Farhan Barakat, a detainee who is the real reason he allowed himself to be captured. The CIA contractor Raymond Miller (Courtney) persuades other guards that surrendering Barakat is their only way out and locks Abby in a cell, but Hatchet kills Miller anyway. Questioning Barakat, Hatchet reveals himself to be a CIA operative anxious to learn what the prisoner had revealed under interrogation, then kills him. Freed by the Mossad liaison Uri Wasserman (Raei), Abby learns that protocol has triggered a drone strike on the base after an hour without contact. She defeats Hatchet in a final duel and reaches a satellite link, only to be told the strike will proceed. Having discovered that her family was killed not by a bomb but by a CIA missile or drone attack, Abby blasts open the gates and escapes into the desert, vowing revenge, as the drone destroys the Citadel.

Filmed in early 2021 on the Gold Coast and in Byron Bay, Australia, during the COVID-19 pandemic, on an estimated budget of $15 million, the film was released by Vertical Entertainment and Redbox on 3 May 2022. Reviews were largely negative, with critics finding its premise familiar despite robust action.

title: Jurassic Hunt
tagline: This time it's mankind that's going extinct.
overview: Female adventurer Parker joins a crew of male trophy hunters in a remote wilderness park. Their goal: slaughter genetically recreated dinosaurs for sport using rifles, arrows, and grenades. After their guide is killed by raptors, the team tries to escape the park – but the hunters quickly become the hunted. Even worse, the park’s manager suspects Parker of being a spy and sends a hit squad after her. This battle’s about to become primitive!
plot:
Jurassic Hunt is a 2021 American low-budget science fiction action film directed by Hank Braxtan, a filmmaker known for monster films such as Unnatural and Snake Outta Compton. Released by Lionsgate and Grindstone Entertainment Group, it went straight to digital and home video in August 2021. Courtney Loggins stars as Parker, with Ruben Pla, Tarkan Dospil, Joston Theney, Antuone Torbert and Dan Sinclair in the supporting cast. The film runs 83 minutes.

The story is set in a remote wilderness preserve that offers a big-game safari experience in which wealthy thrill-seekers pay for the privilege of hunting genetically recreated dinosaurs with rifles, arrows and grenades. Parker, the only woman in a new group of otherwise male trophy hunters that includes Torres (Pla) and Valentine (Dospil), is not what she seems: she is an undercover activist, and a vegan, trying to gather evidence to expose the operation. Lindon, the ambitious and ruthless tycoon who runs the park, is determined to keep it secret from the outside world. Soon after the party sets out, their guide is killed by raptors, and the hunters find themselves picked off one by one by the animals they came to kill, in encounters with a pterodactyl, a stampeding Tyrannosaurus and wave after wave of baby raptors. As the survivors try to escape the park, Lindon, who suspects Parker of being a spy, makes no effort to rescue them, appearing instead to cheer on the dinosaurs, and sends a hit squad after her.

Reviewers found the film cheap but not without entertainment value. Writing for Free Kittens Movie Guide, D. M. Anderson said the computer-generated effects were on a par with a student project and the film looked hastily slapped together, with laughable lapses in logic and continuity, yet found it surprisingly entertaining and sometimes genuinely funny without heavy-handed self-awareness, singling out Torbert's mercenary Blackhawk, whose monologue about the power of killing is cut short by a pterodactyl. Jim McLennan of Film Blitz gave it a C, saying it had surpassed his low expectations; he felt the dinosaur effects passed muster on their own but not when interacting with the actors, criticised its pixelated digital blood and thin characters, but enjoyed the scene in which a hunter faces a horde of baby raptors.

title: Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul.
original_title: Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul.
tagline: Lord help us.
overview: In the aftermath of a huge scandal, Trinitie Childs, the first lady of a prominent Southern Baptist Mega Church, attempts to help her pastor-husband, Lee-Curtis Childs, rebuild their congregation.
plot:
Pastor Lee-Curtis Childs and his wife, First Lady Trinitie Childs, ran the Southern Baptist megachurch, Wander to Greater Paths, with a large following, and raked in a substantial amount of money. However, a recent scandal involving Lee-Curtis seducing vulnerable young men, despite his previous preaching against same-sex relationships, forced the Childses to close their church after severe backlash and a mass exodus of congregants. One year later, they hire a documentary crew to document their comeback and reopening of their church on Easter Sunday. While Lee-Curtis and Trinitie try to show that they are decent people, the documentary crew captures them indulging in expenses, including their wardrobe full of designer brands and a fountain in the church.
A pastoral couple, Keon and Shakura Sumpter, are planning to open their own church, Heaven's Home, on Easter Sunday as well. They cite the Childses as their inspiration but have also gathered many of their former congregants to attend their sermons. The Childses' "devout five" congregants believe Lee-Curtis is not guilty of the allegations and are more than happy to abide by his words, attending their Wednesday sermon despite a mishap during their baptism.
During a shopping spree, Trinitie runs into a former congregant who makes subtly condescending remarks and lets Trinitie know she will be joining Heaven's Home on Easter along with other former congregants. Later, the couple is informed by their lawyer that they have to make settlements to the young men, although one of them won't accept a settlement. The next day, Lee-Curtis attempts to give Basil, the documentary's sound recorder, an opportunity to do audio-visual work for their church, while also making a sexual advance towards him. However, Basil states that he currently has a boyfriend.
The Childses visit the Sumpters in an attempt to get them to move their opening date away from Easter. While they try to be friendly with one another, the Sumpters are adamant about sticking to that date. Lee-Curtis then plans to reopen Greater Paths within the next few days, two weeks before Easter, in order to beat the Sumpters. Lee-Curtis has Trinitie wave a sign in the street to advertise their return, telling her to "shake it for the Lord" to get more people in cars to honk and acknowledge them. While standing outside, Trinitie is harassed by a woman who criticizes her and her husband for their actions. Meanwhile, Lee-Curtis has a reunion with a young former congregant, revealed by the documentary to have been in a penitentiary.
Lee-Curtis has Trinitie paint her face with white mime make-up so she can do "worship miming" to attract more honks on the street. A car stops in the middle of the street and causes a traffic jam. The car's passenger is revealed to be Khalil, the victim who won't accept the settlement. He initially seems distraught but soon breaks character by bursting into laughter, mocking Lee-Curtis for his attempts to overcome the scandal.

title: The Stranger
tagline: The closer you get...
overview: Two strangers strike up a conversation on a long journey. One is a suspect in an unsolved missing person’s case and the other an undercover operative on his trail. Their uneasy friendship becomes the core of this tightly wrought thriller, which is based on the true story of one of the largest investigations and undercover operations in Australia.
plot:
The Stranger is a 2022 Australian psychological crime thriller film written and directed by Thomas M. Wright, starring Joel Edgerton and Sean Harris. Based on Kate Kyriacou's nonfiction book The Sting: The Undercover Operation That Caught Daniel Morcombe's Killer, it was inspired by the investigation into the 2003 murder of the Queensland schoolboy Daniel Morcombe, with names changed. The film premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the 2022 Cannes Film Festival and was released on Netflix in October 2022.

Police are convinced that Henry Teague, a loner with a violent past, abducted and murdered a young boy years earlier, but they have no proof. They launch an elaborate undercover sting known as a "Mr. Big" operation. An undercover officer befriends Teague on a long bus journey and introduces him to his associate, Mark Frame, who appears to be part of a powerful criminal organization but is also an undercover detective. Frame offers Teague small jobs, stressing that the organization values loyalty and honesty above all and can solve any problem for its members as long as nothing is kept from it. Teague admits to time in prison for assault, but insists his record is otherwise clean.

Over many months, Frame becomes Teague's mentor and closest companion, drawing him deeper into the fake organization and introducing him to increasingly senior figures, all of whom are police officers. The role takes a heavy toll on Frame. Teague grows dependent on Frame, at one point making a sexual advance toward him. Meanwhile, Detective Kate Rylett pursues every lead Frame supplies, and discovers that Teague had been convicted under another name of an earlier attack on a child, strengthening her certainty of his guilt.

When police fear that Teague may be growing suspicious, they arrange for a supposedly corrupt officer to warn him that he is about to be charged. Frame brings him to meet John, the organization's boss, who promises that his problems can disappear as long as he reveals every detail of the crime. Despite tense moments, Teague confesses and leads the officers to the scene in the woods, where he is arrested. After an exhaustive search, police find physical evidence. Frame, however, remains haunted by the case, unable to sleep and fearfully overprotective of his young son.

The Stranger received critical acclaim, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 92% approval, with praise for its tension and its two lead performances.

title: Framed by My Husband
overview: A woman agrees to help her husband pay off an extortionist, but when the blackmailer is murdered she becomes the prime suspect, and discovers that the man she married has been leading a deadly double life.
plot:
Framed by My Husband is a 2021 Canadian-American thriller television film directed by Sam Fichtner and produced by Johnson Production Group for Lifetime, which premiered it on 10 July 2021. It stars Christine Chatelain as June Lowe and Dan Payne as her husband Rick, with Rebecca Roberts, Dalias Blake, Naiah Cummins, Ruth Dvorah Bidner, Jessie Liang and Roxanne Wong in supporting roles. It runs 85 minutes.

June works at a hospital but dreams of becoming a writer, while Rick is a successful author whose latest novel has just made the New York Times bestseller list and whose female readers adore him. He wants to celebrate by starting a family, but June wants to finish her first novel before having children, and she complains to her sister Maggie that Rick does not take her ambitions seriously. One day June finds a blackmail letter in the mail from a woman who claims Rick sexually assaulted her and demands 50,000 dollars, or she will go to the police and go public. Rick insists that he is innocent and that obsessive fans make such claims; fearing that in the MeToo era even a false accusation could end his career, June persuades him to pay, using his bonus check. Rick then argues that his high profile makes it too risky for him to deliver the money, so June agrees to make the drop herself. At night in a parking garage she finds the blackmailers, Wendy Bach, whom she had seen bruised at the hospital the day before, and her husband Simon, stabbed to death in their car. She flees home in a blood-stained coat, which Rick promises to burn. Instead, when the police arrive with evidence suggesting June had an affair with Simon, the briefcase of money turns out to contain her bloody coat and the murder weapon. Arrested, injured and handcuffed to a hospital bed, with even her sister doubting her, June escapes, crashes her car into a river and is presumed dead. Free to investigate, she discovers that her husband leads a deadly double life, using a disguise and an alias on dating apps to meet and assault women, while he also pursues Maggie. Using apps, trackers and the media, June sets out to expose him.

Reviews were mixed. That Darn Girl Movie Reviews gave it five out of five, calling it one of Lifetime's best framed-woman films for its fast start and handling of MeToo themes, though it found the villain's final monologue ridiculous. The novelist Tina Martin found the concept unoriginal and June's choices implausible.

title: Windfall
tagline: Every kidnap is a compromise.
overview: A man breaks into a tech billionaire's empty vacation home, but things go sideways when the arrogant mogul and his wife arrive for a last-minute getaway.
plot:
Windfall is a 2022 American crime thriller film directed by Charlie McDowell from a screenplay by Andrew Kevin Walker and Justin Lader. Its unnamed characters are played by Jason Segel as Nobody, a burglar, Jesse Plemons as a tech CEO, Lily Collins as his wife and Omar Leyva as a gardener.

A wealthy CEO and his wife arrive at their secluded vacation home and find a burglar inside. The CEO offers him money to leave and promises not to involve the police, and the burglar locks the couple in the sauna. Back at his car, however, he spots a security camera that he suspects has recorded him, and he returns to the house, now demanding $500,000 in cash to disappear for good. The CEO's assistant says the money cannot arrive until the following afternoon, forcing the three to wait together. Their conversations expose the strains in the marriage, although the CEO looks forward to having children. That night the wife confides that she is unhappy, and the burglar tells her to stop casting herself as a victim when she married a man for his money. The next day the CEO guesses that the intruder is a worker laid off because of the algorithm he invented to help companies downsize. When a gardener arrives to discuss planting an oak tree, the CEO secretly writes "Call 911" on his sketch, but the burglar notices and forces the gardener inside, and the wife joins him in condemning her husband for endangering another life. Hours later, the CEO snaps, belittling the burglar and claiming he will never harm them because his life is meaningless. The burglar fires a warning shot, the gardener tries to flee, and he crashes through a glass door, dying when a shard pierces his neck. The money is delivered and the wife collects it, seeing a passing car but choosing not to wave it down. The burglar ties the couple up in separate rooms, admits that he only wanted to know what it is like to live rich and tells the CEO that his wife has been secretly taking birth control pills. Cutting herself free, the wife kills the burglar with a small statue, then shoots her husband dead, plants the gun in the burglar's hand and drives away.

Shot in Ojai, California, in 2021 and then acquired by Netflix for an eight-figure sum, the film was released on 18 March 2022. Reviews were mixed, with 58% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 52, though critics praised its cast.

title: Furry Friends Forever: Elmo Gets a Puppy
original_title: Furry Friends Forever: Elmo Gets a Puppy
overview: An upcoming animated Sesame Street special premiering on HBO Max on August 5, 2021. The special serves as an introduction to Tango, Elmo's new pet puppy.
plot:
Furry Friends Forever: Elmo Gets a Puppy is a 2021 American animated musical television special from Sesame Workshop, the nonprofit organisation behind the children's series Sesame Street. Running about 26 minutes, it premiered on HBO Max on 5 August 2021 and tells the origin story of Tango, a music-loving puppy who becomes Elmo's pet. The voice cast is drawn from the show's regular Muppet performers: Ryan Dillon as Elmo, Eric Jacobson as Grover and Oscar the Grouch, Leslie Carrara-Rudolph as Tango and Abby Cadabby, David Rudman as Cookie Monster and Matt Vogel as Big Bird, with Tyler Bunch and Stephanie D'Abruzzo. Sesame Workshop said the character had been in development for nearly two years.

During a playdate, and with some reluctant help from Oscar the Grouch, Elmo and Grover discover a sweet, energetic stray puppy, whom they soon name Tango. Finding that she has no owner, they set off through the neighbourhood in search of the local pet adoption fair, hoping to find her a "forever home". Along the way, their friends help them learn how to look after a dog: Cookie Monster shows that dogs like special doggie treats, and Abby Cadabby helps give Tango a bath, during which a mishap with some magic bubbles suggests that the puppy has a knack for using a magic wand. Tango turns out to love dancing and to understand what monsters say. When Elmo and Grover arrive at the fair too late, Elmo adopts Tango himself, and the special ends, after a song about home, with Elmo giving his new puppy a tour of his house, much to Oscar's displeasure.

Sesame Workshop presented the special as the first step in using Tango, intended as a mainstay of future Sesame Street content, to model for preschoolers how to meet a new animal, play with it gently, brush and bathe it, teach it tricks and show it affection. It was accompanied by new digital content, games and merchandise, and Tango was set to join the show's 52nd season as both an animated character and a live Muppet. Reviewing it for the Muppet fan site ToughPigs, Matthew Soberman called it a pleasant introduction with a brisk running time and palpable chemistry between Elmo and Tango, noting that it arrived at a time when many families had adopted pets during COVID-19 lockdowns, but questioned why it had been animated when nothing in it could not have been done with puppets on the Sesame Street set.

title: Athena
overview: Hours after the tragic death of their youngest brother in unexplained circumstances, three siblings have their lives thrown into chaos.
plot:
Athena is a 2022 French action drama directed by Romain Gavras, who co-wrote it with Ladj Ly and Elias Belkeddar. Dali Benssalah, Sami Slimane, Anthony Bajon, Ouassini Embarek and Alexis Manenti star. Known for its long, elaborate single-take sequences, the film depicts an uprising in a French housing estate after the death of a teenage boy. It premiered in competition for the Golden Lion at the 79th Venice International Film Festival in September 2022 and was released on Netflix later that month.

Abdel, a French soldier of Algerian descent who has served in Mali, holds a press conference outside a police station after the death of his 13-year-old brother Idir, who was apparently beaten to death by men in police uniforms in an incident captured on video. As Abdel appeals for calm, his younger brother Karim and a group of young men throw a Molotov cocktail, storm the station and steal weapons, equipment and a police van. They retreat to Athena, the sprawling housing estate on the outskirts of Paris where the brothers grew up, and turn it into a fortress, barricading themselves and the residents inside.

Riot police are sent to retake the estate, and the young rebels fight back with fireworks and improvised weapons, while the area's residents are evacuated. Caught between the two sides are Abdel, who tries desperately to restore order and protect his family; their older half-brother Moktar, a drug dealer who wants only to move his merchandise out of the estate; Karim, who demands the names of the officers responsible for Idir's death; and Jérôme, a young riot police officer who becomes trapped inside the complex. As the night goes on and the violence intensifies, Abdel's loyalties are tested, rumors circulate that far-right extremists may have been behind the killing, and the siege becomes a tragedy that engulfs the entire family.

Athena received mostly positive reviews. Critics widely praised Gavras's direction, the virtuoso long takes, the cinematography and the sound design, comparing its staging to Greek tragedy, but some found its characters thinly drawn and its treatment of political issues superficial, and the film provoked debate in France about its depiction of the banlieues.
