title: Accident Man: Hitman's Holiday
tagline: A vacation to die for.
overview: The Accident Man is back, and this time he must best the top assassins in the world to protect the ungrateful son of a mafia boss, save the life of his only friend and rekindle his relationship with his maniacal father figure.
plot:
Dealing with his guilt after being forced to kill his assassin coworkers, Mike Fallon moves to the island of Malta to decompress and get away from London, finding work as a hitman-for-hire in nearby countries and keeping martial artist Wong Siu-ling on his payroll to fight him at random times and keep his skills sharp. One night, Mike runs into his old friend Finicky Fred, who informs him that their former boss Big Ray lost his assassin's bar after Mike's vengeful rampage. Fred is also out of money because he gave a large sum to a woman with whom he fell in love online. Mike takes pity on Fred and allows him to stay in his house and assist him on hits. The two put together a secret headquarters to test out Fred's gadgets and plan jobs.
On Mike's advice, Fred rejects a contract put out on Dante Zuuzer, the spoiled heir to a Cosa Nostra organization that even Mike fears. After carrying out another hit, Mike and Fred are abducted and taken to meet with Mrs. Zuuzer, who asks Mike to hunt down and kill whoever took out the contract on Dante in exchange for sparing Fred's life; an attempted hit on Dante had been carried out using Mike's modus operandi. The Zuuzers release Mike, who encounters Big Ray in his local pub - Fred had sent a letter to Ray explaining their new business operation against Mike's advice. Ray vows revenge on Mike, revealing that he is in Malta for a job, and Mike deduces he was behind the attempt on Dante's life. Ray explains that the client has raised the bounty to €9 million and opened the contract to any takers, as well as hacked into the tracking device in Dante's watch to broadcast his location.
Mike resolves to protect Dante in order to keep Fred alive. Mike arrives at the karaoke bar where Dante sings, but Dante refuses to destroy his watch and swallows it. Freya du Preeze arrives first and kills Dante's team of bodyguards before Mike fights and kills her with a barbecue skewer. Mike then forces Dante to take a laxative in order to pass the watch, but the two are accosted by blood-drinking Yendi the Vampire, who Mike kills with his own machete. They travel to Mike's headquarters, hoping to keep Dante secure, where Mike meets Siu-ling. Mike fights Poco the Killer Clown and kills him with one of Fred's previously broken gadgets, while Siu-ling fights rival assassin Silas the Strangler and strangles him to death with a heavy chain. Dante manages to pass the watch before nearly being killed by swordsman Oyumi.
Mike challenges him to a hand-to-hand fight for Dante's life, but receives a beating before Big Ray arrives and kills Oyumi with a shotgun. Ray attempts to kill Dante, but Mike convinces him to stand down for Fred and destroy the tracking device. Mike, Ray, and Siu-ling transport Dante to Mrs. Zuuzer to exchange him for Fred; Mrs. Zuuzer orders Mike and Fred to leave the island, but Ray detonates an explosive that Fred had planted in Dante's suit, killing Dante and Mrs. Zuuzer and earning them the €9 million bounty.

title: Abandoned
tagline: In this house, you're never yourself. And never alone.
overview: After a young couple moves into a remote farmhouse with their infant son, the woman's struggles with postpartum psychosis begin to intensify... as the house reveals secrets of its own.
plot:
Abandoned is a 2022 American psychological horror film directed by Spencer Squire, in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Erik Patterson and Jessica Scott. Emma Roberts, who also produced, stars as a young mother struggling after giving birth, with John Gallagher Jr. as her husband and Michael Shannon as a neighbour with ties to the house, along with Paul Schneider and Kate Arrington. Vertical Entertainment released it on June 17, 2022.

Sara and Alex Davis move with their baby son Liam to a remote farmhouse in search of a new start. Alex, a veterinarian, is optimistic, but Sara is finding motherhood overwhelming and feels uneasy. The estate agent reveals that the house has stood empty for decades since a young woman named Anna Solomon killed her baby and her father before taking her own life, but Sara insists on buying it anyway. Left alone with Liam for long days, she feels disconnected from him, especially as he will not breastfeed, and the couple find a locked room that seems to have belonged to a child.

A neighbour, Chris Renner, offers to help with the property, and Sara learns that he is Anna's brother and grew up in the house under their violent father, Robert. Strange things begin to happen. Sara hears children playing behind a door hidden by a heavy wardrobe, belongings disappear, and she glimpses Anna and Robert. When Liam almost tumbles down the stairs while she is distracted by an apparition, a worried Alex brings in the psychiatrist Dr. Carver, who prescribes medication. Sara secretly refuses it, afraid it will keep her from bonding with her son.

Chris tells Sara about the abuse Anna suffered and warns her never to move the wardrobe. As Sara grows close to him, Alex becomes more anxious about her state of mind. Her visions intensify, and the ghost of Robert nearly drowns her in the bath. One night, after hearing screams and footsteps, she finds Liam missing and the sealed room open, filled with the vanished objects. Two ghostly boys appear, one carrying Liam, and accuse her of hurting her child; as one lifts a hatchet, the scene cuts to black.

The next morning Sara seems calm and content, cradling Liam, and family life returns to an unsettling normality, ending with Sara, now pregnant again, smiling on a swing. Critics were largely negative, giving it 16% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Snoopy Presents: For Auld Lang Syne
original_title: Snoopy Presents: For Auld Lang Syne
tagline: "No matter how bad things may seem, I can always rely on my friends."
overview: After finding out her grandmother won't be visiting for Christmas, Lucy decides to cheer herself up by throwing the ultimate New Year's Eve party. Meanwhile, Charlie Brown tries to fulfill one of his resolutions before the clock strikes midnight.
plot:
Snoopy Presents: For Auld Lang Syne is a 2021 American animated television special, the 46th Peanuts special and the first produced for Apple TV+, based on the characters created by Charles M. Schulz. Directed by Clay Kaytis, who co-wrote it with Alex Galatis and Scott Montgomery, it was the first new Peanuts holiday special in 18 years. The voice cast includes Etienne Kellici as Charlie Brown, Isabella Leo as Lucy and Wyatt White as Linus, with Terry McGurrin and Rob Tinkler.

In early December, Lucy van Pelt happily prepares for a visit from her beloved grandmother. Charlie Brown, meanwhile, struggles with his list of New Year's resolutions, failing at every one, until Lucy reduces it to two: build a snowman and do something even remotely creative. Snoopy welcomes a visit from his siblings, and his brother Spike, who has only a photograph of them as puppies, keeps trying to take a new family picture, but is thwarted by bad luck.

On Christmas Eve, Lucy learns that her grandmother will not be coming after all and begins to fear that she is unloved. To lift her spirits, she decides to throw a grand New Year's Eve party, renting an old abandoned theater with all the nickels Charlie Brown has paid her over the years for psychiatric advice. Charlie Brown is put in charge of decorations, and Snoopy and his siblings are hired as the band, though Spike leaves after his camera is destroyed. The party is a disaster: Lucy's strict rules bore everyone, and when she demands that Linus rescue it, he snaps that she has made the evening about herself instead of her friends. The guests drift away, and Charlie Brown accidentally brings down the decorations, failing his second resolution. Snoopy's siblings find Spike at the bus stop and make amends.

Linus visits Lucy in her bedroom to reassure her that he loves her no matter what, and Charlie Brown, having learned the reason for her unhappiness, arrives with all the guests to restart the countdown. This time the celebration pleases everyone, Snoopy's family finally gets its photo, and Lucy helps Charlie Brown achieve a resolution on the spot: being a good friend. The children sing "Auld Lang Syne," and later Lucy happily learns her grandmother will visit for her birthday.

The special premiered on Apple TV+ on December 10, 2021, and was well received, with critics praising its shift in focus to a vulnerable Lucy. It was nominated for Best Animated Special Production at the Annie Awards.

title: The Visitor
tagline: Where he goes, death follows.
overview: After a series of tragedies including the death of his father-in-law, Robert and his wife Maia leave their home in London to move back to her childhood home. But when Robert discovers an old portrait in the attic of a man who is his spitting image, he goes down a rabbit hole to discover the identity of this mysterious doppelganger known only as the visitor. It isn’t long until he realizes – where the visitor goes, death follows.
plot:
The Visitor is a 2022 American psychological horror film directed by Justin P. Lange from a screenplay by Adam Mason and Simon Boyes. Finn Jones stars as Robert Burrows, an Englishman who moves to the American South with his wife, Maia, played by Jessica McNamee, and the cast also includes Dane Rhodes as Joseph Ellis, Donna Biscoe as Margaret Delacroix and Thomas Francis Murphy as Maxwell Braun. It was produced for television through a deal between Blumhouse Television and Epix, with Jason Blum as an executive producer.

Robert, an affable, polite and somewhat oblivious Londoner, travels with Maia to her childhood home in a small Southern town, where the couple hope to settle down and start a family. When Maia takes him to a local bar in her old stomping ground, the residents gravitate toward him and greet him with unusual warmth, almost as though they have been waiting years for his arrival. Robert cannot tell whether the welcome is simply sentimental or hides a darker purpose.

More alarming is a discovery in the house: an old portrait, found in the attic, of a man sitting in an armchair who bears an uncanny resemblance to Robert. Disturbed by the likeness and by frightening dreams, including one in which a blind ghostly figure screams in his face, he sets out to learn the true identity of his mysterious doppelgänger. His search takes him down a frightening rabbit hole into the history of Maia's family and the town, with small clues scattered along the way, until he realizes that every family has its own terrifying secrets and uncovers how he is connected to the man in the painting.

The project was announced in October 2021 as part of Blumhouse Television and Epix's slate of television films. The film, which runs about 80 minutes, was released digitally in the United States by Epix and Paramount Home Entertainment on October 7, 2022. Reviews were largely negative, and the film holds a low rating on Rotten Tomatoes, where only a small minority of critics' reviews are positive. Andy Crump of Paste praised Jones as an unexpectedly believable everyman, as well as Lange's careful, sometimes painterly craftsmanship and an effectively staged early dream sequence, but felt that the screenplay arrived at a thuddingly routine destination and that the late revelation of the mystery was a letdown. Other critics similarly found it atmospheric but generic, relying on familiar small-town horror tropes and a twist that comes too late.

title: A Christmas Miracle for Daisy
overview: Whitney Alder owns interior design firm Marietta Designs, which she runs with her friend Andi in the small town of Marietta, Montana. Whitney is designing Santa’s float for the annual Marietta Christmas Parade when a potential job opportunity comes her way: the full redesign of a landmark home by Christmas Eve.
plot:
A Christmas Miracle for Daisy is a 2021 American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Mike Rohl from a teleplay by J.B. White, adapted from Jane Porter's 2015 novel of the same name, the fifth book in her Taming of the Sheenans series published by Tule. Produced by Brad Krevoy Television and the Motion Picture Corporation of America, with Jill Wagner among its executive producers, it stars Wagner and Nick Bateman, with Tegan Moss, Rubi Tupper, Joe Costa, Andrew Francis, Heather-Claire Nortey and Terence Kelly in supporting roles. Announced in October 2021 as part of GAC Family's Great American Christmas line-up, it premiered on the network on 11 December 2021 and was later distributed on Peacock. It runs 85 minutes.

Whitney Alder (Wagner) owns the interior design firm Marietta Designs, which she runs with her friend Andi (Moss) in the small town of Marietta, Montana. While she is designing Santa's float for the town's annual Christmas parade, a tempting opportunity arrives: the complete redesign of a landmark home, to be finished by Christmas Eve. Despite the tight deadline, Whitney and Andi take the job, only to discover that the house's new owner is Whitney's former boyfriend, Connor Sheenan (Bateman), who has moved to Marietta from Los Angeles with his bright-eyed young daughter, Daisy (Tupper). Connor never intended to become a family man, but when his goddaughter was orphaned he adopted her and committed himself to being a devoted single father. Working together in the house brings back a trove of forgotten memories for Whitney and Connor, while Daisy, whose greatest wish is for a mother to complete her family, decides that Whitney is the perfect candidate, leaving it to the season of miracles to bring the former couple a second chance.

Reviews from holiday-film writers were generally warm. Rissi JC of RissiWrites found the film charming, sweet and better than expected, with a fun spin on a familiar trope; she noted that its production values were not quite equal to those of rival networks and praised Wagner while being less convinced by her co-star. Christiana of My Movie Views gave it 7.5 out of 10, calling it an ordinary but enjoyable Christmas film. In Porter's novel the hero is media mogul Cormac Sheenan, and four-year-old Daisy befriends Marietta's seasonal Santa Claus, whom she believes to be the real one.

title: David and the Elves
overview: Christmas is drawing near, but it’s not a happy time for David. After moving to a big city, his parents have been bogged down with work and forgotten the meaning of Christmas. David decides to change that. Together with Albert the Elf, who escaped from the land of Santa to figure out what Christmas is all about, David sets off to Tatra Mountains, where his grandparents live, on a journey full of adventures.
plot:
David and the Elves (Polish: Dawid i Elfy) is a 2021 Polish Christmas fantasy comedy directed by Michał Rogalski from a screenplay by Mateusz Kuczewski and Marcin Baczyński. Cyprian Grabowski plays a young boy and Jakub Zając a runaway elf, with Anna Smołowik and Michał Czernecki as the boy's parents and Cezary Żak and Monika Krzywkowska as Santa and Mrs. Claus. The film was released worldwide on Netflix on December 6, 2021.

Young David Kosmala loves the Christmases he spends with his parents and grandparents in their home in the Tatra Mountains, surrounded by family traditions. A year later, however, the family has moved to Warsaw, where his parents Hania and Piotr are overwhelmed by their jobs and have little time for him or for the festive season, and David feels lonely in the big city.

At the North Pole, meanwhile, Albert, a popular and confident elf who is tired of his routine, runs away against Santa's wishes, convinced that the people of the human world will adore him and that the trip will restore his Christmas spirit. Reality turns out to be very different. Wandering through Warsaw, he meets David in a park and the two become friends. Albert's magic soon causes chaos: he shrinks a huge lorry into a toy, turns a Christmas tree into a drum kit and transforms the fake beard of David's father into a real one. David tries to explain the strange events to his parents, but only manages to confuse them by describing Albert as a thief.

Santa sets out to find the runaway and realises that the longer Albert stays among humans, the more his Christmas magic drains away, and that he will eventually turn into a toy. Unaware of the danger, Albert keeps using his powers to help his new friend. When his magic finally runs out, he decides to return to the North Pole, and David goes with him to help him find his way, while David's parents, joined by Santa and Mrs. Claus, search for the two.

Sheltering in a forest for the night, David falls asleep, and Albert turns into a toy, undoing all the magic he has worked. Heartbroken, David carries the toy to his grandparents' house in the mountains, where his parents and the Clauses catch up with him. His efforts to bring Albert back seem to fail, until he finds footprints in the snow and Albert reappears behind him. Albert returns to the North Pole with the Clauses, and David's family rediscover the joy of spending Christmas together, singing carols with the elves. Common Sense Media rated it two out of five stars.

title: Grumpy Christmas
overview: Bitter, grumpy patriarch Don Servando and his family travel to spend Christmas with Doña Alicia, a relative who becomes his "ultimate nemesis". It may be Christmas, but Don Servando is set on proving to everyone that Doña Alicia is a terrible person.
plot:
Grumpy Christmas (Spanish: Una Navidad no tan padre) is a 2021 Mexican Christmas comedy film directed by Raúl Martínez and produced by Panorama Global. A sequel to Martínez's 2016 theatrical comedy Un padre no tan padre, it brings back Héctor Bonilla as the cantankerous grandfather Don Servando, alongside Benny Ibarra as his son Fran and Jacqueline Bracamontes as Fran's wife Alma, and adds Angélica María as Alma's aunt, Doña Alicia. The supporting cast includes Renata Notni as Gala, Juan Pablo de Santiago as Renato, Tina Romero, Eduardo Tanús as Memo, Tina French as Gina, Natália Subtil as Gio, Yulian Díaz as Joao and Alex Rose Wiesel.

Don Servando, known to the family as the grumpy grandfather, has become part of a larger and more unconventional household since the events of the first film: besides Fran and Alma, it includes a carefree commune of fun-loving hippies such as Gala, Renato and Bill. This year the whole group sets off on a trip to the beach to spend the holidays with Doña Alicia, a stubborn and demanding woman who quickly becomes Servando's ultimate nemesis. The two elders clash over how Christmas should be celebrated and over who really rules the family. Feeling that his position as patriarch is under threat, Servando stops at nothing to prove to everyone that Alicia is a terrible, self-centered person, even if it means ruining the holiday for all of them. Around their feud, the film weaves a series of smaller subplots involving the other relatives, and the sunny seaside setting replaces the usual snowy holiday backdrop, though snow does eventually make an appearance before the family rediscovers the spirit of unity.

Grumpy Christmas was released on Netflix on 21 December 2021, and was presented in Brazil as Natal, mas Pouco. Reviews were lukewarm. Writing for No es cine todo lo que reluce, David Pérez called the story pleasant but overly predictable and forced, judged the central conflict thin and the subplots unable to balance it, and felt the humor fell short of the first film, while praising the warm chemistry of the cast and the believable family relationships. He likened it to a Mexican take on The Family Stone and Meet the Parents, suitable for viewers who enjoy undemanding holiday comedies. The Brazilian site Tem Alguém Assistindo recommended it as a light watch for fans of Christmas films.

title: L.O.L. Surprise! The Movie
overview: Dazzling doll sisters Queen Bee and Royal Bee make their first movie with help from their fashionable friends in this one-of-a-kind magical adventure.
plot:
L.O.L. Surprise! The Movie is a 2021 American animated family film based on MGA Entertainment's L.O.L. Surprise! line of collectable fashion dolls. Directed by Alex Kamb and Lauren Ciaravalli from a script by Julia Prescott and animated by Pixel Zoo, it combines a live-action framing story with an animated doll world. The voice and live-action cast includes Ayla Rae Neal, Paris Anderson, Sonya Krueger, Ashley Angione, Tickwanya Jones, Sabrina Fest, Sarah J. Bartholomew, Tommi Rose, Frankie Kevich and Jessica Ruth Bell. The film was released on Netflix on 8 October 2021. Rated TV-G, it runs 47 minutes.

Ava (Neal), a young girl, is unhappy because she is packing up her room ahead of a move to a new home that she does not want. As she talks to her L.O.L. Surprise! dolls, light glints through a pair of 3-D glasses and floods the room with colour. When the curious girl puts the glasses on, she is transported into a digital world where her dolls come to life, and she herself becomes a baby doll named Queen Bee, the little sister of the glamorous star Royal Bee (Anderson). Royal Bee and her fashionable friends are making their first movie, which is due to premiere that same evening; with no fixed script, they shoot four different endings and plan to choose their favourite before the premiere. Queen Bee helps her big sister finish the film, taking on her own movie debut with the encouragement of the older dolls, while the crew, in roles ranging from director and actress to special-effects coordinator, faces a car chase filmed against a green screen and a spooky figure in the fog who turns out to be friendly. Through the experience Ava learns to be brave and to accept that change can be good, giving her the courage to face the move in the real world.

Critics writing for parents saw the film chiefly as a promotional vehicle. Common Sense Media rated it suitable for ages seven and up, crediting its predominantly female cast, its diverse range of dolls and its messages of teamwork and encouragement, but warning that these came wrapped in heavy branding for the toy line's dolls, accessories and toys, and that some characters wore short, revealing outfits. Kirsten Hawkes of Parent Previews gave it a C-, calling the animation poor and the script lazy and objecting that, beyond its overt lessons about courage, it suggested to young viewers that girl power came from clothes, cosmetics and celebrity.

title: Smile
tagline: Once you see it, it’s too late.
overview: After witnessing a bizarre, traumatic incident involving a patient, Dr. Rose Cotter starts experiencing frightening occurrences that she can't explain. As an overwhelming terror begins taking over her life, Rose must confront her troubling past in order to survive and escape her horrifying new reality.
plot:
Smile is a 2022 American supernatural horror film directed by Parker Finn and produced by Paramount Pictures.

The movie follows Dr. Rose Cotter (played by Sosie Bacon), a psychologist who returns to her hometown after the death of her mother, only to find herself dealing with a mysterious and terrifying phenomenon that seems to be connected to an antique dental mirror in her family's old house.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the mirror has a dark history and is somehow linked to Rose's own traumatic past. The mirror appears to be exerting some kind of malevolent influence over those who come into contact with it, causing them to smile uncontrollably and eventually succumb to madness and terror.

Rose soon discovers that she is not immune to the mirror's effects and must navigate a series of surreal and terrifying events as she tries to uncover the truth behind the mirror's power. Along the way, she teams up with her skeptical brother Trevor (played by Jessie T. Usher) and a local antique dealer who may hold some clues about the mirror's origins.

As the story builds towards its climax, Rose must confront her own dark past and the evil force that is driving her to madness. The film's climax features a shocking twist that reveals the true nature of the mirror and the source of its power.

Throughout the movie, Finn uses a range of clever visual effects and camera tricks to create a sense of unease and tension, making it clear that Smile is not just a horror movie but also a deeply unsettling exploration of trauma, grief, and the supernatural. The film's score, composed by Michael Abels, adds to the overall sense of dread and unease.

Overall, Smile is a tense and unsettling horror movie that explores themes of trauma, grief, and the supernatural in a unique and thought-provoking way.

title: You Won't Be Alone
tagline: It's a wicked thing this world.
overview: In an isolated mountain village in 19th century Macedonia, a young feral witch accidentally kills a peasant. She assumes the peasant's shape to see what life is like in her skin, igniting a deep seated curiosity to experience life inside the bodies of others.
plot:
In 19th-century Macedonia, Maria – a "Wolf-Eateress" (Macedonian: Волкојатка, romanized: Volkojatka), or witch, with a horrible burned appearance – enters the home of a newborn baby girl. The child's terrified mother Elica says that if Maria spares the girl's life, she will give her up once the girl is 16. Maria agrees, but robs the girl of her voice before leaving. Elica hides her daughter, Nevena, in a cave, and raises her there with no knowledge of the outside world.
On Nevena's 16th birthday Maria arrives in the form of an eagle; Elica chases the bird out of sight, where Maria kills her and takes her form before taking Nevena out of the cave. A witch can use a spell, only once in their entire lifetime, to make someone else a witch; Maria does so by killing a donkey, scratching Nevena's chest and spitting the donkey's blood onto her before burning her wound with fire. Now a witch, Nevena gains deadly retractable black talons on her fingers and palm. Maria then pulls Elica's guts from a hole in her chest, causing her to resume her previous, burned form.
Maria tries to teach Nevena to catch, kill, and eat animals, whose blood witches consume for power, and warns Nevena that humans will hurt her; but the younger witch refuses to feed, preferring to play with the creatures, which angers an abusive and disappointed Maria, who eventually abandons her to fend for herself. Nevena spies on Maria assuming the form of a wolf by putting its entrails into a cavity in her chest, understanding how to shapeshift as a witch. Now on her own, Nevena comes across a village, and accidentally kills a young mother, Bosilka, before using her entrails to take Bosilka's appearance and assume her life. While Nevena's muteness and clueless attitude causes the other villagers to think Bosilka has gone mad, she slowly learns how to live as a human: how to cook and wash, how to communicate non-verbally, and the differences in how men and women treat her. All the while, Maria watches from afar. One night, Bosilka's abusive husband tries to have sex with her. The unfamiliarity of the process, along with the rough nature of her husband, causes her to panic and kill him. She removes Bosilka's entrails from her chest cavity, reverts to her old self and flees.
Nevena assumes the shape of a dog and comes across a group of young men. She watches them bathe and notices how they look at women. She again reverts to her old self before luring one of them, Boris, away and killing him. Nevena then assumes Boris' shape. Now a man, Nevena learns to plow the fields and thresh in Boris' village, but still acts in a confused and childlike way. His peculiar behaviour attracts the attention of the women of the village, who believe him possessed and attempt an exorcism, which they believe is successful, but say that the Wolf-Eateress that bewitched him will one day come back and spirit him away. Again, Maria appears and warns Nevena that growing close to humans will not end well.

title: Fortress: Sniper's Eye
tagline: The war isn't over. It's just starting.
overview: Weeks after the deadly assault on Fortress Camp, Robert makes a daring rescue to save Sasha, the widow of his old nemesis Balzary. But back in the camp's command bunker, it appears Sasha may have devious plans of her own. As a new attack breaks out, Robert is confronted with a familiar face he thought he'd never see again…
plot:
Fortress: Sniper's Eye, also known as Fortress 2, is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Josh Sternfeld and a sequel to Fortress (2021). Jesse Metcalfe and Bruce Willis return as Paul Michaels and his father Robert, a retired CIA agent, with Chad Michael Murray as the villain Frederick Balzary. The supporting cast includes Natali Yura as Sasha, Kelly Greyson, Ser'Darius Blain, Natalie Burn and Michael Sirow. Lionsgate released the film on 29 April 2022.

The first film was set at Fortress, a secret resort for retired American intelligence officers built around a high-tech underground command bunker, which came under attack by Balzary and his mercenaries. A few weeks after that assault, the survivors are trying to recover and reassess their lives. Robert, who believes he killed Balzary, undertakes a risky mission to rescue Sasha, the woman presented as his old enemy's widow, and brings her back to the camp. He is wounded in the operation and spends much of his recovery in the infirmary.

Back at the Fortress, it soon becomes clear that Sasha is not the helpless victim she appeared to be and has plans of her own inside the camp's command center. When a new attack breaks out, the residents are taken hostage, and Robert is confronted with a face he thought he would never see again: Balzary is alive and determined to finish what he started. Robert and Paul, whose relationship has long been strained, must put their differences aside and work together with the other survivors to retake the bunker, protect their friends and stop Balzary and Sasha before their scheme succeeds.

The film was received very poorly. On Rotten Tomatoes, none of the seven critics' reviews collected were positive, with an average rating of 2 out of 10. Jeannette Catsoulis of The New York Times called it a sequel so dumb that no effort by Willis could reasonably be expected to save it, and noted that his character spends most of the film confined to a hospital bed. Leslie Felperin of The Guardian gave it two stars out of five. The film was released shortly after Willis's family announced in March 2022 that he was retiring from acting because of a diagnosis of aphasia, and several critics viewed his final low-budget films, released in the months that followed, with discomfort in light of his condition.

title: The Ambush
tagline: They will bring their brothers home by any means necessary.
overview: It is the winter of 2018, the men and women of the UAE military are deployed to provide aid. At the Mocha Base, spirits are high as three Emirati soldiers anticipate an imminent return home. While on their final routine patrol, the three soldiers, Ali, Bilal and Hindasi are ambushed by heavily armed militants on their route, through a narrow canyon. Trapped, wounded, and out of communication range, the three soldiers realize the gravity of their situation. They are running out of options, munitions - and time. Back at the base, their commander receives word and realizes that the assault on the UAE army patrol was premeditated. A rescue mission is quickly put into action, but will air and land support reach the men in time, and will they survive?
plot:
The Ambush (Arabic: Al Kameen) is a 2021 Emirati war action film directed by the French filmmaker Pierre Morel and written by Brandon and Kurtis Birtell. Based on a real incident during the Yemen war, it was produced by Image Nation Abu Dhabi and AGC Studios, with producers Derek Dauchy and Jennifer Roth and a score by Harry Gregson-Williams. The all-Emirati lead cast includes Marwan Abdulla Saleh, Khalifa Al Jassem, Mohammed Ahmed, Abdulla Saeed Bin Haider, Saeed Alharsh, Hassan Yousuf Alblooshi, Khalifa Albahri, Ghanim Nasser and Mansoor Alfeeli.

In the winter of 2018, soldiers of the UAE armed forces are deployed in Yemen, and at their base in Mocha morale is high, as three of them, Ali, Bilal and Al Hindasi, look forward to returning home soon. During what should be their last routine patrol, their vehicle is caught by heavily armed militants in a narrow mountain canyon. Wounded, trapped and out of radio contact, the three men realize how desperate their position is as they run short of options, ammunition and time. At the base, their commander learns of the attack and understands that the assault on the patrol was planned in advance. He quickly launches a rescue operation, sending another squad of Emirati soldiers with ground and air support into the valley in a race to reach the men before it is too late. The film also follows the families of some of the soldiers at home.

The production was described as the largest Arabic-language feature ever filmed in the Gulf Cooperation Council states, involving a cast and crew of around 400 and shot entirely in the United Arab Emirates, with a team of Emirati filmmakers and cultural consultants, including Hana Kazim, Talal Al Asmani, Alwiya Thani and Alia AlQemzi, working alongside the foreign crew.

The film had its world premiere at VOX Cinemas Yas Mall, attended by the cast and by the real soldiers whose story inspired it, and was released by VOX Distribution in the UAE on 25 November 2021. Its opening weekend drew 100,000 admissions, the fifth-largest opening of the year in the country, and within a week it had become the highest-grossing Emirati and Arabic-language film ever in the UAE, eventually earning more than $5 million worldwide. Morel described it as an inspirational story of brotherhood. In the United States, Well Go USA released it on Blu-ray; one reviewer praised the striking desert scenery but found the film thin, consisting almost entirely of combat.

title: Amina
tagline: She is Amina and she fears nobody.
overview: In 16th-century Zazzau, now Zaria, Nigeria, Amina must utilize her military skills and tactics to defend her family's kingdom. Based on a true story.
plot:
Amina is a 2021 Nigerian historical action drama directed by Izu Ojukwu, based on the life of Amina, the legendary warrior queen of Zazzau in the 16th century, a Hausa kingdom in what is now northern Nigeria, centered on the city of Zaria. Lucy Ameh stars in the title role, with Ali Nuhu, Clarion Chukwurah-Abiola, Chris Gbakann and Ibrahim Mijinyawa. The film premiered on Netflix on 4 November 2021.

The film opens with a duel between Kabarkai, the champion of Zazzau, and Danjuma. Having witnessed the fight, the young Amina tells her father, the ruler of Zazzau, that she wants to become a warrior. Her wish meets resistance from the Magaji, an important official, who points out that the armies of Zazzau have never recruited a woman. Determined, Amina trains in combat and horsemanship and gradually proves herself, defying the restrictions placed on women in her society.

The story follows the events that lead to Amina's rise to the throne of Zazzau. As a princess, she becomes involved in the political intrigues of the court and in the wars between Zazzau and its rivals, while her family faces betrayal from within. Her relationship with her sister Zaria, after whom the city is named, and a romance with Danjuma, a foreign prince, are threatened by the conflicts surrounding them. After suffering painful personal losses, including the death of her sister, Amina leads Zazzau's armies into battle and ultimately claims power, emerging as a formidable ruler who expands the kingdom's influence.

Amina received the most nominations at the 2022 Africa Magic Viewers' Choice Awards. Critics praised its costumes, music and battle scenes, but many faulted its plot, character development and underdeveloped romance. It was also criticized for being performed in Hausa with a non-Hausa lead actress, and for historical inaccuracies, such as its treatment of Amina's mother, Bakwa Turunku, who historians say had herself ruled Zazzau. Ojukwu responded that the scarcity of archives on Nigeria's history made the film difficult to produce.

title: Batman and Superman: Battle of the Super Sons
original_title: Batman and Superman: Battle of the Super Sons
tagline: The ultimate threat. The greatest battle. The perfect team.
overview: After discovering he has powers, 11-year-old Jonathan Kent and assassin-turned-Boy-Wonder Damian Wayne must join forces to rescue their fathers (Superman & Batman) and save the planet from the malevolent alien force known as Starro.
plot:
Batman and Superman: Battle of the Super Sons is a 2022 American animated superhero film released direct to video by Warner Bros. Animation. Based on the comic books of the same name, it is the 50th DC Universe Animated Original Movie and the first DC animated feature made entirely in CGI. Matt Peters directed from a screenplay by Jeremy Adams. Jack Dylan Grazer voices Jonathan Kent and Jack Griffo voices Damian Wayne, with Troy Baker as Batman, Travis Willingham as Superman and Laura Bailey as Lois Lane.

The prologue shows Krypton about to explode. Jor-El and Lara send their infant son Kal-El to Earth, unaware that Starro, an alien parasite that escaped from Jor-El's lab, has stowed away on the ship. Starro falls off during the journey. Kal-El grows up in Kansas as Clark Kent, becomes Superman and marries Lois Lane, and they have a son, Jon. Years later, Jon resents his father's constant absences without knowing that Clark is Superman. After a mysterious impact hits the Justice League Watchtower, Green Arrow is attacked aboard the station by a creature.

When Jon develops heat vision on his birthday, Clark tells him the truth and takes him to Gotham City to ask Batman for advice. There Jon meets Batman's arrogant son, Damian Wayne, who is Robin. Batman and Superman go up to the silent Watchtower, where a possessed Martian Manhunter infects them with Starro spores. Back in the Batcave, Damian destroys the spore meant for him and learns that Starro now controls the Justice League and the Teen Titans and is after Jon next.

Damian rescues Jon, and Jon's heat vision frees Lois. At the Fortress of Solitude, a hologram of Jor-El tells them that the spores answer to a central Starro on the Watchtower. The boys fly there in Kal-El's old ship and fight their possessed heroes, and Jon's invulnerability appears as he shields Damian from an arrow. When heat alone fails, they evacuate the heroes and send the station down to burn up on re-entry. This kills the spores, and the freed Superman catches the falling Watchtower. The two fathers and their sons then defeat Starro on the ground, and the boys call themselves the Super-Sons.

The film premiered at New York Comic Con on October 7, 2022, and came out on home video on October 18. Reviews were positive, and IGN said it was fairly predictable but captured the fun of the young heroes' friendship.

title: Last Shoot Out
tagline: His aim is unrivaled.
overview: Soon after a newlywed learns that her husband had her father shot down, she flees from the Callahan ranch in fear. She's rescued by a gunman who safeguards her at a remote outpost as he staves off her husband's attempts to reclaim his bride.
plot:
Last Shoot Out is a 2021 American Western film directed and produced by Michael Feifer from a screenplay by Lee Martin. A Milestone Studios production presented by Lionsgate and Grindstone Entertainment Group, it stars Brock Harris, Skylar Witte, Michael Welch, Cam Gigandet and Bruce Dern, with Peter Sherayko, David DeLuise, Jay Pickett, Brock Burnett and Larry Poole in supporting roles. Hank Baumert Jr. was the cinematographer, Ted Gianopulos edited the film, and the score was composed by Robert Arzola and Feifer. Lionsgate released it in select theatres and on digital rental on 3 December 2021, followed by DVD, Blu-ray and digital purchase on 7 December. It is rated PG-13 and runs 86 minutes.

Jocelyn (Witte), a small-town beauty whose father, the local lawman, has recently died, marries Jody Callahan (Welch), the dim-witted son of Blair Callahan (Dern), the snarling patriarch of a family of rustlers and killers. On their wedding night at the Callahan ranch she overhears Blair and his shrewder, deadlier son Sid (Gigandet) discussing the possibility that Sid may have to take Jody's place in the marriage bed, and referring to Sid's murder of her father, carried out to stop him from arresting Jody for killing a woman who had mocked him. Horrified, Jocelyn flees and meets two travellers headed for a remote stagecoach station: Red (Sherayko), a grizzled man hauling a wagon of supplies to the outpost, and Billy Tyson (Harris), a taciturn gunman. When Sid and his henchman Twigs (Pickett) arrive to take the runaway bride back, the quick-drawing Billy chooses to wound and disarm Sid rather than kill him, a mercy he comes to regret when Blair descends on the station with his sons and a band of hired guns, ordering them to leave no one alive, including the stranded stagecoach passengers and the station's operator, Joe (DeLuise).

Joe Leydon of Variety called it a small-budget indie aimed at the underserved audience for Westerns, noting echoes of Budd Boetticher's Ranown cycle and Ride the High Country. While slow-paced and padded with too many flashbacks, it was in his view a cut above recent streaming-ready Westerns and a marked improvement over Feifer's Catch the Bullet, with well-staged action and a ferociously nasty turn by Dern, recalling Walter Brennan's Old Man Clanton in My Darling Clementine, though Harris and Gigandet looked more like male models than gunslingers.

title: Slayers
tagline: Vengeance bites back.
overview: A group of superstar influencers are drawn to a reclusive billionaire's mansion only to find themselves trapped in the lair of an evil vampire. The only way out is to be saved by a famous online gamer and an old school vampire hunter.
plot:
Slayers is a 2022 American horror comedy written, produced and directed by K. Asher Levin. Thomas Jane stars as Elliot Jones, a former television personality, with Kara Hayward as Flynn Chambers, Jack Donnelly as her brother Jack, Lydia Hearst as Liz Andrews, Abigail Breslin as Jules Ray and Malin Åkerman as Beverly Rektor. The Avenue Entertainment released it on October 21, 2022.

Flynn, Jack, Liz and Jules make up the "stream team", a group of famous social-media influencers who have been invited to the estate of Stephen Rektor, a billionaire media mogul and pharmaceutical tycoon. Rektor and his family are secretly vampires. On the way to the mansion they encounter Elliot, once a TV personality, whose daughter was killed by a vampire. His warnings are dismissed as paranoia.

Once inside, the group is quickly split up. Their manager, David, is lured into a trap by Beverly Rektor and killed. Liz and Jack, who are a couple, are offered lucrative deals to promote a Rektor vaccine billed as making humanity immune to disease, which in reality is designed to purify human blood for vampires to feed on. Jules follows Harry Rektor to the stables for a date, where Flynn, who has sensed something is wrong, finds him attacking her. Jules is killed, but Elliot arrives and destroys Harry, and he and Flynn retreat to his camper, where he explains the history of the vampires.

Back at the mansion, Beverly injects Liz with a serum that turns her into a vampire, while Jack is drawn into a virtual-reality world where he meets Stephen, the vampire leader and Dark Lord. The Rektors achieve immortality not only by drinking blood but by transferring their blood and spirits into new hosts when their bodies wear out, and they have chosen Liz and Jack as their next vessels. Flynn and Elliot storm the house to save Jack, overcome the henchmen and confront Beverly, now inhabiting Liz's body, as she guards the unfinished transfer between Stephen and Jack. Stephen wakes before the process is complete, but the pair knock out both vampires. With no other known way to kill a Dark Lord, Elliot stays behind with a bomb while Flynn and Jack escape; a post-credits scene confirms that he destroyed the Rektors and their followers.

Announced in 2020 under the title With Teeth, the film was shot in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in November 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. Critics were unimpressed, giving it a 22% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Game of Love
overview: Follows Vivien and Roy as their love story continues and leads them to Roy’s childhood home in Sicily to prepare for the sale of the family estate. During the visit, a mysterious woman arrives and befriends Vivien, much to Roy’s displeasure. Tensions build and lines are crossed as secrets from Roy’s past force the couple to face aspects of their relationship they did not know existed.
plot:
Game of Love, released in some markets as Time Is Up 2, is a 2022 Italian English-language romantic drama film directed by Elisa Amoruso, who wrote the screenplay with Marco Borromei and Anita Rivaroli. A sequel to the 2021 film Time Is Up, it was produced by Lotus Production with RAI Cinema and distributed by 01 Distribution. Bella Thorne and Benjamin Mascolo return as the couple Vivien and Roy, joined by Alma Noce as Anna, Simone Coppo and Michael E. Rodgers. Martina Cocco was the cinematographer, and the film runs 91 minutes.

After a slow start, Vivien and Roy have become a happy couple, and they travel together to Sicily, where Roy grew up. The trip is not simply a nostalgic holiday: Roy has decided to sell his family's old house and estate, to pay for his studies. Soon after they arrive, Vivien meets Anna, a young woman who has fallen from her bicycle and hurt herself. The two quickly hit it off, and Vivien keeps inviting her new friend to join them, much to the displeasure of Roy, who is hostile towards her. Anna turns out to be linked to Roy's past and appears to still have feelings for him, and tensions build as lines are crossed and secrets from his past force the couple to confront parts of their relationship they had not known existed. Meanwhile Roy is offered a contract with a gallery that would let him realise his dream of exhibiting his photographs. After some hesitation about staying in Italy, Vivien chooses to support his ambition and the couple extend their stay, and once the tension over Anna eases they are able to continue their romance.

The film was released in October 2022 and became available on Amazon Prime Video, reaching German subscribers in July 2023. It was poorly received. Oliver Armknecht of Film-Rezensionen.de gave a strongly negative review, writing that while Sicily provided an attractive backdrop of countryside drives, grape harvests and old stone buildings, the story manufactured one contrived problem after another until it resembled an unintentional parody of a soap opera. He also found the mystery surrounding Anna and its resolution absurd, criticised Roy's persistent bad temper and argued that, although Thorne and Mascolo were a real-life couple who had been engaged, the two showed no chemistry on screen, so that the film never explained why the characters were together.

title: A Forbidden Orange
overview: Spain, 1970s. A Clockwork Orange, a film considered by critics and audiences as one of the best works in the history of cinema, directed by Stanley Kubrick and released in 1971, was banned by the strict Franco government. However, the film was finally premiered, without going through censorship, during the 20th edition of the Seminci, the Valladolid Film Festival, on April 24, 1975. How was this possible?
plot:
A Forbidden Orange (Spanish: La naranja prohibida) is a 2021 Spanish documentary film written and directed by Pedro González Bermúdez and produced for TCM España. Narrated by Malcolm McDowell, the star of Stanley Kubrick's A Clockwork Orange, it reconstructs how that film, banned under the Franco regime, received its Spanish premiere at the 20th Valladolid International Film Festival (Seminci) in April 1975, three and a half years after its release in the United States and Britain. Interviewees include Carmelo Romero, director of the festival in 1975, the writer and filmmaker Vicente Molina Foix, the novelist Gustavo Martín Garzo and Fernando Herrero. Made to mark the fiftieth anniversary of Kubrick's film by a director born in 1975, it opened the 66th Seminci on 23 October 2021 at the Teatro Carrión, the same venue that had hosted the 1975 public screening, and was released by TCM in December 2021.

The documentary explains that Warner Bros. had offered the film to the festival more than a year earlier with the approval of the regime's censorship board, at a time when the dictatorship was cautiously testing public reaction in controlled settings. A planned 1974 screening fell through when Kubrick asked for the print back, promising a better copy, and never returned it. Romero then persuaded Kubrick by assuring him that the film would be shown only at the University of Valladolid, a small lie, since it played in the festival's regular programme, though nearly all of the audience were students. The film recounts the enormous queues of young people, the scandal when the theatre owner handed out every ticket to his acquaintances before sale, forcing Romero to print new ones, and the divided reaction to the film's violence. It also records a screening of A Clockwork Orange for present-day university students, who agreed that such a film could not be made today, and Molina Foix's recollections of his relationship with Kubrick.

Reviews were mixed. Santiago Alverú of Cinemanía found it an entertaining anecdote with valuable details, especially from Molina Foix, but called it redundant, overloaded in tone and somewhat commissioned in flavour. Rosebud blog de cine rated it 6.5 out of 10, recommending it to anyone from Valladolid as a tribute to the festival and to freedom of expression, though it stayed on the surface and offered little new to those who know Kubrick's film.

title: The Long Dark Trail
tagline: They escaped from a nightmare just to enter into hell.
overview: After two impoverished teenage brothers manage to escape their abusive father, they embark on a treacherous and haunted journey in the hope of finding their estranged mother who has joined a sadistic cult, deep in the woods of Northwest Pennsylvania.
plot:
The Long Dark Trail is an American independent folk horror film written and directed by Kevin Ignatius and Nick Psinakis and produced by Four Eighteen Films. It stars the real-life brothers Carter and Brady O'Donnell as Henry and Jacob, with Michael Thyer as their abusive father Duane and Trina Campbell as their estranged mother, alongside Alex Hughes. Mitchell Kome was the cinematographer and Ignatius also composed the score, which ranges from Appalachian banjo to electronic music and closes with the vocal track "Hollow". The film runs 78 minutes and carries the tagline "They escaped from a nightmare just to enter into hell."

In the backwoods of northwest Pennsylvania, two impoverished teenage brothers have endured years of brutal abuse from their alcoholic father Duane, who once branded Henry with a clothes iron. In a tense prologue the boys tie Duane to a bed with cable ties and flee his cabin on BMX bikes. Acting on a tip from a customer of their gardening work, they head north across country in search of their mother, who left the family and has joined a sadistic cult deep in the forest, hoping she can give them a better life. Divided into chapters with one-word titles such as "Viaduct" and "Lake", their journey through vast woodland is punctuated by flashbacks to the horrors of home and by ominous signs: Jacob finds a mysterious rock marked with a sigil, an infection of pustules spreads across Henry's neck, and the boys pass what appears to be a burial ground. Intercut scenes hint at deadly rituals in the region, and as hallucinations take hold the brothers eventually discover what kind of company their mother keeps.

The film is dated 2021 in some listings and was released on digital, DVD and Blu-ray by Cleopatra Entertainment on 21 February 2023. Reviews praised its visuals more than its story. Phil Hoad of The Guardian called it an atmospheric, sharply directed fable despite its shoestring budget and minimal plot, while noting debts to Mandy and questioning the processed sound applied to the dialogue. Paul Lê of Bloody Disgusting found it uneven and incoherent but elevated by Kome's photography of the Allegheny landscape and Ignatius's music. Adam Mock of Film Inquiry was far harsher, faulting its slow pace, stilted performances and rushed finale.

title: What We Leave Behind
overview: At the age of 89, Julián Moreno takes one last bus ride to El Paso, Texas, to visit his daughters and their children – a lengthy trip he has made without fail every month for decades. After returning to rural Mexico, he quietly starts building a house in the empty lot next to his home. In the absence of his physical visits, can this new house bridge the distance between his loved ones?
plot:
What We Leave Behind is a 2022 Mexican-American documentary film directed by Iliana Sosa, who co-wrote it with editor Isidore Bethel. A Spanish-language portrait of Sosa's grandfather, Julián Moreno, filmed over several years, it was produced by Emma D. Miller and Sosa through Borderchild Productions and Marcona Media with JustFilms, and developed with support from the Sundance Institute, the IDA, the Austin Film Society and the Gotham Documentary Lab, among others. It premiered at South by Southwest in March 2022, received a theatrical release from Ava DuVernay's ARRAY, and debuted on Netflix in several English-speaking countries on 30 September 2022. It runs 71 minutes.

For about twenty years, Julián made a monthly 560-mile bus trip from his home in San Juan del Río, in the Mexican state of Durango, to El Paso, Texas, to visit his daughters and grandchildren, bringing candy and gifts and leaving after a day or two. As the film begins, he is 89 and making the last of these journeys. Widowed at 45 and the father of seven, some still in his hometown and some in the United States, he once worked as a bracero, a seasonal contract labourer in the US, and he shows his granddaughter his 1964 Alien Laborer's Identification Card. Back in rural Mexico he begins building a cinderblock house on the empty lot beside the small home he shares with his son Jorge, who is blind, and their dog Pinto, a project that, like his cross-border visits, is meant to keep the family close. In a conversation with Jorge, Sosa explores the death of her grandmother at 39 and its effect on the family, and the film visits her grave in the busy local cemetery. Lyrical interludes pair Sosa's voiceover with images of the surrounding landscape, while the soundtrack features an a cappella song by the Cardencheros de Sapioriz, also from Durango. Over the following years the film records Julián's growing frailty and his final days.

What We Leave Behind won the Fandor New Voices Award and the Louis Black "Lone Star" Award at SXSW and was nominated for Best Documentary at the Gotham Awards. It drew universal acclaim, with a Metacritic score of 89 and a perfect Rotten Tomatoes rating. Sheri Linden of The Hollywood Reporter called it first-person filmmaking at its eloquent best, the Boston Globe found it limpid and poetically resonant, and The New York Times named it a Critic's Pick.

title: Love Like the Falling Petals
overview: Haruto Asakura falls in love with hairdresser Misaki Ariake and asks her out. Watching Misaki Ariake work hard to achieve what she wants, Haruto Asakura, who almost gave up his dream to become a photographer, begins to pursue his dream again, but Misaki Ariake is diagnosed with a disease that ages her 10x faster than normal.
plot:
Love Like the Falling Petals (Japanese: 桜のような僕の恋人, Sakura no Yō na Boku no Koibito) is a 2022 Japanese romantic drama film directed by Yoshihiro Fukagawa and written by Tomoko Yoshida, based on Keisuke Uyama's 2017 novel of the same name. Kento Nakajima stars as Haruto Asakura, with Honoka Matsumoto as Misaki Ariake, Kento Nagayama as her older brother Takashi and Jun Kaname as her doctor. The film was released worldwide on Netflix on 24 March 2022.

Haruto, an aspiring photographer who has drifted away from his ambitions, goes for a haircut and is instantly smitten with the young hairdresser who cuts his hair, Misaki, who tells him that he is her very first customer. Wanting to impress her, he introduces himself as a professional photographer, stretching the truth. He keeps returning to the salon, and the two grow closer. When he finally tries to ask her out during a haircut, he moves his head and she accidentally nicks his earlobe, causing him to bleed and faint. Mortified, Misaki meets him to apologize and agrees to go out with him, despite the disapproval of her protective older brother.

On their first outing, to see the cherry blossoms, Haruto confesses that he is not really working as a photographer and does not know what to do with his life. Misaki is angered that he has given up on his dream so easily and urges him not to quit just because things are difficult. Taking her words to heart, he gets a job at a photo studio and works hard to become someone she can be proud of, and their relationship blossoms into a serious romance.

Their happiness is shattered when Misaki falls ill and is diagnosed with a rare progeroid syndrome, a disease that causes her body to age at an extraordinary speed and leaves her with very little time. Devastated and unwilling to let Haruto see her change, she withdraws from him, quits her job at the salon and eventually tells him that she has found someone else, breaking his heart. Cared for by her brother, who desperately searches for a cure, Misaki faces her rapid decline in seclusion, while Haruto, unaware of the truth, throws himself into his photography. The film follows both of them through the seasons as their separate paths move toward a final, bittersweet reckoning, with cherry blossoms serving as a recurring symbol of fleeting beauty and impermanence.

title: Fistful of Vengeance
overview: A revenge mission becomes a fight to save the world from an ancient threat when superpowered assassin Kai tracks a killer to Bangkok.
plot:
Fistful of Vengeance is a 2022 American supernatural martial arts action film directed by Roel Reiné and written by Cameron Litvack, Jessica Chou and Yalun Tu. A follow-up to the first season of the Netflix television series Wu Assassins, it stars Iko Uwais as Kai, Lewis Tan as Lu Xin and Lawrence Kao as Tommy, with Rhatha Phongam, JuJu Chan, Pearl Thusi, Francesca Corney, Jason Tobin and Simon Kuke.

Kai, the current Wu Assassin, and his friends Lu Xin and Tommy travel to Bangkok to find the killer of Tommy's sister Jenny, following the trail of an ancient talisman found on her body. In Thailand they are approached by William Pan, a biotech billionaire, who asks them to capture his twin sister, Ku An Qi, a powerful crime boss and jiangshi who has been absorbing vast amounts of qi to increase her supernatural powers. William explains that he and Ku are descendants of Pangu, the being who shaped the universe and who was killed by the first Wu Assassin after he became mad with power, and that his essence is contained in two talismans, one of which belonged to Ku.

According to William, Ku killed Jenny while searching for Kai, and with both talismans he can strip his sister of her power. Kai and his friends agree to help him and, joined by Tommy's friend Preeya, attempt to abduct Ku during a meeting with the city's Triad bosses. The plan goes wrong when Ku uses mind control to turn everyone in the building against them and Kai is ambushed by his old enemy Zan. Rescued by Zama, an Interpol agent who is pursuing Ku and is Lu Xin's former lover, the group takes refuge in Preeya's village, where a shaman reveals that William is secretly working with his sister to resurrect Pangu and remake the world.

The film combines martial arts fight sequences with Chinese mythology and supernatural elements, continuing the storylines left unresolved by the series.

Fistful of Vengeance was released worldwide on Netflix on February 17, 2022. It received mixed reviews, with 45 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 44.

title: A Christmas Proposal
overview: Chef who dreams of having own food trucks, agrees to pose as girlfriend of an attorney. Working together, they try to prove he's the ideal candidate to take over the family firm, but is complicated as real sparks begin to fly.
plot:
A Christmas Proposal is a 2021 American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Martin Wood and produced by the Motion Picture Corporation of America and Brad Krevoy Television for CBS. It stars Jessica Camacho as Maria Winters and Adam Rodriguez as Julian Diaz, with Luisa d'Oliveira as Maria's best friend Brooklyn, Bianca Caroca, Andres Soto, Claudia Ferri, Juan Chioran, Jaime M. Callica, Serge Houde, Shawn Hook, Malaika Jackson and Frank Crudele. Rodriguez, who also worked on the script to make the Latino family it portrays more authentic, described it as one of the first network Christmas films centred on an American family of Latin descent.

Maria is a struggling personal chef in Seattle who dreams of owning her own line of food trucks and drives for a ride-share app between cooking jobs. On her way to a singles Christmas party she picks up Julian, a wealthy, ambitious and rather cold attorney who pays her to drive him about 100 miles outside the city, where he plans to spend Christmas impressing his powerful father in the hope of being named his successor at the family law firm when he retires on Christmas Eve. Julian fears the job will instead go to his brother Bennett, who has a wife and children and seems more settled. When his parents meet Maria, they assume she is the surprise girlfriend Julian has hinted at, and he decides to run with the misunderstanding, while Maria agrees in return for an investment in her food truck. To keep their story straight without technically lying, the pair go on a crammed "power date" so they can describe their relationship truthfully. Maria cooks the family Christmas dinner, asks everyone to put their phones away at the table, and gradually draws the distracted Diaz family closer, but the business arrangement is complicated as real feelings develop between her and Julian, culminating at a Christmas Eve gala for children in need.

The film premiered on CBS on 12 December 2021. Brett White of Decider recommended it, presenting it as a revival of the major-network TV movie and praising its sleek, high-budget look, the lavish Diaz house, the chemistry between Camacho and Rodriguez and d'Oliveira's comic turn as the wisecracking best friend, and arguing that its inventive touches made an extremely familiar fake-relationship premise feel fresh.

title: 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible
overview: In 2019, Nepalese mountain climber Nirmal “Nims” Purja set out to do the unthinkable by climbing the world’s fourteen highest summits in less than seven months. (The previous record was eight years). He called the effort “Project Possible 14/7” and saw it as a way to inspire others to strive for greater heights in any pursuit. The film follows his team as they seek to defy naysayers and push the limits of human endurance.
plot:
14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible is a 2021 documentary directed by Torquil Jones that follows the Nepali mountaineer Nirmal "Nims" Purja and his team on Project Possible, an attempt to climb all fourteen of the world's eight-thousanders, the peaks higher than 8,000 metres, in under seven months. The previous fastest time, set by South Korea's Kim Chang-ho, was 7 years and 310 days. Jimmy Chin and Elizabeth Vasarhelyi served as executive producers with Purja, and the film features interviews with Reinhold Messner, the first person to climb all fourteen, as well as Chin, Purja's wife Suchi and his brother Kamal.

The expedition opens on Annapurna, statistically the deadliest of the peaks, which Purja summits on 23 April 2019 together with the Canadian climber Don Bowie, who had failed on it several times. The next day Purja goes back up to rescue a stricken Malaysian climber, costing his team its weather window on Dhaulagiri, which they summit in poor conditions on 12 May. Descending from Kanchenjunga after a single 22-hour push, the team comes across two Indian climbers in trouble in the death zone; despite giving them all their oxygen and waiting 12 hours for help, both die. Shaken and behind schedule, Purja climbs Everest, Lhotse and Makalu in a record 48 hours, and his photograph of the huge queue of climbers near Everest's summit goes viral.

Interviews trace Purja's background, including his service in the Gurkhas and Britain's Special Boat Service, a near-fatal sniper wound, his mother's failing health and the financial risks he took to fund the project, which at the outset was largely paid for by remortgaging his house. Moving to the Karakoram, he survives a fall on Nanga Parbat, then climbs the Gasherbrums, K2 and Broad Peak in 23 days; on K2, where avalanche danger has demoralised other teams, his crew fixes ropes through the Bottleneck that let 24 other climbers reach the summit. After rushing home to his mother, who has had a heart attack, he climbs Cho Oyu and Manaslu, lobbies for a Chinese permit and completes the project on Shishapangma on 29 October 2019, six months and six days after he began.

The film premiered at the DOC NYC festival and was released worldwide on Netflix in November 2021. It was well received, with 90% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; The New York Times praised its celebration of communal bonds.

title: God's Crooked Lines
overview: Alice Gould, a private investigator, pretends to be mentally ill in order to enter a psychiatric hospital and gather evidence for the case she is working on: the death of a patient in unclear circumstances.
plot:
God's Crooked Lines (Spanish: Los renglones torcidos de Dios) is a 2022 Spanish psychological thriller directed by Oriol Paulo and starring Bárbara Lennie as Alice Gould. Written by Paulo and Guillem Clua with the collaboration of Lara Sendim, it adapts Torcuato Luca de Tena's 1979 novel of the same name. Set inside a psychiatric hospital, the film is built around the question of whether its heroine is a brilliant investigator or a dangerously unstable patient.

In 1979, Alice Gould de Almenara is admitted to a psychiatric institution. She tells the doctors that she has been "legally abducted" by her husband, Heliodoro, who wants to seize her fortune. In reality, Alice claims, she is a private investigator who has feigned a mental illness to get inside the hospital, at the request of a doctor whose son, Damián, died there in mysterious circumstances. Once inside, she begins investigating among the patients, befriending some of them, including Ignacio Urquieta and a pair of twins, while confronting a predatory inmate known as the Gnome and his protector.

A second timeline, set during a stormy night when a fire and riot break out and a body is found in one of the cells, gradually converges with the main story. When the Gnome is found dead after attacking Alice in the woods, she becomes a suspect, and she struggles to remember what happened. Alice's account of her mission is challenged by the hospital's director, who presents evidence that she tried to poison her husband and that her story is a symptom of paranoia. As the medical council meets to decide her fate, both the doctors and the audience must determine whether Alice is telling the truth.

The film plays with the unreliability of perception and the boundary between sanity and madness, keeping its central ambiguity alive until the end.

God's Crooked Lines premiered at the 70th San Sebastián International Film Festival in September 2022 and was released theatrically in Spain by Warner Bros. on 6 October 2022, becoming one of the highest-grossing Spanish films of the year, before arriving on Netflix in December. It received positive reviews, with Cinemanía calling it a thrilling and elegant exercise, and earned six nominations at the 37th Goya Awards, including Best Actress for Lennie and Best Adapted Screenplay.

title: The Good Neighbor
tagline: Fear what's next door.
overview: A nightmarish evening unfolds for David, a former New York Times journalist, when he and his strange new neighbor Robert, accidentally hit a girl on her bike. Buzzed and disoriented, David lets Robert convince him to flee the scene and leave the girl for dead, in order to protect his career. Robert shows no remorse, and in the name of friendship he does unspeakable things to protect the secret. Now that the police are full-on hunting for the hit-and-run killer, things begin to spiral out of control when David’s local newspaper sends him to cover the story where he meets the deceased girl’s sister Vanessa. Despite the circumstances, and her deep desire to find her sister’s killer, the two immediately have a romantic connection, which surprises and haunts David, while pushing Robert to take brutal steps to keep his new friend to himself.
plot:
The Good Neighbor is a 2022 mystery crime thriller film directed by Stephan Rick, who wrote the screenplay with Ross Partridge, a remake of Rick's 2011 German film of the same name. Luke Kleintank stars as David Stevens, an American journalist, with Jonathan Rhys Meyers as his neighbor, Robert, Eloise Smyth and Bruce Davison. An American-Latvian co-production set and filmed in and around Riga, it received a limited theatrical release in June 2022 before being released on demand.

After a painful breakup, David arrives in Riga, Latvia, to begin a new job at the European Press Network. His editor, Grant, lets him stay in a house on the outskirts of the city while an apartment is prepared, and warns him that, as a newcomer, he will be given the assignments no one else wants. At the office, Grant tries to set him up with a colleague, Alice, but David is more interested in enjoying the city's nightlife as a single man. When he has trouble starting the old car Grant has left him, he is helped by his neighbor, Robert, a friendly but eccentric home-care nurse who tells him that his mother was British.

Lonely one evening, David invites Robert out for drinks. At a club, David flirts with Janine, a young woman from London, while Robert watches with disapproval. Driving home drunk, the two men are involved in a hit-and-run accident on a dark road, in which a cyclist is struck, and Robert persuades David not to report it. Consumed by guilt, David follows the case as the police investigation progresses, but he soon realizes that his new friend is far more dangerous than he appeared. Robert's behavior becomes increasingly possessive and controlling, and he uses their shared secret to bind David to him, while David's attempts to build a relationship and make amends threaten to expose them both. As Robert's obsession escalates into violence, David must find a way to free himself from his neighbor's grip before he loses everything.

The Good Neighbor received mixed reviews. Variety found it polished and well acted enough to be reasonably entertaining for its running time, but not original, tense or plausible enough to avoid a sense of letdown. Luke Y. Thompson of The A.V. Club graded it a C+, while other reviewers praised its unusual Riga setting and its suspense.

title: American Sicario
tagline: The story of America's most dangerous drug trafficker.
overview: The story of the rise and fall of the first American-born drug lord in Mexico, this tale of power, money, greed and betrayal amongst rival members of the drug cartels finds American gangster Erik Vasquez scheming to become the top dog in the Mexican underworld, only to find himself making enemies out of both the powerful cartels and his own allies.
plot:
American Sicario is a 2021 American crime action film directed by Raja "RJ" Collins from a screenplay by Rich Ronat, presented as being based on a true story. Produced in association with VMI Worldwide and GFG Entertainment and distributed by Saban Films, it stars Philippe A. Haddad as an American-born drug lord in Mexico, with Danny Trejo, Cali Morales, Maurice Compte, Maya Stojan, Jaylen Moore, Johnny Rey Diaz, Dionysio Basco and David A. Lockhart in supporting roles. The film opened in select US theatres on 10 December 2021 and was released on demand and on digital platforms on 14 December. It is rated R for violence, pervasive language, drug use and sexual material.

The film charts the rise and fall of Erik Vasquez (Haddad), a burly Texas native who fled to Mexico to escape narcotics charges in Laredo and has since worked his way up the cartel food chain, building his own gang and smuggling drugs back across the border. He now has a pregnant wife, Gloria (Morales), and a father-in-law, Pedro (Trejo), who is staying with them for an extended visit. Pedro, a veteran who once dealt drugs and worked with the cartels himself before getting out, has firm ideas about how Erik should treat Gloria and her unborn child, and warns him that in their business nothing is more important than family and loyalty. Scheming to become the top figure in the Mexican underworld, Erik tries to outmanoeuvre his bosses, the Feliz brothers (Compte and Diaz), and also crosses paths with DEA agent Monica Wells (Stojan). His ambition and greed turn both the powerful cartels and his own allies against him, culminating in an attack on his mansion, while his clashes with Pedro test the bonds of family and loyalty.

Critics generally found the film derivative. Josh Lasser of The TV and Film Guy's Reviews considered the cartel storyline bland and populated by two-dimensional characters, but enjoyed the lighter, more comic family thread driven by Trejo's sly presence, regretting that it played second fiddle. John Strange of Selig Film News gave it two stars, calling the gunfights poorly staged and edited and saying Trejo was wasted on the material. Mae Trumata of The Upcoming was more positive, praising the high-contrast, neon-lit cinematography and editing, the mansion assault sequence and the well-drawn generational contrast between Erik and Pedro.

title: Virus:32
tagline: 32 seconds to live or die.
overview: A virus is unleashed and a chilling massacre runs through the streets of Montevideo.
plot:
Virus:32 (Spanish: Virus 32) is a 2022 Uruguayan-Argentine horror film directed by Gustavo Hernández, who co-wrote it with Juma Fodde Roma. Produced by Aeroplano Cine, Mother Superior Films and Latido Films, with Sebastián Aloi and Ignacio García Cucucovich as producers and music by Hernán González, it stars Paula Silva, Daniel Hendler and the young Pilar García, with Franco Rilla and Sofía González. Set in Montevideo, it takes its title from a crucial detail: after each kill, the infected fall still for exactly thirty-two seconds.

Iris (Silva) works as a night guard at a vast, rundown sports club. Separated from her husband Javier (Rilla) since the death of their young son, she shares custody of their eight-year-old daughter Tata (García), and one night, having forgotten it is her turn, she must bring the girl along to work. Meanwhile, a virus is spreading through the city, turning people into savage killers. Leaving Tata in the gym with a walkie-talkie and watching her through the security cameras, Iris patrols the building, where strange figures have begun to appear. Attacked by an infected man and witnessing assaults in the street, she notices the thirty-two-second pause that follows each killing. Then Tata vanishes from the monitors. Searching the dark corridors as more infected arrive, Iris meets Luis (Hendler), a stranger who claims to know where her daughter is but demands that she first help deliver his wife's baby. She agrees, only to discover that the woman, bound and gagged in a wheelchair, is infected. Their ordeal leads through a besieged swimming pool, where the dying Javier appears, to a desperate birth, while Iris clings to the hope of finding Tata alive and escaping toward the port.

The film opened in Argentine cinemas on 21 April 2022 through Star Distribution and was released on video on demand in France that July. It received positive reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting more than 90% approval. Página 12 called it a magnificent horror tale and praised Silva's excellent performance, La Nación wrote that it is genuinely scary and sustains tension throughout with well-timed twists, and Clarín admired its perceptive script, agile direction and the work of Silva, a menacing Hendler and the debuting García. Otros Cines considered it a valuable example of the zombie subgenre in Latin American cinema, which rarely explores the theme, and Russian critic Stanislav Zelvensky included it among the best horror films of 2022.

tagline: You will definitely become stronger.
overview: Over a month has passed since 10,000 users were trapped inside the "Sword Art Online" world. Asuna, who cleared the first floor of the floating iron castle of Aincrad, joined up with Kirito and continued her journey to reach the top floor.
