title: The Wonderful Summer of Mickey Mouse
original_title: The Wonderful Summer of Mickey Mouse
overview: Mickey Mouse and his friends each recall the wild events leading up to the Annual Summer Fireworks Spectacular from their point-of-view.
plot:
The Wonderful Summer of Mickey Mouse is a 2022 American animated television special produced by Disney Television Animation for the streaming service Disney+. It is the third of four seasonal specials forming the second season of The Wonderful World of Mickey Mouse, following the winter and spring editions, and unlike its predecessors tells a single story rather than presenting separate shorts. It was directed and written by Karl Hadrika, Eddie Trigueros, Jason Reicher and Kristen Morrison, with writers including Paul Rudish, Darrick Bachman, William Reiss, Nick Lauer, Stevie Borbolla and Ricky Roxburgh. The voice cast features Chris Diamantopoulos as Mickey Mouse, Kaitlyn Robrock as Minnie Mouse, Tony Anselmo as Donald Duck, Tress MacNeille as Daisy Duck and Bill Farmer as Goofy. The special premiered on Disney+ on 8 July 2022 and runs about 22 minutes.

As Mickey races his boat to the marina for the town's annual Summer Spectacular fireworks show, a helicopter, a car and a luxury yacht all converge with him on the floating fireworks barge, which is destroyed. The Mayor, the Walrus from Alice in Wonderland, demands to know who is responsible, and each of the five friends tells their side of the story, beginning with a group call Mickey made at 2 a.m. to plan the day. Determined to get a perfect spot, Mickey dreamed of arriving early but overslept until 4 p.m. Minnie overloaded her car with double of everything, from pies to melting ice cream, until soda and mints launched it into the sky. Daisy, resolved to arrive exactly on time, woke to find her car crushed in her driveway and finally commandeered Scrooge McDuck's yacht. Donald, who had stayed up building a helicopter to take Daisy to the show, accidentally dropped it onto her car before crashing towards the barge, and Goofy had been camped beside the barge all along. Realising that they all share the blame, the friends work together to stage an improvised spectacular for their neighbours.

Jeremy Brown of What's On Disney Plus gave the special two and a half stars, calling it his least favourite of the seasonal specials so far and wishing for several summer stories rather than a recap of a single day, though he praised the animation and moments such as Donald destroying Daisy's car. Alex Reif of Laughing Place found it a lot of fun despite fewer Easter eggs than its predecessors, noting cameos including Chuuby from Mickey and Minnie's Runaway Railway, Snow White's forest friends and Clarabelle Cow.

title: A Christmas Mystery
tagline: Solve the crime. Save the season.
overview: When her best friend's father is falsely accused of stealing the town's prized jingle bells, a young amateur sleuth and her friends must find the real thief before Christmas.
plot:
A Christmas Mystery is a 2022 American family Christmas mystery film directed by Alex Ranarivelo and produced by ESX Entertainment and Lila Lane Pictures for HBO Max. It stars Violet McGraw as the eleven-year-old amateur sleuth Violet Pierce, with Eddie Cibrian as her father, the local sheriff, Santino Barnard as her best friend Kenny Bottoms, Drew Powell as Kenny's father George, Lauren Lindsey Donzis as Violet's older sister Maddie, Leonardo Cecchi as Kenny's older brother Harrison, Christoph Sanders as Deputy Terry and Beau Bridges as Mayor Donovan, alongside Oscar Nunez. Rated PG, it runs 87 minutes under the tagline "Solve the crime. Save the season."

A narrator recounts how, a century earlier, the mill town of Pleasant Bay, Oregon, fell on hard times when a drought closed its mill, until on Christmas Eve young Jimmy Stubbins found a strip of golden jingle bells that had fallen from Santa's sleigh and wished for the town's fortunes to be restored. By the next morning the river was flowing again and the mill was reopening. The bells became a symbol of hope, were put on display at the town museum and have been credited with Pleasant Bay's prosperity ever since. In the present, three days before Christmas, the bells are stolen, and the sheriff arrests George Bottoms, who works at the museum and has a past brush with the law, as the only person apparently able to reach them. Mayor Donovan, more concerned about his re-election than the town, is furious. Convinced that George is innocent, Violet, who has absorbed police procedure from watching her father and his bumbling deputy, the mayor's son, sets out with Kenny to find the real thief before Christmas, enlisting Maddie and Kenny's resentful brother Harrison. As the four uncover evidence the police overlooked, a romance grows between the teenagers, and their search leads into the underground tunnels beneath the town.

The film premiered on HBO Max on 24 November 2022. Liz Kocan of Decider recommended it as a sweet, Scooby-gang style whodunnit that turns into a Goonies-like adventure in its last third, praising McGraw's grounded performance, though she felt Bridges deserved a better role. Ricky Valero of Ready Steady Cut called it predictable but cute and enjoyed its score, while Barbara Shulgasser-Parker of Common Sense Media described it as a solid, kid-centred holiday movie.

title: Girl in the Picture
tagline: Her identity was a mystery to everyone. Even her.
overview: A young mother’s mysterious death and her son’s subsequent kidnapping blow open a decades-long mystery about the woman’s true identity, and the murderous federal fugitive at the center of it all.
plot:
Girl in the Picture is a 2022 American true-crime documentary directed by Skye Borgman and produced for Netflix. It is based on the investigative books A Beautiful Child and Finding Sharon by journalist Matt Birkbeck, who served as an executive producer and appears in the film. Through interviews with friends, relatives, investigators and journalists, archival photographs and reenactments, it reconstructs one of the most disturbing cases of identity theft and child abduction in American history. Netflix released the film on 6 July 2022.

In 1990, a young woman known as Tonya Hughes was struck by a car in a suspicious hit-and-run in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and died of her injuries. She left behind a young son, and her husband, an older man named Clarence Hughes, behaved strangely after her death. Investigators soon discovered that her life had been built on false identities. The woman had grown up as Sharon Marshall, a bright student in Forest Park, Georgia, who had been raised by a man posing as her father. That man turned out to be Franklin Delano Floyd, a federal fugitive with a long criminal record who had abducted her as a small child.

For roughly two decades, Floyd controlled every aspect of Sharon's life, moving her from state to state under different names, sexually abusing her and ultimately forcing her to marry him. Despite earning a scholarship, she was never able to escape him, and she had worked as an exotic dancer before her death. A few years later, Floyd abducted her son from his school at gunpoint; the boy was never found. The documentary follows the long efforts of Birkbeck, the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children and the FBI to piece together the truth, identify Sharon's real name and family, and uncover further crimes connected to Floyd, who was eventually convicted of murder and sentenced to death in Florida. Advances in DNA testing ultimately allowed her true identity to be established.

Girl in the Picture received generally positive reviews, with critics praising its careful storytelling and its focus on Sharon as a person rather than a victim, though some found its use of reenactments and its structure of withheld revelations sensational.

title: Hex
tagline: Jump. Pull. Pray. Die.
overview: Following a mysterious disappearance on a jump, a group of skydivers experiences paranormal occurrences that leave them fighting for their lives.
plot:
Hex is a 2022 American supernatural horror film directed by Chris Johnston and Andy Malchiodi, both making their feature directing debuts, from a screenplay by Hans Rodionoff, the writer of Deep Blue Sea 2 and Lost Boys: The Thirst. Set in the world of sport skydiving, it stars Kayla Adams, Matthew Holcomb, Chloe Berman, Bryan David Roberts, Eric Alperin, Brad Worch II and Schno Mozingo, with Cody Renee Cameron. Although it carries a 2020 copyright and its release was postponed from August, the film was released on video-on-demand and digital platforms by Lionsgate in late October 2022. It is rated R for language, some violent content and brief nudity.

The film opens with a montage of old illustrations of demons, skydivers performing a risky manoeuvre and blood being dripped onto an altimeter as it is assembled, ending with one of the parachutists falling to their death. Ten years later, Sarah (Adams), an avid skydiver like her late father, is the new member of a local skydiving club. Payson (Holcomb) is eager for her to join his team of Lisa (Berman), Wade (Roberts), Evan (Alperin) and Greg (Worch), because he wants to attempt The Hex, the dangerous and allegedly cursed formation jump that went wrong a decade earlier; the only ominous presence at the drop zone is Kris (Mozingo), a grizzled old parachute packer. The team pulls off the formation, but one of them never lands, vanishing in mid-air and even disappearing from the video of the jump. When the group jumps again the next day, another member suffers a heart attack on the way down, and further deaths follow, from a body found with every bone broken to an exploding apartment. Sarah, who seems to be the only one unaware that her father died performing The Hex along with the rest of his team, is drawn into a story of curses and deals with demons.

Reviews were negative. Jim Morazzini of Voices From the Balcony, in a review republished by Nerdly, gave it two out of five, calling it a waste of potential, "Point Break reaches its Final Destination"; he admired some impressive jump footage and the initially intriguing mystery, but found the script full of obvious twists and gaping plot holes, the deaths random and the gore light. Brian Costello of Common Sense Media described an interesting premise lost in flawed execution and clunky storytelling, with low-budget limitations increasingly evident, though he found its depiction of skydiving culture partly believable.

plot:
The Seven Deadly Sins: Grudge of Edinburgh Part 1 is a 2022 Japanese computer-animated fantasy action film directed by Bob Shirahata from a screenplay by Rintarō Ikeda. Based on Nakaba Suzuki's manga The Seven Deadly Sins, it is the first half of a two-part story co-produced by Alfred Imageworks and Marvy Jack for Netflix. Unlike earlier entries, it uses CG animation. Key members of the original voice cast return, with Ayumu Murase voicing the teenage Tristan and Mikako Komatsu the younger Tristan.

After their coronation as king and queen of Liones, Meliodas, of the Demon Clan, and Elizabeth, of the Goddess Clan, have a son, Tristan, who inherits the powers of both parents. At ten, while training with Lancelot, the son of Ban and a fairy, Tristan loses control to the demon side of his nature and gravely injures his friend, who vanishes shortly after. Ashamed and frightened of losing control again, Tristan turns to the gentler, healing side of his abilities, straining his bond with his parents.

Four years later Elizabeth falls gravely ill from a curse cast by Priest, a servant of Deathpierce, a former Holy Knight who seeks revenge for the injustices he suffered at the hands of the Demon and Goddess Clans fourteen years earlier. Tristan's goddess powers cannot cure his mother, so when he senses Priest he rushes out of the kingdom alone to save her. Gowther tracks him and alerts their old companions from the disbanded Seven Deadly Sins. Meanwhile Deathpierce is capturing demons, giants and fairies and fusing them into monstrous chimeras with his mystical Chaos Staff, planning to use them to conquer Liones.

On the road Tristan meets a hostile fairy who has rescued three non-human children from the Empties, the magical automatons serving Deathpierce. Uneasy allies, the pair trail the captive parents of those children to Edinburgh, the stronghold Deathpierce rules, and free them. When Tristan is nearly killed while struggling to master his demonic instincts, the fairy saves him and takes on a human form, revealing himself to be Lancelot.

Netflix released the film on December 20, 2022, with Part 2 following in August 2023. Anime News Network gave it a B-minus, enjoying the chance to reconnect with the characters and their children and calling it the start of a pretty good adventure, while IGN found it entertaining but incomplete.

title: Loving Adults
overview: The thin line between love and hate turns deadly when a wife discovers her husband’s affair — and they both take extreme measures to get what they want.
plot:
Loving Adults (Danish: Kærlighed for voksne) is a 2022 Danish drama film directed by Barbara Topsøe-Rothenborg. Dar Salim stars as Christian Holm and Sonja Richter as his wife, Leonora, with Sus Wilkins as Xenia, Mikael Birkkjær as the police commissioner and Lars Ranthe as Kim.

The story is framed as a tale told by a police commissioner to his daughter. Christian works in construction alongside his friend Peter, while Leonora gave up a career as a violinist years earlier to care for their son, Johan, whose illness is finally in remission as he nears his high school graduation. When Christian receives a 4 a.m. text he claims is from Peter and smashes his phone rather than show it to her, Leonora suspects an affair with Xenia, a young architect working with him on a contract. At an office party she catches the two having sex, with Xenia meeting her gaze. When Christian tries to end the marriage, Leonora threatens to report that he embezzled company money to pay for Johan's treatment unless he leaves Xenia. Seeking leverage, Christian learns from an old schoolmate of Leonora's that her former boyfriend Mike died in a mysterious fall from a cliff during a party, and he accuses her of pushing him. Thrown out of the house, Christian waits on Leonora's usual running route and runs her down with a company van, only to find her arriving home safely, having taken another route; he has hit a different woman. Shaken, he pretends to have ended the affair.

Leonora notices that Christian washed the van and realizes he meant to kill her. She tries to turn him in, but he persuades the commissioner of his innocence for the time being. She then confesses to Christian that she did kill Mike and insists that he help her kill Xenia, reasoning that he will not try to murder her again if he has no one to leave her for. At a spa resort, Leonora creates an alibi by playing a recording of his voice and sending Xenia a breakup message from his phone while Christian slips away to Xenia's allotment. He reconciles with Xenia instead, but Leonora, having predicted he would not go through with it, stabs Xenia to death. The commissioner, suspicious, brings police dogs, which bark at a Sankt Hans bonfire; he realizes the body is hidden inside, but Christian lights it before he can stop him. The commissioner's story is revealed to be a cautionary tale told to his daughter before her wedding, and abroad, a grieving Christian scatters Xenia's remains in the water.

title: Bullet Proof
tagline: Get out. Fast!
overview: The Thief  pulls off the robbery of a lifetime when he robs the psychotic drug lord, Temple. The plan goes off without a hitch until the Thief discovers a stowaway in his getaway car - Temple's pregnant wife, Mia.
plot:
Bullet Proof, previously titled Death Pursuit, is a 2022 action crime thriller film directed by James Clayton, a character actor making his feature directorial debut, who also stars as the unnamed lead and developed the story; the screenplay is credited to Cooper Bibaud and Danny Mac. Produced by companies including IndustryWorks Studios, Play by Play Entertainment, Peacemaker Filmworks, RAW Camera Company, Greendale Productions and Grindstone Entertainment Group, it co-stars Vinnie Jones as a ruthless drug lord and Lina Lecompte as his pregnant wife, with Janvier Katabarwa, Danny Mac, Glenn Ennis, Philip Granger and Lori Triolo in supporting roles. Lionsgate released the film in select theatres and on demand in August 2022. It runs 81 minutes.

At a junkyard where the face-tattooed henchmen of the psychotic drug lord Temple (Jones) are about to execute a man who betrayed them, a skilled thief known only as the Thief (Clayton) sneaks in, grabs a large stash of cash, fights off the gang amid a hail of bullets and escapes in a stolen car. After a collision forces him to take another vehicle, he pulls over on the highway to bandage a wound and discovers a stowaway hiding in the trunk: Mia (Lecompte), Temple's pregnant wife, who has fled because she refuses to raise her child with such a brutal father, and who overheard the Thief's getaway plan. Furious at both the robbery and her betrayal, Temple sends his associate Skinny (Mac) and his top enforcer, a seemingly unstoppable assassin known as the Frenchman (Katabarwa), to recover the money, Mia and his unborn child. The reluctant partners go on the run with Temple's killers on their trail, their escape complicated by a stop at a clinic for Mia's pregnancy and by a gang of local thugs who try to steal the money for themselves.

Reviews were mixed to negative. Julian Roman of MovieWeb praised the strong, Guy Ritchie-style opening, the groovy soundtrack, the chemistry between Clayton and Lecompte and Jones and Katabarwa as sadistic villains, but felt a filler-heavy second act brought the film to a crawl, recommending it only as a pure B-movie. AMovieGuy.com gave it two stars out of four, crediting Clayton's energy and quick editing but finding the action mundane, the leads' chemistry ice cold and Jones underused. Ewan Gleadow of Cult Following criticised its generic storytelling, poorly developed action and blurred, trailer-like visuals.

title: South Park the Streaming Wars Part 2
original_title: South Park the Streaming Wars Part 2
overview: A drought has brought the town of South Park to the brink of disaster.
plot:
"South Park: The Streaming Wars Part 2" is a 2022 American adult animated television special written and directed by Trey Parker, who voices most of the characters with co-creator Matt Stone. The fourth South Park special and the 319th episode overall, it was released on Paramount+ on July 13, 2022, and concludes the story begun in "South Park: The Streaming Wars", in which a severe drought grips Colorado and the eccentric water-park owner Pi Pi plans to profit from it.

As the drought worsens, Cartman takes his mother Liane to court, while his friends testify that he spent their earnings on breast implants; the case is thrown out. Randy Marsh wakes on a bench, terrifying onlookers, and is tranquillised by police, who explain that he went "full nuclear Karen". Remorseful, he abandons his marijuana farm and returns to his old career as a geologist to tackle the water shortage. Tolkien searches the abandoned home of the late Robert Cussler for clues to the whereabouts of his missing father, Steve, while Cartman convinces himself that Tolkien is sleeping with his mother.

At a Denver council meeting, Pi Pi pitches a plan to run the whole state on urine, backed by celebrities who previously promoted cryptocurrency and NFTs. Randy instead proposes a desalination plant, which the city adopts, so Pi Pi orders his enforcers, including ManBearPig, to get rid of him. Detective Harris tells the boys that ManBearPig is being coerced because Pi Pi is holding his mate, PigBearGirl, and their offspring, Chuck Chuck. Steve, injured, wakes in a sewer after the creatures have tended his wounds. Cartman, Butters and Tolkien sneak into the water park, find Chuck Chuck and are captured, as Pi Pi reveals his scheme to them.

When ManBearPig wrecks the desalination plant, Randy's family persuade him to become Karen again with a strain of marijuana Sharon had kept. He storms the water park and exposes Pi Pi in the middle of a commercial shoot, allowing the boys to escape with the help of PigBearGirl and Chuck Chuck. Tolkien is reunited with his father, and ManBearPig, freed from coercion, decapitates Pi Pi. Randy persuades Cartman and other people with breast implants to drain their saline to supply the plant, which brings water back to Denver, and the creature family returns to the woods.

Critics responded well, with ComingSoon.net rating it 9 out of 10 and calling it a step up from the first part.

title: Skinamarink
tagline: In this house...
overview: Two children wake up in the middle of the night to find their father is missing, and all the windows and doors in their home have vanished.
plot:
Skinamarink is a 2022 Canadian experimental horror film written and directed by Kyle Edward Ball in his feature debut. It stars Lucas Paul as four-year-old Kevin and Dali Rose Tetreault as his six-year-old sister Kaylee, with Ross Paul and Jaime Hill as their father and mother. Ball, who had run a YouTube channel recreating nightmares described by viewers, developed the film from his short Heck (2020) and shot it on digital video in his childhood home in Edmonton on a budget of about $15,000.

In 1995, Kevin is injured in what Kaylee says was a sleepwalking accident and is brought home from the hospital. In the middle of the night, the two children wake to find that their father has vanished and that the windows, doors and other objects in the house are gradually disappearing. They settle downstairs in front of the television, watching old cartoons, but the house stays dark: they hear unexplained thumps, find a chair upside down on the ceiling, and discover that the downstairs toilet has disappeared. Kevin wonders whether their father "went with mom," but Kaylee does not want to talk about their mother.

A voice calls Kaylee upstairs, where she sees her father, who tells her to look under the bed, and then her mother, who says that they love the children and tells her to close her eyes before vanishing. From the closet come her mother's voice, moans of pain and the sound of breaking bones, and a hand reaches around a corner. Kaylee flees downstairs, and the siblings barricade the hallway with the couch, but while Kevin sleeps she disappears. The voice draws Kevin to the basement, where Kaylee appears without eyes or a mouth, and it tells him it wants to play. Obeying its commands, Kevin hurts his own eye, then calls 9-1-1, before the phone turns into a toy. The voice says it can "do anything" and that it took Kaylee's mouth because she disobeyed. Kevin follows it upstairs, finding himself walking on the ceiling, as on-screen text reads "572 days," Kaylee fades away, and finally an indistinct face looms over his bed and tells him to go to sleep, ignoring his questions about its name.

Skinamarink premiered at the Fantasia Film Festival on July 25, 2022, and after leaked copies built word-of-mouth buzz online, IFC Midnight released it in North American theaters on January 13, 2023. It grossed nearly $900,000 in its first four days, a commercial success, and received generally favorable reviews (73% on Rotten Tomatoes, 66 on Metacritic).

title: Royalteen
overview: A teenager struggles to keep her scandal-ridden past and a big secret from getting out when she strikes up an unlikely romance with the crown prince.
plot:
Royalteen (Norwegian: Royalteen: Arvingen, "The Heir") is a 2022 Norwegian teen romantic drama directed by Per-Olav Sørensen and Emilie Beck for Netflix, based on the young-adult novel series by Randi Fuglehaug and Anne Gunn Halvorsen. Co-written by Ester Schartum-Hansen, it stars Ines Høysæter Asserson as Lena and Mathias Storhøi as Crown Prince Karl Johan, known as Kalle, with Elli Rhiannon Müller Osborne as his twin sister Margrethe and Veslemøy Mørkrid and Petter Width Kristiansen as Lena's parents. The film runs 107 minutes and was conceived as the first installment of a franchise.

Lena is a teenager whose parents have uprooted their lives and found new jobs so that the family can move to Oslo and give her a fresh start after a scandal in her previous town, the reasons for which are not revealed at first. At her new school, which the royal twins attend, she strikes up a friendly conversation with Kalle on her first day. The prince, who is trying to shake off his party-boy image and is weary of people who see only his public persona, takes a liking to her, and the two slowly begin a romance through a series of ups and downs, including surprise visits to her home and the pressures of life in the public eye. Lena, who seems unimpressed that she is dating a royal, is not completely honest with Kalle about why she moved, and the secret she carries keeps haunting her; she devotedly cares for a baby she introduces to classmates as her little brother, though the child's real connection to her is more complicated. Her past catches up with her through old friends she treated badly, while the protective Margrethe, determined to preserve the royal status quo, makes biting remarks about Lena's ordinary background and opposes the relationship. As the truth threatens to come out, Lena must decide what she is willing to reveal to keep her love.

Royalteen was released on Netflix on 17 August 2022. Reviews were mixed. Decider's Radhika Menon advised skipping it, finding the romance clunky, Lena's secret obvious from the first act and the ending confusing, though she praised the strong chemistry between Asserson and Storhøi and the parents' grounded performances. On High on Films, Akash Deshpande considered the premise a reiteration of familiar teen tropes with surface-level class commentary, but found it consistently engaging thanks to unhurried direction and committed acting. Norwegian newspaper VG was more enthusiastic.

title: Broad Peak
overview: After climbing Broad Peak mountain, Maciej Berbeka learns his journey to the summit is incomplete. 25 years later, he sets out to finish what he started.
plot:
Broad Peak is a 2022 Polish biographical adventure drama directed by Leszek Dawid about mountaineer Maciej Berbeka and his quest to make the first winter ascent of Broad Peak, an eight-thousander in the Karakoram. Ireneusz Czop plays Berbeka, with Maja Ostaszewska as his wife, Ewa, Łukasz Simlat as Krzysztof Wielicki, Piotr Głowacki as Aleksander Lwow.

In March 1988, a Polish expedition in Pakistan is struggling on K2. Two of its members, Berbeka and Lwow, set out against the wishes of their leader, Zawada, to attempt the first winter and first alpine-style ascent of neighboring Broad Peak. Leaving base camp on the Baltoro Glacier, they are hit by a blizzard, and Zawada urges them to turn back if it does not ease. On the summit push, Lwow sees bad weather approaching and retreats, but Berbeka presses on alone into the death zone. After a tense silence on the radio, he reports that he has reached the top. He survives the descent and returns to Poland a celebrity, though haunted by flashbacks of the climb.

Three months later, an article by Lwow reveals that Berbeka actually stopped at the Rocky Summit, 17 meters short of the true summit. Furious, he confronts Zawada, who explains that the team wanted him back alive and knew he would have kept climbing had he known the truth. As the story spreads in Poland, Berbeka withdraws from mountaineering. In June 2012, twenty-four years later, Krzysztof Wielicki finds him and asks him to join a winter expedition to Broad Peak, arguing that he deserves to finish what he started. Berbeka initially refuses but eventually joins a team of Wielicki, Bielecki, Tomasz Kowalski and Artur Małek. On the summit push the team falls behind schedule, and at the Rocky Summit Wielicki warns that there is not enough daylight left and orders them down. Ignoring him, Berbeka and the three other climbers reach the summit on 5 March 2013, completing the first winter ascent of the mountain. A closing title reveals that Berbeka and Kowalski died during the descent.

Filming began in 2018 in the Karakoram and the Italian Alps; in Pakistan, 250 sherpas carried three and a half tons of equipment. Netflix released the film on 14 September 2022. Common Sense Media found some of the drama forced and the conquest selfish, while Decider called Ostaszewska's performance the closest thing the film had to an emotional core.

title: Stowaway
overview: A tenacious party girl fights to survive after three thieves commandeer her luxury yacht. Unable to escape and trapped on the yacht at high seas, the prey becomes the hunter as she turns the tables on the intruders and takes matters into her own hands.
plot:
Stowaway, developed under the title The Yacht, is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Declan Whitebloom, a music-video director making his feature debut, from a screenplay by Ian Hayden. Ruby Rose stars as Bella Denton, with Frank Grillo as Meeser, Patrick Schwarzenegger as Michael, Scotty Bohnen as Sunshine, Danny Bohnen as Jim, Luis Da Silva Jr. as Captain Lawson and Major Dodge as Bella's father, Arthur Denton; the former American football player Vernon Davis also appears. Saban Films handled the release.

Bella is a tough, streetwise young woman who has drifted through petty theft and partying, scarred by a childhood in which her father, a mercenary, was absent. When the estranged Arthur dies suddenly, he leaves her a luxury yacht, an unexpected windfall she is still trying to make sense of. After meeting Michael, a stranger, in a bar, she brings him aboard for a night of luxury, but the boat does not stay theirs for long. Three criminals led by Meeser, a former associate of her father, seize the yacht at sea in search of money that he and Arthur stole together.

Trapped on board and unable to escape, Bella turns from prey to hunter, using her wits to fight back against the intruders in a cat-and-mouse game below and above deck, while Michael gets away to find help. Throughout, the men around her insist that her father was a good person, a view she resents given her own experience of him, and Captain Lawson reveals that Arthur had in fact given the stolen money away to charities. Meeser murders the captain, but Bella escapes from the vessel and sets off an explosive device, and she is rescued by the coast guard, alerted by Michael. Afterward, she donates part of the yacht's insurance payout to Lawson's widow.

The film was released on the streaming service AMC+ on 5 August 2022. Reviews were negative. Common Sense Media gave it two stars out of five, calling it a tedious boat-bound thriller with a sluggish plot, villains who keep explaining their scheme, shaky camerawork and an unconvincing final act, though it found the mystery around the pirates kept it watchable. Screen Rant, also awarding two stars, praised Rose's convincing lead performance and Grillo's efforts to lift a thinly written role, but faulted poor lighting, illogical choices and a script that sidelines its only woman's perspective, judging it no match for Panic Room.

title: Wifelike
tagline: They're too human to be perfect. She's too perfect to be human.
overview: A grieving detective in the near-future hunts down criminals who trade artificial humans on the black market. In the fight to end AI exploitation, an underground resistance attempts to infiltrate him by sabotaging the programming of the artificial human assigned as his companion to behave like his late wife. She begins to question her reality as memories of a past life begin to surface in a world where nothing is as it seems.
plot:
Wifelike is a 2022 American science fiction thriller written and directed by James Bird, starring Jonathan Rhys Meyers and Elena Kampouris, with Doron Bell, Agam Darshi and Sara Sampaio in supporting roles. It was released in select theaters and on digital platforms on August 12, 2022.

In the near future, a company called Wifelike manufactures expensive android replicas of deceased women for the men who mourn them. These companions are designed to be subservient to their owners, but they gradually begin to develop consciousness. A militant activist group, S.C.A.I.R., considers the androids slaves and seeks to destroy the company. One faction steals companions, reprograms them and uses them to commit crimes and bombings, and the authorities have been unable to identify its leader, known as the Ringmaster.

William Bradwell is a seasoned agent who tracks down stolen androids and returns them to their owners. He orders a companion modeled on his late wife, Meredith, who begins learning about her life in order to become more like her. William tells her that Meredith was once a S.C.A.I.R. activist who gave up the cause after falling in love with him. It is not the first time he has gone through this process: earlier versions of his companion were stolen by the group and recovered by him, each time with their memories wiped.

As the new companion learns, she begins to dream of a masked man who claims to have known her before her last reset, and she is visited by Louise, a S.C.A.I.R. member who seems to know her previous iterations. William discovers that some androids have joined the group willingly to escape their owners, and he enters the digital "dreamscape" that manages the companions' thoughts to confront the masked man. Taken back to Wifelike for another wipe, the companion learns from other androids that she can retain hidden memories, and she secretly keeps playing her role. Evidence emerges that William murdered the man presumed to be the Ringmaster and that he is hiding the truth about Meredith. Overriding her safety protocols, the companion kills William and returns to S.C.A.I.R., revealing that she herself is the true Ringmaster, while the company announces a crackdown led by an android version of William.

The film received poor reviews, holding a 13% rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on eight reviews.

title: Scrooge: A Christmas Carol
overview: On a cold Christmas Eve, selfish miser Ebenezer Scrooge has one night left to face his past — and change the future — before time runs out.
plot:
Scrooge: A Christmas Carol is a 2022 animated musical fantasy film directed by Stephen Donnelly and produced by Timeless Films, an animated reimagining of the 1970 musical Scrooge by Leslie Bricusse, itself based on Charles Dickens's 1843 novella A Christmas Carol. Luke Evans voices Ebenezer Scrooge, with Olivia Colman, Jessie Buckley, Jonathan Pryce, Johnny Flynn, Fra Fee, James Cosmo and Trevor Dion Nicholas. Dedicated to Bricusse, who died in 2021, it opened in select cinemas on November 18, 2022, before reaching Netflix on December 2.

On Christmas Eve 1843 in London, the miserly moneylender Scrooge, accompanied by his friendly mastiff Prudence, dodges his cheerful nephew Harry, refuses a donation to charity and adds to the debt of the toy-shop owner Tom Jenkins, who borrowed to pay for his mother's medical care. Scrooge resents Harry because his beloved sister Jen died giving birth to him. He grudgingly gives his underpaid clerk, Bob Cratchit, Christmas Day off; the Cratchits live in poverty, and their youngest son, Tiny Tim, is seriously ill and cannot afford treatment.

At home Scrooge is visited by the ghost of his late partner Jacob Marley, Prudence's former owner, who taught him to be ruthless and now drags the chains of his misdeeds. Marley warns Scrooge of the same fate and announces three visitors. The first, Past, a shifting, wax-like spirit, shows Scrooge how his father's imprisonment for debt forced him to support his mother and sister, his happy years working for the kindly Mr. Fezziwig, and his engagement to Fezziwig's daughter Isabel, which ended after Scrooge joined Marley and helped close the bakery that was Bob's childhood home.

The second spirit, the joyful giant Present, shows Harry's affection for his uncle and the Cratchits' grateful celebration in their cramped home. The third, Yet to Come, shows Tom leading a celebration that Scrooge first takes as praise, until he learns it is a reaction to his own death, that Tiny Tim has died and that almost no one mourns him. Glimpsing the afterlife that awaits him, Scrooge vows to change.

Waking on Christmas morning, he makes peace with Isabel's new life and throws a party, cancelling Tom's debt, giving to the charity, presenting Harry with a Father Christmas doll made by Jen and making Bob his business partner. Critics were divided, with 40% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and criticism of the animation and songs.

title: Untold: The Race of the Century
original_title: Untold: The Race of the Century
overview: The Australia II yacht crew looks back on the motivation, dedication and innovation that led to their historic victory at the 1983 America's Cup.
plot:
Untold: The Race of the Century is a 2022 American sports documentary film directed by Chapman Way and Maclain Way, the producers of Netflix's Untold anthology series. Part of the series' second volume, it recounts how the Australian yacht Australia II ended the New York Yacht Club's 132-year hold on the America's Cup in 1983, described in the film as the longest winning streak in the history of sport. It was released on Netflix on 6 September 2022.

The documentary opens with a primer on the America's Cup, the oldest international competition still contested in any sport, in which a defending and a challenging boat race until one wins four times. For decades the New York Yacht Club, the epitome of American old money, had defended the trophy in Newport, Rhode Island, and in 1983 its skipper was Dennis Conner, a brilliant and intensely driven sailor who recalls winning 38 straight races. The Australian challenger John Bertrand, whose great-grandfather had worked on the design of an America's Cup boat, had studied American sailing at MIT; backed by the flamboyant financier Alan Bond, later convicted of financial crimes, he assembled a crew chosen for intellect and confidence and embraced psychological testing and visualisation, unusual practices at the time. The film focuses on the boat's designer, Ben Lexcen, a barefoot eccentric with three years of formal schooling who died in 1988, and his radical winged keel. The keel was hidden from view and guarded around the clock as Australia II won 47 of 55 qualifying races, and Lexcen "accidentally" left a false sketch of it on a copy-shop photocopier, which quickly circulated around Newport. Conner and the New York Yacht Club, facing the loss of the Cup and the right to host it, tried to have the boat banned, arguing that Dutch engineers rather than Lexcen had designed it, but failed. The final third follows the races between Conner's Liberty and Australia II: after mechanical failures, the Australians fell behind 3–1 before rallying to win the deciding seventh race, as audiences in Australia, including the prime minister, cheered them on. Interviewed decades later, Bertrand and Conner still show the emotions of victory and defeat.

Decider's Scott Hines recommended it as a thrilling story even for viewers who know nothing about sailing, praising its production values. Michael Grant of Awful Announcing found the opening slow but called the battle of wills between Bertrand and Conner engrossing.

title: Inside the Mind of a Cat
original_title: Inside the Mind of a Cat
overview: Cat experts dive into the mind of the feline to reveal the true capabilities of the pouncing pet in this captivating and cuddly documentary.
plot:
Inside the Mind of a Cat is a 2022 American documentary film directed by Andy Mitchell and produced by Red Rock Films for Netflix. Running 67 minutes, it draws on recent research into feline behaviour, physiology and cognition to argue that cats are not the aloof, inscrutable pets they are often taken to be. Interviewees include Yuki Hattori of the Tokyo Feline Medical Center, Bruce Kornreich of the Cornell Feline Health Center, Wailani Sung of the San Francisco SPCA, the researcher Saho Takagi of Azabu University and the cat psychologist Kristyn Vitale of Unity College, along with Maryna and Svitlana Savitska of the Savitsky Cats, a trained performing troupe that reached the quarter-finals of America's Got Talent.

The film notes that scientific study of cats lags roughly fifteen years behind research on dogs, and that holding cats to canine expectations has long been a mistake: cats show affection and loyalty but are not driven to please their owners. Combining interviews, archival footage, animated sequences and viral cat videos, it examines the animals' unusual skeletal structure and balance, the many vocalisations they use, including meows directed at humans to win a response, and signs of trust such as slow blinking or lying belly up. It asks whether cats know their own names, play favourites and truly love their owners. A historical thread traces how cats largely domesticated themselves by hunting rodents for early farmers, cites ancient remains found in Cyprus as evidence of the long human bond, describes how the persecution of cats in medieval Europe may have helped plague spread, and features Herman, a cat enlisted with the US Coast Guard in the 1940s, as well as Istanbul's protective approach to street cats. The Savitsky Cats demonstrate that felines can be trained through techniques such as clicker training and positive reinforcement.

The documentary was released on Netflix on 18 August 2022. Joel Keller of Decider recommended it as a family-friendly starting point for new and prospective cat owners, enjoying its adorable subjects and the acrobatic Savitsky Cats while noting that much of its information is available elsewhere and that it does not go deeply into topics such as indoor versus outdoor living. Greg Wheeler of The Review Geek rated it 7.5 out of 10, calling it fun and informative though rushed in its final minutes, and Common Sense Media described it as a purr-fect primer for children.

title: The Christmas Retreat
overview: When Kim's boyfriend breaks up with her instead of proposing, Kim's mom takes her away to a Christmas Retreat to reconnect with the spirit of the holiday. There she meets newly unemployed Mark.
plot:
The Christmas Retreat is a 2022 Canadian Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Jason Bourque from a screenplay by Erica Deutschman. Produced by Reel One Entertainment and Champlain Media with CME Lakeside Productions, it stars Rhiannon Fish and Clayton James, with Lynn Whyte, Jonathan Hawley Purvis, Carly Fawcett, Vanessa Lynn and James MacDonald in supporting roles. The film premiered on the American cable network UPtv on 11 November 2022, coinciding with Veterans Day, and runs 90 minutes.

Kim (Fish) is a workaholic who keeps working even during her office Christmas party and ignores her colleague's and her mother's urging to take time off. While hailing a taxi one night she clashes with Mark (James), another busy professional, and makes him late for an important meeting; as a result his boss, who favours his own inexperienced son, fires Mark. When Kim's boyfriend Steven (Purvis) breaks up with her instead of proposing because she is always busy, her mother Mary (Whyte) whisks her away to a week-long Christmas retreat in the mountains to reconnect with the spirit of the holiday. There they meet the retreat's owner Rae (Fawcett) and her newly unemployed brother Mark, who has come to clear his head, while Mary reunites with her friend Celeste (Lynn) and Celeste's older brother Ted (MacDonald), a retired photographer. The retreat's first rule bans all electronic devices, but Kim hides her phone in a sock to keep up with work and with Steven; when Mark catches her, she points out that he has kept his too, and they agree not to report each other. Through gingerbread house and wreath making, Christmas storytelling and a visit to a pancake restaurant, Kim and Mark overcome their mutual hostility and the mistakes neither wants to admit, and slowly fall for each other, while a romance also blossoms between Mary and Ted.

Reviews were mixed. Markos Papadatos of True Hollywood Talk gave the film four out of five stars, calling it a heartwarming, feel-good film that held the viewer's attention, with good chemistry between the charming James and the bubbly, sassy Fish, and describing Whyte as sensational as Mary. Nick Wangersky of the Canadian film site HNMag found it predictable from start to finish, with leads who were not especially likeable and supporting characters who were not around long enough, though he enjoyed the mountain setting.

title: Single and Ready to Jingle
overview: Emma Warner feels like she lives Christmas year-round. As SVP at a toy company, she has had a great year with the season’s most successful toy but she is exhausted. All she wants is a non-holiday vacation with hot guys and a beach. Her assistant books her a flight to St. Johns but she ends up on the wrong plane and lands in St. Johns, Alaska, a town that goes all out for Christmas. Local holiday hero, Connor is stuck dealing with Emma who he considers a scrooge until her childhood Christmas memories thaw her to this town and to Connor.
plot:
Single and Ready to Jingle is a 2022 Canadian Christmas romantic comedy television film produced by Reel One Entertainment, Champlain Media and CME Lakeside Productions for Lifetime. It stars Natasha Wilson as Emma Warner and Edward Ruttle as Connor, with Eva Tavares, Crystal Tisiga, Lynn Whyte, Beth Fotheringham, James MacDonald, Merry Lou Proudfoot, C.J. Wilkins and Storeigh Daniel. The film runs 90 minutes and premiered on Lifetime in late November 2022 during the network's holiday programming.

Emma is a senior vice president at a successful toy company in Chicago who feels she lives Christmas all year round. She once loved the holiday, but spending twelve months a year thinking about it has left her no time for dating or much else, and after a strong year in which she developed one of the season's most successful toys, a K-pop panda, she is exhausted. All she wants is a holiday-free getaway at a tropical singles resort, so she asks her assistant and friend Lucy to book her a trip to St. John in the Caribbean. Because of a booking mix-up, however, she lands in St. John, Alaska, dressed in sandals and a strapless jumpsuit, in sub-zero temperatures, in a small town devoted to everything Christmas. When a snowstorm shuts the airport, she is stranded. Connor, a local holiday hero who considers her a Scrooge, gives her his coat and a ride to the Sleigh Bell Inn, run by his sister Callie and her wife, where Emma is checked into the festive Candy Cane Suite. As Connor shows her the town, from snowball fights and snowshoeing to the toys he makes for local children, Emma's childhood memories of Christmas begin to thaw her, until she discovers that Connor has a connection to her work that he has kept from her, and the two must sort out their feelings before she flies home.

Reviews were mostly negative. Kristen of TV Tweetie found the premise cute, comparing Emma's predicament to Home Alone 2, and liked Wilson and Ruttle in the leads, especially the caring Connor, but she judged the film flawed by a slow start, clichés and errors such as characters standing outdoors without hats or gloves in temperatures said to be twelve below zero, and did not recommend it. Patrick Serrano of Lifetime Uncorked gave it his lowest ratings, describing its plot as erratic and the result as almost a parody of a bad TV movie, though he welcomed its depiction of a lesbian couple.

title: A Trip to Infinity
overview: Does infinity exist? Can we experience the Infinite? In an animated film (created by artists from 10 countries) the world's most cutting-edge scientists and mathematicians go in search of the infinite and its mind-bending implications for the universe.  Eminent mathematicians, particle physicists and cosmologists dive into infinity and its mind-bending implications for the universe.
plot:
A Trip to Infinity is a 2022 American animated documentary film directed by Jonathan Halperin and Drew Takahashi, in their feature directorial debut, and written by Halperin and Alex Ricciardi. Produced by Room 608 and Make Make Entertainment, with animation by Studio AKA, Compost Creative and artists from ten countries, it explores the concept of infinity through interviews with mathematicians, physicists, cosmologists and philosophers. It was released on Netflix on 26 September 2022.

The film's participants include the physicists Brian Greene, Janna Levin, Stephon Alexander, Carlo Rovelli and Anthony Aguirre, the astrophysicist Delilah Gates, the mathematicians Steven Strogatz, Eugenia Cheng and Moon Duchin, the philosophers Rebecca Goldstein and Kenny Easwaran, and the physicist and novelist Alan Lightman. Organised into numbered chapters and illustrated by animation in a wide range of styles, from the literal to the metaphorical, it asks whether infinity exists, whether it can be found in the physical world, and whether a mortal person could ever experience the endless. Strogatz narrates "The Infinite Hotel", a cartoon based on the German mathematician David Hilbert's thought experiment about a fully occupied hotel that can always find room for more guests, even infinitely many. Other segments consider how infinity can make one equal zero, the very large and the very small, black holes and wormholes, and an apple left in a box for so long that it decays into particles and eventually becomes an apple again. Gates reflects on whether the universe might be finite yet appear endless to its inhabitants, like a dot travelling round a circle or across the surface of a ball, and the film notes that there are infinitely many ways for the universe to be finite but only a few for it to be infinite. The film closes by asking whether human creativity itself is infinite, leaving the impression that infinity reveals the limits of human understanding.

A Trip to Infinity won the award for Outstanding Graphic Design and Art Direction at the 44th News and Documentary Emmy Awards. John Serba of Decider found it slickly made and terrifically entertaining without dumbing down its ideas, singling out Strogatz's infectious enthusiasm. In The New Yorker, the mathematician Dan Rockmore praised its experts and the Infinite Hotel sequence but felt that its psychedelic animations and philosophical detours sometimes distracted from the mathematics.

title: V/H/S/99
tagline: VHS goes to hell.
overview: A teenager’s home video leads to a series of horrifying revelations.
plot:
V/H/S/99 is a 2022 American found footage horror anthology produced by Studio71 and Bloody Disgusting, the sequel to V/H/S/94 and the fifth installment in the V/H/S franchise. Set in 1999, at the end of the VHS era, it contains five segments written and directed by Maggie Levin, Johannes Roberts, Flying Lotus, Tyler MacIntyre, and the duo Vanessa and Joseph Winter. Unlike earlier films in the series, it has no framing narrative; instead, short stop-motion animations of toy soldiers made by a character from one of the stories serve as interludes.

In Levin's "Shredding", members of a young punk band who record their antics for a web show break into the ruins of a music venue where another band died in a fire and stampede, and mock the dead musicians, with grisly consequences. In Roberts's "Suicide Bid", a college freshman desperate to join a prestigious sorority agrees to a hazing ritual in which she is buried overnight in a coffin in a graveyard, re-creating an urban legend about a girl who vanished there two decades earlier.

Flying Lotus's "Ozzy's Dungeon" follows a girl badly injured on a sadistic children's game show and her mother's twisted revenge on the show's host. In MacIntyre's "The Gawkers", a group of teenage boys use a camcorder to spy on an attractive new neighbor whose yard is filled with stone busts, while the younger brother they exclude befriends her, with deadly consequences. In the Winters' "To Hell and Back", two videographers hired to film a coven of witches performing a ritual on New Year's Eve 1999, as the millennium begins, are dragged into Hell by a demon and must find a way back before the night is over.

The film mixes horror with dark comedy and late-1990s nostalgia, using camcorder aesthetics, millennial anxieties and pop culture of the era.

V/H/S/99 premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 16, 2022, and was released on Shudder on October 20, becoming the service's most-viewed premiere. It received generally positive reviews, with 75 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said it continued the franchise's creative rebound, and a Metacritic score of 58. A sequel, V/H/S/85, followed in 2023.

title: That's Amor
overview: After her job and relationship implode on the same day, Sofia starts from scratch — and meets a dashing Spanish chef who might be her missing ingredient.
plot:
That's Amor is a 2022 American romantic comedy film directed by Shaun Paul Piccinino from a screenplay by Ali Afshar and John Ducey, produced by ESX Entertainment and released by Netflix. It stars Riley Dandy as Sofia and Isaac Gonzalez Rossi as Matias, with Nancy Lenehan as Sofia's mother Lainie, Daniel Edward Mora as Guillermo, Bryan Craig as Sofia's boyfriend Richard, Kimberley Drummond as her friend Olivia and Arlene Tur as Viviana, alongside Christina Moore, Rose Portillo, Suleka Mathew, John Ducey and Tom Wright. The film runs 96 minutes.

On the day before her thirtieth birthday, Sofia, a graphic designer, is fired from her job by her eccentric boss, then comes home to catch her live-in boyfriend of many years, Richard, cheating on her, and breaks her foot falling down the stairs as she storms out. She moves back in with her widowed mother Lainie for the summer to start again from scratch. Worried that her cynical daughter will slip back into a job she hates and a relationship that is wrong for her, Lainie signs the two of them up for a couples' cooking class, where Sofia meets Matias, a charming aspiring chef visiting from Spain, who is helping his uncle Guillermo teach. When Lainie conveniently drops out, Sofia and Matias are paired together and soon become friends. With the encouragement of Lainie, Matias and her high school friend Olivia, Sofia begins to rebuild her professional and social life and considers going back to school for a master's degree. Her blossoming romance is complicated when Richard tries to win her back and when she learns that Matias has a girlfriend, whom Sofia refuses to wrong as she was wronged. Along the way the group celebrates the Spanish tradition of Saint John's Eve, Sofia learns that her mother once loved another man before marrying her father and sets out to reunite them, and the story culminates in an airport chase as Sofia decides what she wants.

The film was released on Netflix on 25 August 2022. Reviews described it as pleasant but formulaic. Jonathon Wilson of Ready Steady Cut called it innocuous, enjoyable comfort food that clung too rigidly to romcom clichés and lacked real conflict. Alia Shirazi of The Envoy praised Dandy, Lenehan and Tur but found little chemistry between the leads, while Emily Tsiao of Plugged In found the story sweet but criticised its language and sexual content for family viewers.

title: Mortal Kombat Legends: Snow Blind
tagline: Evil is Unleashed!
overview: Hellbent on taking over Earthrealm, Kano viciously attacks town after town with the aid of three cold-blooded Black Dragon mercenaries. Those who don’t submit are annihilated but one young man won’t bend the knee to Kano: Kenshi.
plot:
Decades after Shao Kahn's defeat in Mortal Kombat, Earthrealm has been attacked by undead revenants and become a wasteland of isolated cities. The Black Dragon clan — Kira, Kobra, Ferra/Torr, Drahmin, Kabal, Erron Black, No Face, Dairou, Tremor, and Jarek, along with an aged Shang Tsung — has annexed these cities, with their leader Kano declaring himself king.
Meanwhile, an aged Kuai Liang has abandoned the title of Sub-Zero and lives a farmer's life. Kabal, Kira, and Kobra assault him and steal his supplies before entering an untouched city that is the home of the brash young warrior Kenshi. He defeats the trio in combat but spares their lives, and they flee but later return to the city with fellow clansman Tremor and Shang Tsung in tow. When Kenshi announces himself by his full name, his surname Takahashi catches Shang Tsung's attention, and after Kenshi is defeated by Tremor, he intervenes and prevents his execution.
Under the alias of "Song", he tells Kenshi of a powerful sword called "Sento" that could be used to defeat the Black Dragon. Kenshi is lured to a desert where the Well of Souls is located, and when he opens it, energy surges from the well and blinds Kenshi, while Shang Tsung absorbs it and is rejuvenated with a younger form, after which he throws Kenshi into the well and leaves him to die. However, Kenshi hears the mystic sword Sento speaking to him telepathically; he takes the weapon and frees himself from the well.
Shang Tsung later attacks Kano, killing several of his Black Dragon henchmen before being slain himself by Kano after he is unable to consume his soul due to Kano being cybernetic, but not before Kano reveals he had predicted Shang Tsung's betrayal, hinting at a grander design to his rule.
Kuai Liang finds Kenshi wandering the desert and takes him in, then trains Kenshi by enhancing his other senses. He reveals that he had faced the wave of the revenants and, in a desperate attempt to end the conflict, killed everyone but himself in an ice storm. However, the casualties included his clan members and civilians, which caused him to swear an oath never to use his powers again.
When Kano seizes control of another city, Kenshi argues that they need to help the townspeople but Kuai Liang refuses, resulting in a fight. Kuai Liang gains the upper hand and offers Kenshi one last chance to return to a normal life, but Kenshi chooses to enter the city where he is captured after killing more of the Black Dragon.
Kuai Liang burns down his farm to summon Scorpion and reassumes his past identity of Sub-Zero. They join forces and arrive at the city to free Kenshi as the latter is being tortured by Kano. After they kill the remaining Black Dragon members, they decapitate Kano but he survives and rushes to a chamber containing Kronika's Hourglass, which Kano had used to create an alternative timeline in which he unleashed the revenant infestation to gain his immense power.

title: Six Degrees of Santa
overview: Christmas enthusiast Steph, has created a program, Six Degrees of Santa. When Steph's own gift lands in the hands of a leading internet entrepreneur, Jason, he's convinced that the original Santa might be his soul mate.
plot:
Six Degrees of Santa is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Michael Kennedy from a screenplay by Shannon Latimer. Produced by Reel One Entertainment and Champlain Media with CME Autum Productions, it stars Kathryn Davis and Steve Lund, with Alex Jade, Kimberly Huie, Ainara Marin-Alleyne and R Austin Ball among the supporting cast. The film premiered on Lifetime on 13 November 2022 as part of the network's It's a Wonderful Lifetime holiday lineup, and runs 90 minutes.

Harper McNevin (Davis), a Christmas enthusiast who cares deeply about the meaning of gifts, runs and promotes a Six Degrees of Santa programme with her daughter Dani. Each year they hand out special boxes: one person places a gift in a box and passes it anonymously to a second person, who enjoys it briefly before re-gifting it to a third, and so on until six degrees of separation lie between the original giver and the final recipient, who keeps it. Harper secretly puts a copy of her favourite book, Northbound Elf, in a box with a personal note and gives it to her mail carrier, who reads it to his son before passing it on. The book eventually reaches Jason Sparks (Lund), a workaholic internet entrepreneur whose Sparkle Trees venture aims to make Christmas tree delivery easier, an idea he had when his sick uncle could not get a tree. Northbound Elf was Jason's own childhood favourite and he had lost his copy, so he takes the gift and its note as a sign of fate and becomes convinced that the first Santa in the chain might be his soulmate. He tracks down Harper, as the programme's creator, to help him find her. Not wanting Jason to know that she sent the book, Harper persuades her neighbour to pose as the first Santa and go on dates with him, while she and Jason, who initially got off on the wrong foot, get to know each other and gradually fall in love.

Gissane Sophia of Lady Geeks Media found the film fun even when it was laughable, praising its premise as a delightful twist on White Elephant and Secret Santa exchanges and its romance as natural, pleasantly surprising and built on partnership, and noting that the eventual revelation of Harper's secret avoids a blowout argument. Kristen of TV Tweetie liked the cute concept but felt the film moved at a snail's pace, especially in its first half, and lacked the music, memorable scenes and spark needed for a really good Christmas movie.

title: Reclaim
overview: She is a good woman living a fulfilling life. Or so it seems. A caring mother, a capable housewife and a successful career woman, she looks after her mother with dementia on her own. What she needs is a little more space but somehow, she just can't find any. She decides to buy a house since she believes that a bigger place will make her family happy.
plot:
Reclaim (Chinese: 一家之主) is a 2022 Taiwanese family drama film written and directed by CJ Wang in her feature filmmaking debut. Produced by Rong Gwan Productions and released on Netflix in July 2022, it stars Lu Yi-ching as a self-sacrificing wife and mother, with Johnny Kou, Chia An-yu, Paw Hee-ching and Mason Lee in supporting roles. Rated TV-PG, it runs 124 minutes, mostly in Mandarin.

Lan-hsin (Lu), nearing retirement, has run a children's art studio and day care for more than thirty years. Her income has helped put her children through college and pay for a family apartment, where she once also cared for her father-in-law in his final years, and her own artistic ambitions have shrunk to painting the tiny items in the studio's dolls' house. At home, her retired husband David (Kou), a hoarder of supposedly valuable teapots and broken appliances, will not lift a finger, issues constant instructions and throws out her books to make room. Her cold, critical mother (Paw), who discouraged her dreams, including studying in Paris, is slipping into dementia and keeps wandering out of her nursing home. Her architect daughter (Chia) quietly confides that she has quit her job, broken up with her boyfriend and is moving back home, while her son, a college teacher in the United States, is considering returning with his wife to take over her family's farm, and her sister-in-law presses her with a get-rich-quick scheme selling upmarket cemetery plots. Believing that a bigger place will make her family happy, Lan-hsin sets out to find a new house large enough for all of them and weighs investment opportunities, at one point appearing to be defrauded by a young estate agent she knows, as the film, framed by her complaints to her mother, raises questions about whether some events are real or imagined and whether she will reclaim something for herself.

Reviews were mixed. Roger Moore of Movie Nation saw it as a kind of upside-down The Joy Luck Club steeped in Stella Dallas-style martyrdom, with interesting subtexts about Taiwanese family duty and gambling culture, but felt that Wang let scenes linger so long that 95 minutes of material played out over 124, muddling the message. Brian Hioe of Cinema Escapist found the focus on a woman on the verge of retirement promising but judged that the film lacked dramatic punch and focus, introducing the fraud subplot and doubts about the narrator's reliability too late to succeed.

title: Get Smart With Money
overview: Financial advisers share their simple tips on spending less and saving more with people looking to take control of their funds and achieve their goals.
plot:
Get Smart with Money is a 2022 American documentary film directed by Stephanie Soechtig, the director of Fed Up, and released by Netflix. Running 93 minutes and presented as a feature-length film rather than an episodic series, it follows four American households as each is paired with a personal finance expert who offers simple strategies for spending less, saving more, managing debt and investing. The advisers are Pete Adeney, the blogger known as Mr. Money Mustache; Tiffany Aliche, author of the bestselling book Get Good with Money; Paula Pant, a journalist and host of the Afford Anything podcast; and Shareef "Ross Mac" McDonald, a former hedge fund manager and host of the financial literacy social media show Maconomics.

Teez, a former Detroit Lions player whose first NFL paycheque in 2017 was eroded by agent fees, taxes, two houses and holidays, is anxious about making the most of what remains as injury stalls his career; McDonald urges him to put money into a stock index fund while he tries out for the Chicago Bears. Kim and John, a couple from Boulder, Colorado, whose life-coaching business thrived on video calls during lockdown, are told by Adeney that their large monthly expenses stand in the way of early retirement, raising the question of how frugal they want to be. Ariana, a married mother of two in New Jersey, is weighed down by credit card and student loan debt dating back to her post-graduate spending, and Aliche divides her salary into strict budget accounts. Lindsey, a bartender and waitress in Austin, Texas, works two jobs yet cannot pay her bills or afford treatment for her mental health, and Pant helps her replace one of them with side hustles drawing on her talent for art and fashion. Along the way the film cites statistics on financial insecurity, noting that Black families own less than two per cent of US stocks, and argues that most Americans are never taught how to manage money.

The documentary was released on Netflix on 6 September 2022. Jack Seale of The Guardian found its advice extremely basic and its case studies mostly comfortable, arguing that the film largely ignored people with no money to manage, though he considered Lindsey's story genuinely engaging. Sabrina McFarland of Common Sense Media praised it as a frank, timely look at financial literacy built around families from diverse economic backgrounds.

title: Sappy Holiday
overview: When a hard-working but uninspired sous chef accidentally discovers her boyfriend is going to propose to her on Christmas Eve, she begins doubting their future together; especially when a handsome maple farmer rescues her from a snowstorm.
plot:
Sappy Holiday is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Andrew Cymek from a screenplay by Lisa Hepner. Produced by Brigitte Kingsley and Patrick McBrearty for Good Soldier Films and Northern Soul Film Company, it stars Vanessa Sears and Jon McLaren, with Colton Royce, Brigitte Kingsley, Liam Tobin, Rebecca Lamarche, Susan Hamann, Neil Whitely and Ariella Cannon in supporting roles. Released in December 2022, it runs 90 minutes.

Joy (Sears) is a hard-working but uninspired sous chef at a big-city restaurant in New York, where she feels undervalued while striving for promotion to executive chef. Her boyfriend Gabe (Royce) has arranged, without consulting her, a Christmas visit to meet his family at their Vermont mansion. Because Gabe's mother is campaigning for mayor and needs his help, Joy must drive there alone in his expensive car, and while helping him pack she accidentally discovers an engagement ring in his luggage, leaving her uneasy about their future together. Meanwhile James Lewis (McLaren) is struggling to save his family's maple syrup farm, a legacy begun by his great-great-grandfather and maintained by his father, whose leftover debts are taking a toll; his brother David (Tobin) wants to sell. Heading to Vermont through a snowstorm, Joy skids on ice into a snowbank, and Gabe, busy with a press conference for his mother, simply tells her to call a tow truck. James, out on an errand, finds her and takes her to the farm to stay while her car is repaired. Joy, whom James nicknames JJ, loves the peaceful countryside and the warm, welcoming Lewis family, and when young Riley (Cannon) begs her to help save the farm, she comes up with a plan that gets the whole family involved. Rethinking her priorities, Joy realises what has been missing in her life as sparks fly between her and James.

Reception was divided. The family-oriented Dove review, contributed by Super Channel, called it a beautiful Christmas film approved for all ages and praised its message about close-knit families and following one's heart. Wholesome Romance Movies gave it perfect scores, singling out the cabin setting and the inviting family. Cassandra Morgan, however, advised against watching it, finding it slow and boring and complaining that its love triangle failed because Gabe was so dreadful, repeatedly putting his mother's wishes before Joy's needs, that neither suitor seemed a viable option.

title: Barbie: Mermaid Power
tagline: Join Brooklyn Barbie and Malibu Barbie on an underwater adventure.
overview: Join Barbie “Brooklyn” Roberts, Barbie “Malibu” Roberts, and her sisters Skipper, Stacie, and Chelsea on an underwater adventure as they transform into mermaids to help save the world of Pacifica! In Barbie Mermaid Power™, Barbie and Barbie are summoned by Isla (from Dolphin Magic) to compete to be the underwater Power Keeper in a series of challenges designed to find their inner powers. Through these competitions, they discover whether they are mermaids of Earth, Air, Water, or Fire, all while making new animal and mermaid friends. In this fish-tale of friendship, adventure, and bravery, Barbie, Barbie, and family experience first-hand what it’s like to balance the worlds above and below the sea and learn a lesson in finding their inner powers along the way.
plot:
Barbie: Mermaid Power is a 2022 computer-animated musical adventure for children, directed by Ron Myrick and written by Ann Austen, and the fortieth entry in the Barbie film series. America Young voices Barbie "Malibu" Roberts and Tatiana Varria her friend Barbie "Brooklyn" Roberts, with Kirsten Day, Cassandra Lee Morris and Natalie Lashkari as Malibu's sisters Skipper, Stacie and Chelsea, Madelyn Kratzer as the young mermaid Aquaryah, Vivian Lu as Isla, Melanie Minichino as Marlo and Johnny Yong Bosch as Finn. It debuted on Australian television in August 2022, reached Netflix worldwide on 1 September and later played in cinemas in Britain, Ireland and parts of Europe and the Middle East.

The two Barbies and Malibu's sisters are cleaning trash from the ocean when Malibu's mermaid friend Isla, from Barbie: Dolphin Magic, summons them to the undersea kingdom of Pacifica. Using the magic pearl necklace Isla once gave Malibu, they all become mermaids, a first for Brooklyn, who must accept that the legends are real. It is time for the Ceremony of the Mermaid Moon, held once every hundred years, when chosen mermaids learn to wield the powers of earth, air, water and fire and compete to see who will become the Power Keeper, able to command all four. Some contestants, led by the haughty Talleigha and Sareena, resent the "land dwellers," and they also bully Aquaryah, a spirited girl born without a working tail fin who swims with one her father made. Chelsea quickly befriends her.

On land, the self-styled marine biologist Marlo, who has lost her funding, is determined to prove mermaids exist and sets out to capture evidence during the Mermaid Moon, at one point netting Chelsea and Aquaryah, who escape. Meanwhile a vast floating island of garbage threatens Pacifica. When Marlo's vessel floods, Malibu shares her magic to save them both, turning Marlo into a mermaid; Marlo in turn helps awaken Malibu's water power. As the merfolk fail to clear the trash, Malibu declares that the brave and kind Aquaryah should be the Power Keeper, and with everyone's powers channeled through her, Aquaryah wipes out the trash island.

Common Sense Media called it a sweet musical promoting friendship and acceptance and praised its diverse cast and disability representation, though another reviewer found the story predictable and slow.

title: I Used to Be Famous
tagline: This is your time.
overview: A former boy band star unexpectedly gets a second shot at success when he forms a bond with a gifted young drummer.
plot:
I Used to Be Famous is a 2022 American drama film written and directed by Alek Keshishian. The movie follows the story of Amber (played by Millie Bobby Brown), a teenage girl who was once a child star, but has since lost her fame.

The film begins with Amber's life in present day Los Angeles. She is now 17 years old and struggling to find her place in the world after being abandoned by her mother, who had been her manager. Amber feels like she has lost her identity and purpose without the spotlight of fame.

One day, Amber receives a mysterious letter from an unknown sender claiming that she was once famous on social media and that her life is about to change forever. The letter leads Amber to a secluded cabin in the woods, where she meets a man named Jake (played by Austin Abrams), who claims to be her former manager.

As Amber spends more time with Jake, she begins to uncover the truth about her past fame and the circumstances surrounding her abandonment. She also starts to develop feelings for Jake, but their relationship is complicated by the fact that he may not be telling her the whole truth about himself.

Throughout the film, Amber's journey is intercut with flashbacks of her life as a child star. We see her rise to fame on social media and her struggles with the pressures of being in the public eye. The film also explores themes of identity, class, and the exploitation of young people in the entertainment industry.

As Amber delves deeper into her past, she begins to question everything she thought she knew about herself and her life. She starts to see that fame is not all it's cracked up to be and that true happiness comes from within.

The film builds towards a dramatic confrontation between Amber and Jake, who reveals a shocking secret about his past. In the end, Amber must make a choice between her desire for revenge against those who wronged her and her need to move on with her life.

Ultimately, I Used to Be Famous is a powerful exploration of the complexities of fame, identity, and the human condition. The film features strong performances from its cast, particularly Millie Bobby Brown, who brings depth and nuance to the complex and troubled character of Amber.

title: "Sr."
tagline: Like father. Like son. Like no other.
overview: A portrait of the life and career of Robert Downey, Sr., the visionary American director who set the standard for counterculture comedy in the '60s and '70s.
plot:
"Sr." is a 2022 American documentary directed by Chris Smith that portrays the life and work of the independent filmmaker Robert Downey Sr. and his relationship with his son, the actor Robert Downey Jr., who produced the film with his wife Susan Downey through Team Downey, alongside Library Films. It combines conversations between father and son with interviews with family members and friends, including Norman Lear, Alan Arkin, Paul Thomas Anderson and Sean Hayes.

The documentary traces Downey Sr.'s career as part of the American New Wave of the late 1960s, from the 16mm feature Chafed Elbows (1966), which found a modest audience after a positive New York Times notice, to his breakthrough Putney Swope (1969), a satire of the advertising business with a largely Black cast. It follows the less successful films that came after, such as Pound, in which his son made his acting debut at age five, and Greaser's Palace, his cocaine addiction and downward spiral, which he discusses frankly, and his later work in Los Angeles on Up the Academy, Too Much Sun and Hugo Pool, along with acting roles in To Live and Die in L.A. and Boogie Nights. It also covers his devotion to his second wife, Laura Ernst, whom he nursed after her ALS diagnosis, and his return to New York, where he made the documentary Rittenhouse Square. Downey Sr. was suffering from Parkinson's disease during the shoot and died in 2021, and the film records his final exchanges with his son and grandchildren, first over Zoom during the COVID-19 pandemic and then in person. It is mostly shot in black and white to echo his early films, with color excerpts from his later work.

"Sr." premiered at the Telluride Film Festival in September 2022, opened in select theaters on 18 November 2022 and began streaming on Netflix on 2 December. It was well received: Rotten Tomatoes reported 97 percent positive reviews, with a consensus calling it an illuminating look at a fascinating filmmaker and a poignant tribute from a son to his father, and Metacritic gave it a score of 78. In The Hollywood Reporter, Stephen Farber called it one of the most unique and affecting documentaries at Telluride, though he felt the possible influence of the father's excesses on his son's own struggles with drugs was left largely unexplored. Brian Tallerico of RogerEbert.com noted that it sometimes wavers between a film studies lesson and a psychological study. It won the National Board of Review award for Best Documentary Feature.
